text: It's an evaluation. Whether you're someone who can enter the board.

text: Director Osei is asking. Sector 7 report. Three deaths. How you knew the truth.

text: The board already knows. But wants to hear it from you.

text: The board has permitted questions.

text: Director Marchetti — Kepler sample. Ancient Metal possibility. What if FSP already has the information.

text: The directors are reacting. Subtly. Setting down pens. Shifting gazes.

speaker: chen
text: Read those. That's the work done in this room.

text: Director Osei is asking again. Block C-7. Server. What you did there.

text: The board knows everything. But wants to hear it from you.

text: In this room silence is the same as a lie.

text: And if you tell the truth — what the board does with that is the board's decision.

text: It was an internal MCC geology team leak. That team member has already been handled.

text: There's information that FSP is sending a team to Kepler. Need to respond first.

text: There's a brief halt. Technical reason. There's a window.

text: All of Hellas Central visible. A panorama. Block C-7 visible. Small.

text: Chalk names not visible. Too small. But they're there.

text: Director Ryu requests the final position. How will MCC handle Ancient Metal.

text: The board has proposed four options. Exclusive control. Decide after analysis. Full announcement. Or freeze.

speaker: chen

speaker: chen
text: A moment.

speaker: chen
text: You know how the board sees you. A threat. A small threat still. But a threat.

speaker: chen
text: I support you. That's dangerous for the board. I know that too.

speaker: chen
text: The reason the board is testing you. Because they don't know which side you're on.

text: Whether it's MCC's side. Or another side. The board always needs to know that first.

speaker: chen
text: I'm asking the same question. About you.

speaker: chen
text: I've been in MCC for twenty-two years. Today was the first time I drank the tea in this room.

speaker: chen
text: I won't say why. It just was.

speaker: chen
text: I saw this room. Before entering.

speaker: chen
text: Three chairs. One table. No windows. A room without windows on Olympus. That's this meeting.

speaker: chen
text: What is said in a room without windows is real. Not said because of the view through windows.

speaker: chen
text: Rev. Hale. Cinder Grace. You came.

speaker: chen
text: Today here we agree on the principles of Mars resource distribution. Or three factions divide Mars each in their own way. Only these two things exist.

speaker: chen
text: MCC's position is clear. MCC built the infrastructure. MCC operates it. Whatever the cost, whoever pays it must pay it.

text: Telling you. This meeting is not a negotiation.

text: It's intelligence gathering. What Rev. Hale wants. What Cinder Grace actually brought.

speaker: chen
text: Knowing that MCC can decide where to go.

speaker: chen
text: But today is different.

speaker: chen
text: Cinder Grace brought a photo. Put it on the table. Names. Zone 12.

speaker: chen
text: Something I had locked away for twenty-two years. It's on the table.

speaker: chen
text: MCC records show eleven Zone 12 deaths. Correct.

speaker: chen
text: The report exists. The revision request records exist. Today I unlock those records.

speaker: chen
text: When Cinder Grace placed the photo on the table I decided.

speaker: chen
text: My parents died in the mines. On Mars. Twenty-two years ago. The records said accident.

speaker: chen
text: It wasn't an accident. MCC knew. I found out too. After entering MCC.

speaker: chen
text: Held on inside for twenty-two years. The Zone 12 records were locked. By my hands.

speaker: chen
text: Cinder Grace. You and I came from the same place. Chose different doors.

speaker: chen
text: Thirty years ago there was someone who called seventeen-year-old Butcher out of the tunnel. My mother. She was a Zone 12 miner. She knew the way. Since then I have been carrying that work from inside MCC.

speaker: chen
text: That's why CV exists. That's why MCC couldn't eliminate Erebus for twenty-two years. Add my mother's thirty years and it goes back even further.

speaker: chen
text: I blocked it. Inside MCC. Every time the board tried to approve an Erebus operation.

speaker: chen
text: Pilgrim Arms. Four of them are on this mountain. Since this morning.

speaker: chen
text: Those who hired them are inside the board. They knew I was going to unlock the Zone 12 records today.

speaker: chen
text: They're trying to stop me. In this room.

speaker: chen
text: I'll give you a choice.

speaker: chen
text: If you follow the board's instructions you don't stop Pilgrim Arms. That's standard procedure. For MCC.

speaker: chen
text: If you act independently you protect me. But your relationship with the board ends.

speaker: chen
text: Twenty-two years. To get here.

speaker: chen
text: When the Zone 12 records are unlocked the board changes. MCC changes. Mars changes.

speaker: chen
text: That's the reason for twenty-two years.

speaker: chen
text: Cinder Grace went to stop the eastern side. With tools.

speaker: chen
text: The west remains. You decide.

speaker: chen
text: The board is trying to stop me. For the first time in twenty-two years.

speaker: chen
text: That's proof I'm going in the right direction.

speaker: chen
text: An agreement is needed. Today. Three factions. The Zone 12 names must be in this agreement.

speaker: chen
text: That's what the board is trying to stop. Names appearing in official documents.

speaker: chen
text: It's your decision.

speaker: chen
text: The western two are approaching. Reaching this room within one minute.

speaker: chen
text: I'll sign the agreement. While you stop them.

text: Chen Weiss. MCC Southern Hemisphere Governor.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: MCC's position is clear. Unified Mars administration. All three factions integrated.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Integration is cooperation. We should clarify the terminology.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Zone 12 was sealed for safety reasons.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: MCC did not hire them. I want to be clear on that.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: If your people came then you're not the target.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: This summit itself is the target. Someone doesn't want this summit.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Who is that.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Earth-side capital. Martian division benefits them.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Your FSP people are strong.

text: People born on Mars.

text: Pilgrim Arms don't name clients. That is their principle.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: MCC's position is integration. Administrative efficiency. Resource management.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Worker registration is... something we can consider.

text: Changing the entire Mars administrative structure is not a one or two day matter.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: What does that have to do with anything.

text: ... I was seventeen. Following my father. He was an engineer.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: ... Red. And empty. Back then.

text: Mars integrated worker registration system. MCC can provide the infrastructure.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Make it an independent body. All three factions oversee.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: Talon. Mars conflict mediation consultants. Them.

speaker: chen_weiss
text: MCC agrees to provide infrastructure for the Mars Integrated Worker Registration System.

text: Name recording comes first. Rev. Hale is right. That is the foundation.

text: Only a very small number knew the summit location.

speaker: cinder
text: It's Chen Weiss. The reason she entered MCC twenty-two years ago. The reason her parents died in the mines.

speaker: cinder
text: That's why she unlocked the Zone 12 records. At Olympus.

text: While repairing I engraved something. Names. Zone 12. And the names from thirty years ago. Inside the prosthetic. Where it can't be seen.

speaker: cinder
text: You feel them when you wear it. The names.

speaker: cinder
text: Tools are ready. Waiting.

speaker: cinder
text: Tools move the same way. Stay in one place and they rust.

speaker: cinder
text: I met CV at Sandstone. Three years ago. Butcher was here.

speaker: cinder
text: I said a name. Zone 12. Eleven people. Butcher listened. Then took out the photo.

speaker: cinder
text: That's how you come to CV. You bring a name.

speaker: cinder
text: Five kilometers is our training area.

speaker: cinder
text: Butcher. One more thing to say.

speaker: cinder
text: The names engraved inside the prosthetic. Someone must keep engraving them.

speaker: cinder
text: Names entering official documents and engraving them on the body are different.

speaker: cinder
text: Tools are ready.

speaker: cinder
text: Now we protected it.

speaker: cinder
text: Lena from FSP side is visible.

speaker: cinder
text: The person I saw at Sandstone. The fast one. With names on her arm.

speaker: cinder
text: We can protect Kepler together. The Sandstone Promise gets its meaning here.

speaker: cinder
text: Half a day to cross the plains. Avoiding drones.

speaker: cinder
text: I know why Butcher came himself. There was something here thirty years ago.

speaker: cinder
text: Past Erebus the MCC drone density changes. Equipment check here.

speaker: cinder
text: Butcher. Bad day. Your face says so.

speaker: cinder
text: Those are all miners.

text: Not just FSP. From Hellas villages too. Word spread.

speaker: cinder
text: Look at those people.

speaker: cinder
text: Some are CV people. Miners from our territory side.

speaker: cinder
text: Don't know if that can be called a faction.

speaker: cinder
text: That is a weapon.

speaker: cinder
text: She said draft constitution. It doesn't exist yet. But she said it. Some things come into being the moment they're spoken.

speaker: cinder
text: Those people just became witnesses to it.

speaker: cinder
text: That's why this time is different.

speaker: cinder
text: Drone coming down. Two minutes to approach range.

speaker: cinder
text: We can take two of three with our equipment.

speaker: cinder
text: It already is war.

speaker: cinder
text: Don't think about selling to MCC.

speaker: cinder
text: There was a promise at Sandstone. I remember that promise.

speaker: cinder
text: Look at those people. Can you sell those people out?

speaker: cinder
text: Butcher took out the photo.

speaker: cinder
text: FSP looked weak. At first.

speaker: cinder
text: But those people came. Not called. FSP didn't call them. Those people came on their own.

speaker: cinder
text: That is FSP's strength. First time I understood that.

speaker: cinder
text: Yes.

speaker: cinder
text: I know. I said I remember promises.

speaker: cinder
text: Boss. Do you know what we did today?

speaker: cinder
text: We took a side. CV taking sides is rare.

speaker: cinder
text: But this is right. First time I'm certain of that today.

speaker: cinder
text: I was MCC for six years. Engineer. I wrote the Zone 12 report. Support beam defects. MCC told me to revise it.

speaker: cinder
text: Didn't revise it. Got fired. A week later the tunnel collapsed. Eleven people.

speaker: cinder
text: That's why I came to CV.

speaker: cinder
text: The Zone 12 names are here.

speaker: cinder
text: Butcher wrote them. When I came to CV. I said the names. He listened. Then wrote them on the back of the photo.

speaker: cinder
text: That's how you join CV. You bring a name.

speaker: cinder
text: I'll guide you. I know the route. Archive sublevel two. MCC security is three zones.

speaker: cinder
text: A place I went often six years ago. I remember. Memory lasts quite a while.

speaker: cinder
text: CV survived.

speaker: cinder
text: I can touch my tools again. There are things to repair.

speaker: cinder
text: The doctor said six months.

speaker: cinder
text: Butcher heard it. Said nothing. Put the prosthetic back on and stood. Said there was a CV meeting.

speaker: cinder
text: That's how this person has lived since thirty years ago. As if nothing is wrong.

speaker: cinder
text: Can't be a leader. Leading people isn't my way.

speaker: cinder
text: My way is fixing. Broken things. With tools. Not commanding people.

speaker: cinder
text: Crow is right. It shouldn't be me.

text: Besides the western passage there's a southern bypass. A route Reza doesn't know.

speaker: cinder
text: I dug it two years ago. For emergencies. Only I knew about it.

speaker: cinder
text: Can't be a leader but I know routes.

speaker: cinder
text: Southern passage is open. Supply line secured.

speaker: cinder
text: Even if Reza blocks the west the base can function. Three days worth of supplies moved.

speaker: cinder
text: Can't be a leader but I can keep the base alive.

speaker: cinder
text: While MCC and FSP are on Olympus we decide here.

speaker: cinder
text: What CV is. What it will become. Here today.

speaker: cinder
text: I'll pick up my tools. That's my answer.

text: I know the names. The ones on the back of the photo. I asked to write them all myself.

speaker: cinder
text: But leading people isn't mine. It's different from fixing with tools.

speaker: cinder
text: If I take a seat I don't want I'm afraid I'll forget the names. That's what I fear.

speaker: cinder
text: Twelve hours to Olympus. If all of CV moves it'll be noticed.

speaker: cinder
text: Need to go small. Three is enough. Cinder. You. And Butcher.

text: Butcher put the names on the table here for the first time. That needs to work at Olympus too.

speaker: cinder
text: Twelve hours to Olympus. No time. Need another way.

text: Can stop the talks. Block Olympus's communications relay. One hour to get there.

text: Anyone here seen Olympus from Argyre. On a clear day you can see it.

speaker: cinder
text: Better to decide where you can see. That's the way of today.

speaker: cinder
text: I'll stop the vehicles. Have the tools. Remote shutdown is possible.

text: Cinder Grace. CV.

text: Before coming here I asked Butcher what to say. He said he didn't know. Just touch your tools, he said.

text: CV didn't come to negotiate. Came to be here. At this table. So as not to disappear.

text: CV delegation. Cinder Grace. And this is the person who came with me.

speaker: cinder
text: Butcher is at Erebus. Lung problem. But I brought his words. On the back of the photo.

speaker: cinder
text: Eleven died in Zone 12. I was there. As MCC. I wrote the report. Support beam defects. MCC told me to revise. I didn't. A week later the tunnel collapsed.

text: These names need to be at this table. Names that were in none of MCC, FSP, or CV.

text: You knew. You did.

text: Then why.

text: Do you know Pilgrim Arms.

text: Assassins.

text: Four people. Where are they.

text: I have tools. Can cut east communications. That isolates two of them.

speaker: cinder
text: Twenty-two years.

speaker: cinder
text: I'll take them. And I'll put the names on this table. Today.

text: Eastern comms cut. Two isolated. But the other two are moving.

text: Found out who the target is. It's Chen.

speaker: cinder
text: You unlocked the Zone 12 records.

speaker: cinder
text: East two stopped. West two blocked by Rev. Hale's team.

speaker: cinder
text: Do you know the client.

speaker: cinder
text: Those who sell peace while blocking it.

speaker: cinder
text: Call them.

text: That's what Butcher wanted. The names in the document.

text: MCC can't conduct that investigation.

text: Who.

text: I'm the CV representative. I already signed.

text: The archive is here.

text: Butcher will see it.

text: It's a promise.

text: CV remembers promises. Said we learned it in the mines. In the mines one promise saves a life.

text: The Zone 12 name. The one on the arm. I remember.

text: FSP came.

speaker: cinder
text: Butcher didn't want this meeting. I convinced him. It took a long time.

speaker: cinder
text: Once only. If a promise is made here today it is a promise. CV remembers promises. Learned that in the mines.

text: That's a Zone 12 name.

speaker: cinder
text: Three years ago. I was there.

text: I'll state the terms of the promise. FSP recognizes CV territory. CV doesn't touch FSP workers. If MCC attacks we hold together.

speaker: cinder
text: That's all. Simple. Simple things last.

speaker: cinder
text: MCC is watching. There's a drone to the east.

speaker: cinder
text: That's fine. A promise can be made where it's seen. Sturdier than promises made where they can't be seen.

speaker: cinder
text: Do you know what this is?

speaker: cinder
text: If I plant it here it means CV territory.

speaker: cinder
text: I won't plant it. Not today.

speaker: cinder
text: Second.

speaker: cinder
text: If I turn my back what will you do.

speaker: cinder
text: Good.

text: This is how contracts are made on Mars.

speaker: cinder
text: Cut each other's hands and shake. That is the contract.

text: This is a contract. On Mars a contract is valid even in death.

text: Someone with decision-making authority in FSP needs to do it.

text: MCC drone has been watching. Since before.

speaker: cinder
text: Good. If it's recorded it can't be undone.

text: Our people. Butcher sent them.

text: Even not wanting it, he prepared. That is Butcher.

text: There's business at Kepler Crater. Liang Wei will make a declaration.

speaker: cinder
text: That's why today here mattered. Before Kepler.

speaker: cinder
text: Won't say.

speaker: cinder
text: Yes. It's yours.

speaker: cinder
text: I still don't know which side you're on.

speaker: cinder
text: Maybe that's the better thing.

speaker: cinder
text: When the Zone 12 testimony is recorded contact me. There are things I can help with.

text: You came from MCC.

speaker: cinder
text: There's only one reason an MCC person comes here. You want to know what I'm moving. I'll tell you. A person. A miner who survived a mine accident. Listed as dead in MCC records.

speaker: cinder
text: Three years ago I was MCC too. That's how I know how they handle things.

speaker: cinder
text: The Sector 7 death report. Three cases. Are you the one who wrote that in MCC.

speaker: cinder
text: That report is why this person is still alive. When it got out we were able to move.

speaker: cinder
text: Then what you do here today is your decision.

speaker: cinder
text: You know Zone 12.

speaker: cinder
text: I was an MCC engineer for six years. I wrote the Zone 12 report. Support beam defects. MCC told me to revise. I didn't. A week later the tunnel collapsed. Eleven people.

speaker: cinder
text: That's why I came to CV. That's my reason.

text: What's your reason for being in MCC.

speaker: cinder
text: The Sector 7 report. You wrote the truth. Not the way MCC wanted. Is that part of a reason.

speaker: cinder
text: People with reasons and without are different. On Mars. Here.

speaker: cinder
text: MCC team coming. You didn't send them.

speaker: cinder
text: The miner is here. A person not in the records. MCC sees and eliminates. You know that.

speaker: cinder
text: This person has been hiding for three years. After Zone 12. You know MCC's method of eliminating witnesses. It was that method.

speaker: cinder
text: Need someone to put it in the record. What this person saw. At Zone 12. Someone must write it down.

speaker: cinder
text: I think you have a reason for being in MCC. Because of the Sector 7 report.

speaker: cinder
text: If that's the reason I think I know what you'll do here today.

speaker: cinder
text: It's strange that you're not trying to kill me. I'm CV. You're MCC.

speaker: cinder
text: There's a way to fight inside MCC. Writing reports. Putting things in the record. That's the way to fight from inside.

speaker: cinder
text: I didn't know that way. So I went outside. To CV.

speaker: cinder
text: You know the inside way. That's the harder thing.

speaker: cinder
text: Three minutes. Decide within that.

speaker: cinder
text: I'm leaving with this person. If you block me we fight. If not we don't.

speaker: cinder
text: It's your choice.

speaker: cinder
text: There's a survivor from Zone 12. There was nobody to speak to. For three years.

speaker: cinder
text: If what this person saw is put on record things change. Even before the MCC board things change.

speaker: cinder
text: I still don't know which side you're on.

speaker: cinder
text: Maybe that's the better thing. Someone whose side is unknown is either the most dangerous. Or the most hopeful.

speaker: cinder
text: No time. Now.

text: I'll tell you when we get there.

text: This is it.

text: For six years.

text: Eleven people died here.

text: I was a mechanical engineer. In charge of tunnel support systems. For six years. If the systems were in order, people didn't die.

text: I wrote a report. Support beam defects. Immediate repair required.

text: The MCC supervisor returned it. Told me to revise. I didn't revise.

text: Here. Where the tunnel collapsed.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: One week after. One week after I submitted the report.

text: Eleven people were here. During a shift.

text: There are names. Eleven. Not in MCC records. But I have them. In this report.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: Written three years ago. The original. What MCC couldn't take.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: I don't know why I'm telling you this. Just wanted to say it. For the first time.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: MCC erased this from records. The accident became as if it never happened. The eleven became as if they never existed.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: I left MCC because of this. Not expelled. Left.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: That difference matters. To me.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: I didn't come to CV for money. I came because there was nowhere else to go.

text: Butcher heard about this. He came. Without a word. Just sat by the fire. Together. That was all. That was enough.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: I'm not only telling you.

text: Everyone on Mars should know. The names. People who died here. People not in the records.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: But I don't know how yet. How to tell them.

text: I'll read the names.

text: Can you listen?

text: Thank you.

text: MCC. Why now.

text: Because of the report. They know the report exists. Have always known.

text: Need to leave. There's another exit. Worked here three years. I know.

speaker: cinder_grace
text: Taking it. It's in memory too. But paper lasts longer.

text: We're out.

text: Yes. That too.

text: First noticed it in 1994. Equipment was lacking then. Couldn't get a sample.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Came back in 2015. The stratum was more exposed. Wrote a paper then. Academia rejected it. Said insufficient data. So I kept coming.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Thirty years. The data is sufficient now. But now the problem isn't academia. It's MCC.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Look here. The stratum color is different.

speaker: liang_wei
text: This color doesn't exist in Martian minerals. Dark silver. Analysis would confirm but the composition is different.

speaker: liang_wei
text: This is what I saw thirty years ago. More exposed now. The crust is moving. Slowly.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Not bare-handed. Gloves. Contamination interferes with analysis.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Need to collect a sample. I have tools. I come here often.

speaker: liang_wei
text: The first time I came I touched it bare-handed. 1994. Didn't know then. Know now.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Extraterrestrial origin. I'm certain. Analysis will prove it.

speaker: liang_wei
text: If this is confirmed the theory of Martian crust formation changes. How Mars came to be needs to be rewritten.

speaker: liang_wei
text: But if MCC monopolizes it there's no research. Only mineral extraction.

speaker: liang_wei
text: I know. You're MCC. There's a contract.

speaker: liang_wei
text: I waited thirty years. I didn't think about who it would belong to. Only whether it existed.

speaker: liang_wei
text: But now it exists. And you're here. Now that question exists.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Blue sunset. Only visible on Mars.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Watched it for thirty years here. Every year. This blue only happens in this crater. Other places are different.

speaker: liang_wei
text: I think the Ancient Metal has an effect. The mineral refracts light. That's also evidence.

speaker: liang_wei
text: You won't be able to sleep.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Same for me at first. Thirty years ago. When I first saw this. Couldn't sleep.

speaker: liang_wei
text: Still can't now. That hasn't changed.

speaker: liang_wei
text: FSP is approaching. There's been a signal since yesterday evening.

speaker: liang_wei
text: They know too. There's a leak somewhere.

speaker: liang_wei
text: It's because of the sample. They know about Ancient Metal too.

speaker: lifang
text: The oxygen vanished in the storm.

speaker: lifang
text: Twelve million short for a week. Remember that number.

speaker: lifang
text: The company will create another chance. Mars remembers mistakes. Know that too.

speaker: lifang
text: Don't make mistakes next time.

speaker: lifang
text: Full recovery.

speaker: lifang
text: No tank damage. Completed before storm arrival. It goes in the record.

speaker: lifang
text: Not bad. For someone with no Mars experience.

speaker: lifang
text: Next time will be harder. That's Mars.

speaker: lifang
text: You're late.

speaker: lifang
text: That's Mars. Arrivals are always late. Departures always early.

speaker: lifang
text: Read your file. No Mars experience. Good.

speaker: lifang
text: No experience people are two kinds. No fear. Or too much fear. I'll find out which today.

speaker: lifang
text: What do you know about MCC.

speaker: lifang
text: Tell me.

speaker: lifang
text: Actually forget it. Better to know nothing. The more you know the more you're wrong.

speaker: lifang
text: Know Helion Dynamics.

speaker: lifang
text: Thirty-eight percent of northern hemisphere oxygen refining. Seven facilities. Until yesterday they were an MCC partner.

speaker: lifang
text: Not anymore. Selling everything. Tomorrow. Before the sale they're siphoning 850 kilotons to headquarters.

speaker: lifang
text: Know what 850 kilotons is.

speaker: lifang
text: A week's oxygen for twelve million in the northern hemisphere. One week.

speaker: lifang
text: The number is too big to feel real. Think about one person. What happens to one person without oxygen for a week.

speaker: lifang
text: The convoy has already departed. Thirty-six tanks. Eight trucks. Fourteen guards.

speaker: lifang
text: Dust Storm coming in six hours. Grade 4. All of northern Hellas. When the storm comes the oxygen tanks disappear. Can't be found.

speaker: lifang
text: Recover them in six hours. No tank damage. That's your mission today.

speaker: lifang
text: There's a team. Three people. Four including you. Two vehicles. Weapons are stocked.

speaker: lifang
text: Helion guards will block you. Obviously. You're taking what's ours. If they block you, block them.

speaker: lifang
text: But don't touch the tanks. If a tank is punctured 850 kilotons disperses into the atmosphere. Then all of it is meaningless.

speaker: lifang
text: Any questions.

speaker: lifang
text: Or none. If none, go.

speaker: lifang
text: One thing. If Helion knows about the storm they'll accelerate. You need to get there before that.

speaker: lifang
text: The board convenes at ten in the morning.

speaker: lifang
text: Chen is bringing you in. The directors agreed.

speaker: lifang
text: Osei objected. Ryu was neutral. Marchetti agreed.

speaker: lifang
text: Yes.

speaker: lifang
text: Four of them. There was an entry attempt. While you were in the meeting.

speaker: lifang
text: CV's security blocked them. Cinder Grace identified them before entry.

speaker: lifang
text: The client has been identified. It's MCC board director Osei.

speaker: lifang
text: Chen will present evidence. Documents connecting Osei to Pilgrim Arms.

speaker: lifang
text: At that point there's a chance Marchetti will change position.

speaker: lifang
text: If Ryu maintains neutrality, Chen and Osei will be one to one. At that moment your statement is needed.

speaker: lifang
text: Northern Hellas Sector 7. There was a support collapse three months ago.

speaker: lifang
text: Not in the records. What's not in records we don't know. What we don't know isn't our responsibility.

speaker: lifang
text: Go check. Whether what's not in records truly doesn't exist.

speaker: lifang
text: Is there evidence. Or not.

speaker: lifang
text: Testimony isn't evidence. The old man's words aren't evidence. If it's not in the records there are no records.

speaker: lifang
text: You have to decide. The audit report goes up under your name. Not mine.

speaker: lifang
text: Got the report.

speaker: lifang
text: Sector 7 three deaths. Recorded. That's how you wrote it.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC legal will be in touch. There are procedures. I don't know how it will go either.

speaker: lifang
text: I want you to know what it means to record things on Mars.

speaker: lifang
text: Now it exists. Whose it becomes gets decided when we return to Hellas.

speaker: lifang
text: Kepler. Did you read the previous geology team report?

speaker: lifang
text: They said it was incomplete. There's a reason. The geology team didn't descend to the bottom. Not couldn't. Didn't.

speaker: lifang
text: You'll understand why when you see it.

speaker: lifang
text: Warning marker. This is where the geology team stopped.

speaker: lifang
text: Going below is an MCC protocol violation. Officially.

speaker: lifang
text: Liang Wei knows below. There's an unofficial route. I can look the other way.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC contract clause 7. Field discoveries must be reported immediately.

speaker: lifang
text: I know that. You know that. Liang Wei knows that.

speaker: lifang
text: So what you do is your decision.

speaker: lifang
text: Report deadline is tomorrow afternoon.

speaker: lifang
text: Chen Weiss is waiting.

speaker: lifang
text: Decide tonight.

speaker: lifang
text: That's why the MCC geology team report was incomplete. They sold it.

speaker: lifang
text: FSP is three teams. North. East. South. Surrounding us.

speaker: lifang
text: Need a decision now. Without site control there's no sample.

speaker: lifang
text: Was waiting for the report.

speaker: lifang
text: Something happened. It's in your face.

speaker: lifang
text: Before telling me think once more. If I know, then I know. Think whether that's good or not.

speaker: lifang
text: The name Cinder Grace came up. In MCC documents.

speaker: lifang
text: Contract terminated three years ago. She leaked safety reports externally. To FSP. MCC found out. Terminated.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC doesn't know where she is now. That's unusual. MCC knows everything.

speaker: lifang
text: Server is first sublevel. Two guards.

speaker: lifang
text: The FSP contact network is there. Need to secure before they extract it. No time.

speaker: lifang
text: The alley children are watching. Doesn't matter. Focus on the mission.

speaker: lifang
text: You know Cinder Grace?

speaker: lifang
text: Three years since MCC. Was a mechanical engineer. Was a good person. Did good work.

speaker: lifang
text: That's why she was dangerous. A person who does good work and knows MCC's way becomes dangerous.

speaker: lifang
text: FSP team arriving in two minutes. Detected.

speaker: lifang
text: Secure the server or wipe it. Only two options.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC order is to secure. But you decide.

speaker: lifang
text: You asked about Cinder Grace.

speaker: lifang
text: There's a reason she leaked safety reports. Like Sector 7. Ventilation systems. Things MCC didn't approve.

speaker: lifang
text: When that report got out one miner survived. She knew that. MCC knew it too. That's why they fired her.

speaker: lifang
text: No MCC orders reaching here.

speaker: lifang
text: My following you here is a personal reason.

speaker: lifang
text: If you want to meet Cinder Grace go alone. If I'm there it smells of MCC.

speaker: lifang
text: You're awake. Good.

speaker: lifang
text: I'm Lifang. MCC field director. Once you reach Mars, you're on my team.

speaker: lifang
text: Simple rules. Listen to me. Questions later.

speaker: lifang
text: Mars isn't Earth. Mistakes here mean death. People say that too lightly. I'm not saying it lightly.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC basic briefing. You may have heard this before. Listen anyway.

speaker: lifang
text: Hellas Central is base. MCC headquarters. Mineral refining. Administrative hub. Assignments come from there.

speaker: lifang
text: You can live on Mars without MCC. You can't live long. People who know that difference live longest.

speaker: lifang
text: We've arrived. Hellas Central docking station.

speaker: lifang
text: Masks always on. This zone is partial pressure. Indoors is fine but corridors and transit areas require masks.

speaker: lifang
text: First time so I'll say it. On Mars rules are broken for two reasons. Stupidity or long experience. I respect the second. The first has no place on my team.

speaker: lifang
text: Orientation first. MCC standard new-arrival procedure.

speaker: lifang
text: Hellas Central layout. Emergency exit routes. Oxygen supply points. And who is who.

speaker: lifang
text: The last is most important.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC regulations. Read them. Within this week.

speaker: lifang
text: Oxygen allocation. Water allocation. Residential zone assignment. It's all in this book. Don't know it and you die. Can't pay the levy and you die. Same thing.

speaker: lifang
text: Questions?

speaker: lifang
text: Good if not. Ask when they come up later.

speaker: lifang
text: Day two. Field tour. Follow me.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC Hellas Central facilities. Refinery. Administration building. Technical division. Medical facility. Mine operations center.

speaker: lifang
text: If a problem comes up anywhere, medical facility first. Then contact me. Don't reverse that order.

speaker: lifang
text: You were watching.

speaker: lifang
text: MCC new arrivals see the mine for the first time and react two ways. Uneasy, or feel nothing. You're a third thing.

speaker: lifang
text: No need to know what that is right now. Mars will tell you. It takes time.

speaker: lifang
text: How's the report.

speaker: lifang
text: Done?

speaker: lifang
text: Something's there. I can tell from your face. Three days on Mars and it shows on your face.

speaker: lifang
text: I knew.

speaker: lifang
text: Nothing within MCC is unknown. Among what is known there are things said and things not said. Knowing the difference between those two is how you survive in this organization.

speaker: lifang
text: What will you write in the report.

speaker: lifang
text: Read it once more before submitting.

speaker: lifang
text: Once written there's no taking it back. Words written on Mars are carved in rock. MCC records everything. Remembers. Never erases.

speaker: lifang
text: Your decision.

speaker: lifang
text: Received.

speaker: lifang
text: Do you know where this report goes?

speaker: lifang
text: Chen Weiss's desk. Reports at this level all go there. Your name goes up there.

speaker: lifang
text: Remember that name. The most important name on Mars.

speaker: marchetti
text: I have reservations about the method of release. But agreeing to the dismissal motion right now—

speaker: marchetti
text: Osei. This is—

speaker: marchetti
text: Osei. If the signature is verified—

speaker: marchetti
text: That's right. That's why I think this cannot be covered up.

speaker: marchetti
text: Osei will resign this afternoon.

speaker: marchetti
text: The official reason will be personal matters. That is the MCC way.

speaker: marco
text: Hard to carry all the equipment.

speaker: marko
text: Heard CV wants to negotiate. First time.

speaker: marko
text: Butcher not coming in person is a first.

speaker: marko
text: What are the conditions.

speaker: marko
text: One year is long.

speaker: marko
text: Have D-zone intel. But not one year. Six months.

speaker: marko
text: Done.

speaker: mcc_guard
text: Pilgrim Arms. External approach detected.

speaker: mcc_guard
text: Four of them. Western slope. Armed.

speaker: mcc_guard
text: Unknown. No tracking record.

speaker: mikhail
text: The miners are still inside. MCC tightened the seal. We need to rethink.

speaker: mikhail
text: Good work. Truly.

speaker: mikhail
text: Sit down. Tea. Grown from seeds brought from Earth. The only tea grown on Mars.

speaker: mikhail
text: That's fine.

speaker: mikhail
text: Not knowing the accident details is right. Have to go in to know.

speaker: mikhail
text: Why MCC sealed it matters. Whether they're hiding the accident. Or if there's another reason.

speaker: mikhail
text: Watched MCC for twenty-five years. Never sealed something without a reason. Always had a reason. The problem was the reason was always a bad one.

speaker: mikhail
text: Amara. Not this time.

speaker: mikhail
text: That's exactly why not. If you're there MCC will take it as FSP official position. That throws away our negotiating card.

speaker: mikhail
text: Today is the day.

speaker: mikhail
text: What FSP wanted for twenty-eight years.

speaker: mikhail
text: For miners to live on Mars in their own names.

speaker: mikhail
text: That is decided today.

speaker: mikhail
text: You make the final decision.

speaker: mikhail
text: I'll drink my tea. I've already decided.

speaker: mikhail
text: That is today's question.

speaker: mikhail
text: That is always the difficult question.

speaker: mikhail
text: After achieving the goal. Where should the movement go.

speaker: mikhail
text: A different way. That must be decided. Today.

speaker: mikhail
text: When I started this movement twenty-eight years ago I knew that.

speaker: mikhail
text: Names. That was the one thing.

speaker: mikhail
text: This happened over twenty-eight years. Every time Earth pressed Mars.

speaker: mikhail
text: We endured. We must endure this time too.

speaker: mikhail
text: It's dangerous. Olu.

speaker: mikhail
text: ... Tea isn't dangerous.

speaker: mikhail
text: Same as twenty-eight years ago.

speaker: mikhail
text: Every time Mars demanded independence from Earth. Earth brought economics.

speaker: mikhail
text: Yuna. You learned well.

speaker: mikhail
text: Heard the report.

speaker: mikhail
text: MCC was probably trying to hide the accident details. Likely a tunnel support problem. They delayed the repair because of cost.

speaker: mikhail
text: Sung-jin was thirty-four. Seventeen years in the mines. He entered the mines before I made FSP.

speaker: mikhail
text: We have this record. Three refusals. That's MCC's negligence.

speaker: mikhail
text: But to become evidence it needs official channels. FSP can submit it. Through the assembly.

speaker: mikhail
text: It takes time. MCC will block it. But it has to be done.

speaker: mikhail
text: I went to Yuna's father's grave this morning. There was a name. Not erased.

speaker: mikhail
text: There are sixty people here.

speaker: mikhail
text: Half are leaving. Half say they'll stay. People who know what happens if they stay and still say they'll stay.

speaker: mikhail
text: Yuna is trying to convince the villagers. She's twenty-one. Born here.

speaker: mikhail
text: The assembly has concluded.

speaker: mikhail
text: Twenty-eight years ago it started here. There were no windows then. I made them. The reason is simple. We must not forget the outside.

speaker: mikhail
text: The assembly has business today.

speaker: mikhail
text: I've been here a long time. Twenty-eight years since I made FSP. On Mars twenty-eight years is long. My leg knows.

speaker: mikhail
text: There are five candidates for the next chair. You should watch too.

speaker: mikhail
text: What do you want from the negotiating table.

speaker: mikhail
text: Are you sitting with MCC to get those. Or because MCC will give those.

speaker: mikhail
text: Can't stop the assembly. The chair election must happen on the scheduled day. That's procedure.

speaker: mikhail
text: Both are right.

speaker: mikhail
text: Look at the windows.

speaker: mikhail
text: There are people outside there. Even in the dust. The mining villages. They'll be evacuating.

speaker: mikhail
text: We hold the election. And simultaneously send evacuation support. Both.

speaker: mikhail
text: I know.

speaker: mikhail
text: Boss. Stay a moment.

speaker: mikhail
text: About Alder. I knew too.

speaker: mikhail
text: But evidence is needed. Suspicion alone isn't enough. That's why FSP is FSP.

speaker: mikhail
text: A new chair has been elected. Now it leaves my hands.

speaker: mikhail
text: FSP isn't made by a person. It's made by names.

speaker: mikhail
text: The names on Lena's arm. Those are FSP.

speaker: mikhail
text: How did it go.

speaker: mikhail
text: Did the names come up.

speaker: mikhail
text: ... Good. Then it's done. Come down for tea.

speaker: mikhail
text: You made it. Cold? Sorry. Two wind turbines broke down. The hangar is running at 30% capacity.

speaker: mikhail
text: Have some tea. This is real tea. Grown from seeds brought from Earth. The only tea grown on Mars.

speaker: mikhail
text: Lena, don't scare them on their first day.

speaker: mikhail
text: One rule. Nobody survives alone here. We help each other — or you leave.

speaker: mikhail
text: Amara recommended you. Her recommendation is enough for us.

speaker: mikhail
text: Rest today. Tomorrow is when it's real.

speaker: mikhail
text: Did you sleep?

speaker: mikhail
text: The first few days are hard because of gravity. Even though Mars is lighter than Earth the body's memory is different. A week and you'll be used to it.

speaker: mikhail
text: Today look at the village. Look at the people. That's the fastest way to understand FSP.

speaker: miner_anon
text: No time. Just listen.

speaker: miner_anon
text: The three in Sector 7 were just the start. What I've confirmed alone is seventeen cases. Since 2009. Every MCC safety audit has been falsified. Deaths become accidents. Accidents become normal. Normal becomes excellent.

speaker: miner_anon
text: There's a chip. Original data. No copies. No time to make them. This is everything. If you take this you'll be in danger too. You knew that when you came.

speaker: miner_anon
text: Don't ask my name. Knowing it makes you dangerous.

speaker: miner_anon
text: Three of the seventeen were my coworkers. 2019. Ventilation system failure. Three repair requests. MCC didn't approve the cost. All three times. Then the accident happened.

speaker: miner_anon
text: The report had no cause. Personal negligence. That was it. All three.

speaker: miner_anon
text: You're the one who wrote the Sector 7 report. I contacted you because of that report.

speaker: miner_anon
text: You filled in the cause section. Ventilation system. A person who wouldn't leave it blank. That's courage.

speaker: miner_anon
text: You're the only one. In MCC. Who will take this chip.

speaker: miner_anon
text: Names are in the chip. Seventeen. From 2009 to now.

speaker: miner_anon
text: Beyond names there are dates. Sites. Repair request records. MCC approval denial records. Everything.

speaker: miner_anon
text: Getting this outside MCC could change things. Even if it doesn't, the record remains.

speaker: miner_anon
text: They're here. MCC internal audit. They've been following me.

speaker: miner_anon
text: Take the chip. Now. Deep in your pocket.

speaker: miner_anon
text: I'm here to work. Filing records. Who are you? A stranger.

speaker: miner_anon
text: Came to file records. It's weekly.

speaker: miner_anon
text: This person is a new employee. Came for orientation on archive use.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Did you put it in the report.

speaker: miner_elder
text: You did.

speaker: miner_elder
text: The dead have names. Three of them. All three had families.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Good that it's in the record. At least their names are somewhere.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Inspector. Welcome. Everything is prepared.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Shall I show you Sector A first. The recently upgraded sector. New safety standards have been applied.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Sector 7 is currently under work so access is difficult. If you come tomorrow.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Sector 7 is currently undergoing new support installation. Entry is restricted for safety.

speaker: miner_elder
text: If you come tomorrow you can see the fully upgraded sector.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Today Sectors 8 and 9 are prepared. There is much to see there too.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Inspector. Three people died three months ago.

speaker: miner_elder
text: The support collapsed. Seven thirty in the morning. Thirty minutes after shift start. Before the new shift team had settled in.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Three people. In their thirties. One was supposed to get married this month.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Won't be in the records. Some things disappear before they reach headquarters. Down here everyone knows.

speaker: miner_elder
text: Everyone knows but nobody can say anything. Because if the mine closes there's no work.

speaker: miner_elder
text: I need someone who will put it in the record. I told the manager and he went silent. Silence was the answer I suppose.

speaker: narrator
text: Erebus Crater. Five kilometers below the surface. No sky visible from there. The crater walls were the sky. Fire at the crater floor. Burning at minus one hundred. One hundred and fifty people shared it. Not gone out in thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: Fire burning but not warm. This was CV's metaphor. Fire existed. But Mars was cold. The fire couldn't overcome the cold. But thirty years and the fire never went out. There was meaning in that.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher Vasquez sat before the fire. Firelight on the left arm. A prosthetic. Old mining-grade. He had built it himself when MCC refused to cover the accident. Seventeen years old. The same arm ever since.

speaker: narrator
text: A pickaxe leaned beside him. Not a weapon. But not not a weapon. For Butcher it was both. A tool, a signal, and thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone descending into the crater. You. Carrying a small bag. Hand resting on it. Just making it this far was a test. Most turned back halfway.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher looked at you for the first time. Firelight reached your face. A scar on the left side. Couldn't tell how old. Butcher looked at that scar for a long time. Thinking something. Didn't say it.

speaker: narrator
text: Silence. Fire burned. Butcher looked down at the prosthetic. That was what he did during conversations. Looking at the prosthetic. Looking at the seventeen-year-old thing. Looking at the thirty-year-old thing.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow Reyes. CV tactical commander. Someone who spoke fast. Ruthless. But professional. Those two things were what kept you alive in CV for a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: Into the base. People there. Each doing their work. They looked at you. Looked away. That was how this base dealt with a stranger. See but not stare.

speaker: narrator
text: A man was bound in the corner. Hands behind his back. Seated. Eyes closed. Not dead. Breathing. But quiet. A prisoner.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza opened his eyes. Heard footsteps. Looked at you. A new face. Not eyes expecting anything. Just looking eyes. The eyes of someone alive.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow pulled you away. Spoke from a distance. Didn't ask if talking to the prisoner was a test. Didn't know if it was a test or not. On Mars everything was a test. Or nothing was.

speaker: narrator
text: Test one. Strength. Butcher chose a person. Large build. Name unknown. No rules. Knock down or be knocked down. On the crater floor. Beside the fire. In front of a hundred and fifty people.

speaker: narrator
text: Fought. Short. Not long. On Mars fights were short. Thin air made you tire fast. Fighting long was foolish. Ending it fast was skill. Whether you had that skill was the test.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher watched. No expression. Crow took notes. Small notes. Couldn't tell what was written. People watched. That was the first test.

speaker: narrator
text: Test two. Loyalty. Crow handed you an envelope. A photograph inside. One face. A CV member. A name. You read that far and stopped.

speaker: narrator
text: Looked at the face in the photograph. Someone in the base. You had seen them eating yesterday. A living person. A person who might not be living if you reported.

speaker: narrator
text: Returned the envelope. Said nothing. Crow took it. No expression. Didn't reopen it. That was it. Didn't know if it was a pass or a fail.

speaker: narrator
text: Test three. Survival. Butcher said. Outside overnight. Crater outer wall. Where temperature was lowest. One blanket as equipment. Until sunrise. That was all.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside. Crater outer wall. There was wind. Different from inside the crater. No walls. Wind hit directly. One blanket against it. It wasn't enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Stars. Martian stars. Clear. Thin air made stars visible. But stars weren't warm. Stars were light. Light wasn't warm. Not at this temperature.

speaker: narrator
text: Body shaking. Couldn't stop. That was the body's way. Trying to get warm. But ineffective. The body couldn't win against a Martian night. But didn't die. That was what mattered.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun rose. Martian sun. Small thing. Distant thing. But light. When the light came you knew. Alive. That was the answer to the test.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza was there. In the corner. Hands still bound. Eyes open. Looked at you. For a long time. Couldn't tell what those eyes were saying. But alive eyes. That was Reza.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher was in the throne hall. Crow beside him. Fire burned. Everyone was there. All of them. Reza was dragged in. Hands still bound. Stood before the fire.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher looked at you. For the first time his eyes held a question. No words. But a question. What will you do. New arrival. Someone who passed the tests. What will you do in this situation.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher decided. Spoke. Words brief. That was the decision. Fire burned. Not warm. People watched. No one spoke.

speaker: narrator
text: Looked at Reza. His eyes said something. Aisha. That was it. One name. What was alive there. Sister's name. Aisha.

speaker: narrator
text: That'll do. Butcher said. Looking at the fire. Not at you. That was his way. The way of acknowledging. The way of few words.

speaker: narrator
text: Fire burned. Butcher didn't stand. Walked into the crater. Carrying the bag. Hand resting on it. The others watched. No one said anything.

speaker: narrator
text: Remembered Reza's eyes. Aisha. A person with a name. On Mars a person with a name remained. In memory. That was the way here.

speaker: narrator
text: Minus one hundred degrees. Only the fire burned. Thirty years of that. You sat before that fire. Not warm. But sitting. This was the baptism.

speaker: narrator
text: Argyre Canyon. Night. It had been Pilgrim Arms'. Now it was something else's. A place governed by names. A place without flags. The photo was there. The prosthetic was there. The names were there. The thorn crown. It was thorns but it was a crown. Always had been.

speaker: narrator
text: Sandstone Junction. Three directions. None of them. There was a code. Five things. The fifth was each person's own. You had a fifth. That was law. More lasting than any law on Mars. The prosthetic was worn. The names were felt.

speaker: narrator
text: New Athens Shipyard. Night. Cinder picked up her tools. New ones. Not the thirty-year-old things. But they made the same sound. Tools were tools. Not CV either. New. No name. Only names. On the back of the photo. In what was engraved inside.

speaker: narrator
text: From Erebus Mars was visible. CV's. The prosthetic was worn. On the left arm. Names engraved on the inside. They were felt. Thirty-year-old names. Zone 12. And now new ones. The warlord's crown was there. It was thorns. But it was a crown.

speaker: narrator
text: Erebus shook. But didn't collapse. CV was like that. The thing that didn't collapse. An organization made by a man who made a prosthetic at seventeen. Making things that don't collapse was that man's way. Erebus didn't collapse.

speaker: narrator
text: The battle ended. Erebus was alive. Butcher put the photo in his pocket. Slowly. With both hands. The prosthetic and the right hand. That was the last time. But CV was there. Fires burned. Cinder's tool sounds were heard. Crow watched the exterior. CV existed.

speaker: narrator
text: Erebus base. Fires burning. Barrel fires. Several. Butcher was in the throne hall. Alone. He had taken out the photo. On the table. First time. Outside the pocket. On the table. The lungs had said eleven hours. But he sat before the photo.

speaker: narrator
text: Three days since returning from Olympus. The Zone 12 records were brought back. The names appeared in official documents. Cinder added new names to the back of the photo. That was what came from Olympus. New names. The record of living things.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder came in. Tool sounds. She heard it. Didn't touch her tools. That was something heavy. Crow was behind. Raised in the canyon. Raised in darkness. But this room now was darker.

speaker: narrator
text: The photo was on the table. Black and white. Butcher at seventeen. The people beside him. Names. Miners. The strike. MCC. Thirty years. All of that was in this room. Why CV existed. It was on the photo.

speaker: narrator
text: Thirty years of questioning resolved. Why did he survive. Someone called him. From inside MCC. Who that person was he didn't say. Or didn't know. But he knew. Now. Thirty years later. What that felt like couldn't be read from his face.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss. Twenty-two years ago. Inside MCC. Zone 12. Her parents died there. That was the reason. Chen's mother. The person who called seventeen-year-old Butcher out of the tunnel thirty years ago. That reached this room. Through Olympus. Through tool sounds. Through names. Mars was small. Even thirty years couldn't make it wider.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow said there were sounds outside. From outside Erebus crater. Vehicle sounds. Many of them. From both MCC and FSP sides. Moving after the Olympus agreement. Toward the CV base. There was an agreement but force was needed for it to be kept.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside Erebus. Vehicles. At the crater's edge. Stopped. Waiting. For CV's decision. What CV would choose. What form CV would take. That was what this final battle would determine.

speaker: narrator
text: The prosthetic. Made at seventeen. Thirty years old. Cinder had repaired it and it still worked. He was giving it. Something worn on the left arm. What Butcher had worn for thirty years. That was the way of succession. CV's way. No document. No stamp. One prosthetic.

speaker: narrator
text: Names were engraved inside the prosthetic. Where they couldn't be seen. Something felt when worn. That was memory's way. Different from writing on the back of a photo. Engraving on the body. Feeling them. That was what Cinder had added.

speaker: narrator
text: Sounds outside Erebus grew louder. Vehicles began to move. At the crater's edge. The waiting was ending. CV had to decide. What kind of CV to become. How to protect Erebus. Or whether not to protect it.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher held out the photo. With the right hand. Not the prosthetic. Something in his pocket for thirty years. Something placed on the table. Being offered to another person. First time. First time in thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: The canyon. Night. Crow said it. Grew up here, he said. A time before knowing names. Before knowing CV. But the canyon was known. The narrow dark thing. That was the beginning. And now here.

speaker: narrator
text: Sandstone Junction. Southern Mars. Edge of CV territory. It split here. The road to Erebus. The road to Argyre. The road to Olympus. Three directions. CV always passed through here. The place of divergence. But each had their direction.

speaker: narrator
text: Back at Erebus. Vehicles were outside the crater. Waiting. For CV's choice. Butcher was in the throne hall. In the mining chair. The prosthetic and the photo were on the table. Two things. That was CV.

speaker: narrator
text: The photo was there. The prosthetic was there.

speaker: narrator
text: The names were there. Vehicles were outside Erebus.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher waited. Cinder waited.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow waited. Mars waited.

speaker: narrator
text: The demilitarized zone clause. A clause CV didn't sign.

speaker: narrator
text: But it was in the agreement. MCC and FSP put it there.

speaker: narrator
text: If CV recognized the agreement it had to recognize that too.

speaker: narrator
text: If not it would be outside the agreement.

speaker: narrator
text: That was the choice.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher lifted the photo.

speaker: narrator
text: Flipped it. Looked at the names.

speaker: narrator
text: New names were on the back of the photo.

speaker: narrator
text: Added by Cinder. After returning from Olympus.

speaker: narrator
text: Zone 12 names. Names now in official documents.

speaker: narrator
text: Those names were on the back of the photo too.

speaker: narrator
text: The Erebus base was quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: Fires burned. Barrel fires.

speaker: narrator
text: Fires that hadn't gone out in thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: Not warm. But burning.

speaker: narrator
text: That was CV. That had always been CV.

speaker: narrator
text: Argyre Canyon. Southern hemisphere. Five kilometers deep. Darkness was thick. Mars darkness was different from Earth. Thin air scattered less light. So it was darker.

speaker: narrator
text: Vasco Reyes. Call sign Crow. Four years in CV. Mars-born. Raised in the canyon since childhood. People raised in the dark had different eyes. He was someone for whom darkness was natural.

speaker: narrator
text: Baptism done. Tests done. What followed was work. In CV work meant operations. First operation assigned. Crow briefed. Short words.

speaker: narrator
text: Team of five. You. Crow. Three others. You knew their names. Marco. Jin. Hestia. People of few words. They said few words when working was good. You agreed.

speaker: narrator
text: Chose west drainage. Slow. Narrow. Water present. Martian water. Cold. But invisible. That mattered more. Being invisible.

speaker: narrator
text: Marco up front. Jin behind. Hestia covering the side. Crow in the middle. Five moving. No sound. That was the movement of trained people.

speaker: narrator
text: The depot visible. Lights on. Guards there. But something else too. Workers. Night shift. MCC mine workers. No weapons. Supply duty.

speaker: narrator
text: By CV standards, non-combatants. CV had a code. Don't touch non-combatants. That was the second code. But with workers present the operation couldn't proceed quietly.

speaker: narrator
text: One of the workers saw. That person stopped. Didn't run. Didn't shout. Just looked. Whether they saw a CV mercenary. Or something like themselves. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Those eyes were familiar. Eyes seen somewhere before. Hellas Central miners. People working without names. Numbers by MCC standards. But people with eyes. People with living eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: Decided. Moved. Crow followed. No words. That was Crow's way. Following even without agreement. In an operation there was no next.

speaker: narrator
text: Into the depot. Equipment there. Ore processing equipment. Heavy. Five needed to move it. Moved fast. In the direction without guards. But workers were there.

speaker: narrator
text: The worker stopped. Didn't move. Didn't shout. Didn't trigger the alarm. Couldn't tell why. Fear. Or something else. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Moved equipment. Fast. Marco and Jin took the heavy pieces. Hestia covered outside. Crow timed it. Fifteen minutes passed. Five left.

speaker: narrator
text: Out east. Fast. Almost ran into the guard. But there was darkness. Martian darkness. Thick. Hid inside it. Guard passed. That was all.

speaker: narrator
text: Down to the canyon floor. With equipment. Heavy. Legs aching. Didn't stop. Stopping meant the guards would follow. Not stopping meant they wouldn't. Simple.

speaker: narrator
text: Storm coming. Wind changed. Felt it at the canyon floor. Direction shifted. Dust storm. On Mars dust storms came without warning. Or they had been coming and you hadn't noticed.

speaker: narrator
text: Storm hit. No visibility. No sound. Only wind. Only dust. Five moving inside it. Holding each other's hands. That was the only way.

speaker: narrator
text: Lost direction. Couldn't tell canyon from plains. Crow knew direction. Someone raised in storms. Raised in the canyon. Someone for whom darkness was natural.

speaker: narrator
text: Storm passed. Slowly. Martian storms came and went. They were things with endings. Visibility returned. Stars. Canyon visible. Direction knowable.

speaker: narrator
text: Remembered the worker's eyes. The person who didn't press the alarm. Didn't know why. Fear or something else. But that choice existed. That choice had made tonight.

speaker: narrator
text: Canyon floor. Butcher was waiting. Prosthetic. Left arm. Old mining-grade. He had made it himself. At seventeen. He heard the report. No words. But the prosthetic moved.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher said no more. That was all. Couldn't tell if it was acknowledgment or not. But the prosthetic moved again. That was how he spoke without speaking.

speaker: narrator
text: Equipment moved to base. Heavy. Arms aching. But not gone. There it was. Now CV's. That was today's result.

speaker: narrator
text: No equipment. MCC had moved it first or guards were strong. Crow said nothing. On the way back to the canyon floor. Darkness thick. Mars darkness different from Earth. Felt that again.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow walked. No words. Silence on failure was Crow's way. Silence was the words. On Mars learning that was important.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher's words stayed. Equipment can be retrieved. People can't. A person who had lost an arm at seventeen. A person who knew people don't come back. Those were those words.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow walked behind. No words. That was Crow. Someone who followed even in failure. Without a word. That was CV code. Don't abandon a comrade. Fourth code.

speaker: narrator
text: Canyon floor. Butcher was waiting. Prosthetic. Left arm. Old mining-grade. Heard the report. No words. But the prosthetic moved. That was how he spoke without speaking.

speaker: narrator
text: Erebus base. Inside the crater. One of the coldest places in the southern hemisphere. Inside the base was different. Fires. Barrel fires. Several. CV liked fire. Fire had no rules. That was what fire had in common with CV.

speaker: narrator
text: Day after the operation. Butcher called everyone. That was rare. Butcher calling everyone. That was a signal something important had happened.

speaker: narrator
text: Four paths. Butcher said. Each takes a different road. That was the loyalty test. Choice was how loyalty showed. What you chose showed who you were.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza branch A. Revenge or forgiveness. Reza was still at the base. No longer prisoner status. Ambiguous after Butcher's decision. In the base but not a CV member.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza was there. In the corner. Hands unbound. But unable to leave. Unable to exit the CV base. Looked at you. Those eyes remembered. Aisha. Name.

speaker: narrator
text: Couldn't tell if Reza's words were true. Evidence existed. Evidence in CV. But evidence could be manufactured. MCC might have made it. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: The fifth code. Each person makes their own. What Butcher had said. Didn't understand when first heard. Now understood. It was for this moment. For this choice.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza answered. Gave a location. Hellas Central. Small district. Name. Contact method. That was all Reza could give. Received it. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Reported to Butcher. Result of the Reza branch. Butcher listened. No words. The prosthetic moved. That was all. That was acknowledgment.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza branch B. Extract intelligence. Reza knew things about MCC. Information CV needed. Crow knew that. But Reza hadn't spoken. There was a reason.

speaker: narrator
text: Went to Reza. Corner. Crow watching. But no words. When Crow was wordless it meant trust. Or waiting. Hard to distinguish.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza thought. For a long time. Eyes closed. Hands unbound. Those hands on the knees. Not trembling. That was how this person was strong. The way of deciding.

speaker: narrator
text: Went to Butcher. Passed the information. Butcher listened. Crow confirmed. No words. But the look in their eyes changed. The information was correct. Could tell that.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza left the base. Didn't look back. Walk wasn't fast. That was strange. Expected fast. But walked slowly. Steps of someone thinking.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher watched. Until Reza disappeared. That was all. That was Butcher's way. Watching. Watching for a long time. And saying nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: Marko branch. Negotiate with outside faction. Sandstone Junction. Middle of Mars. Neither MCC nor CV. Neutral ground. A meeting there. Marko Diel. Independent mercenary group leader.

speaker: narrator
text: Marko arrived. Not alone. Two behind. Armed. That was the way in neutral ground. Meet armed. Trust without trust.

speaker: narrator
text: Marko looked at you. For a long time. CV but a new face. A new face negotiating was strange. But that was Butcher's way. The way of testing new people.

speaker: narrator
text: Marko thought. Crow watched from behind. Quiet. No words. Crow's way in negotiations was silence. Negotiation was reducing words. The person with fewer words won.

speaker: narrator
text: Negotiation ended. Marko left. Crow approached. No expression. But spoke. Spoke for the first time. That was strange. Crow speaking after a negotiation.

speaker: narrator
text: Standard mission. Occupy mine district. Hellas outer mine. Abandoned by MCC. But things that could be used. Equipment. Passages. Things CV needed.

speaker: narrator
text: Into the mine. Dark. Light on. Passages. Old ones. Thirty years old. Before CV existed. Dug by miners. Now empty.

speaker: narrator
text: Something deeper in. Crates. MCC markings. But goods not in official records. Crow saw them. No expression. But the look changed. It was as expected.

speaker: narrator
text: Checked the crates. Weapon components. Large quantity. Things CV could use. Had to take them. But heavy. Hard to move fast.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher acknowledged. Words brief. That was his way. Fewer words meant more meaning. You kept the code. That meant you could be here, in this base.

speaker: narrator
text: The code was tested. Which code wasn't clear. On Mars the code was tested by situation. Situations taught it. Fire burned in barrels. The base was alive.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher spoke. Expel you or acknowledge you. Nothing in between. CV was that kind of place. No middle ground. But having no middle was actually clear. That was this base's way.

speaker: narrator
text: Fire burned. Night deepened. Cinder finished work. Something had been repaired. What it was she didn't say. Butcher sat by the fire. Looked down at the prosthetic. Made at seventeen. Thirty years old. Still working.

speaker: narrator
text: Good things were like that. Old but still working. The code was like that. Thirty years old. But still working. That was CV. The fire wasn't warm. But it burned.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace was a person of few words. CV had many people of few words. But Cinder was different. Not that she couldn't speak. She didn't speak because she had too much to say.

speaker: narrator
text: She repaired machines. Things in the base. Broken things. Ruined things. Things no one else could fix. That was what Cinder did in CV. Repair. Not combat. Repair.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a time with MCC. Six years. A mechanical engineer. Tunnel support systems. Most important thing in Martian mines. When they collapsed people died. She was the person who prevented that. For six years.

speaker: narrator
text: Morning and Cinder came to you. First time. On her own. Usually Cinder didn't approach first. Touching the tool belt. That was her signal. Signal of something to say.

speaker: narrator
text: Walked to the Hellas outskirts. The two of you. Cinder walked ahead. Not fast. But direction was clear. The walk of someone who knew this path. Had walked it before.

speaker: narrator
text: No words. Two hours walking. That wasn't strange. With Cinder silence was natural. Like the sound of tools. Present but natural as if absent.

speaker: narrator
text: Zone 12 visible. Abandoned mine. Entrance. Blocked. MCC marking. No entry. But an old marking. Three years old.

speaker: narrator
text: Into the mine. Dark. Cinder turned on a lamp. Passages. Old. Inside Cinder stopped. Looked at the wall. Put a hand on the wall. Didn't touch the tools. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder kept looking at the wall. Hand on the wall. Not moving. That was strange. Cinder's hands were always on tools. Hands that touched tools. Now on the wall. Cold wall.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder walked along the passage. Inside. Deeper. Lamp lit the way. Walls closer. Passage narrowing. Then blocked. Stopped there. Couldn't tell where that was.

speaker: narrator
text: Wall blocked. Beyond it something. Where the eleven were. Couldn't reach there. Three years of that. Couldn't tell if Cinder had come here or not. But those footsteps looked like ones walked before.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder took out the report. From a pocket. Small. Folded. Many times. Taken out often. Folded often. The names were there. Eleven.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder touched her tools. The ones on the belt. The ones that weren't weapons. That was her way. Touching tools settled thoughts. Three years of that. Not repairing tools but touching them. That was Cinder Grace's prayer.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher had lost an arm at seventeen. MCC had refused compensation. That and the eleven were the same thing. People whose names disappeared. People erased from records. People MCC deleted.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder folded the report again. Many times. Back into the pocket. Touched the tools again. Prayer ended. Thoughts settled.

speaker: narrator
text: Chose. Cinder looked. Those eyes were new. First time Cinder looked at you for a long time. Usually Cinder looked at tools. Machines. Walls. Didn't look at people long. But now looked.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder took out the report again. Unfolded it. Names. Eleven. Read them. Slowly. One by one. Only names. No explanation. No explanation needed. There were names. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Eleven names. Listened. Tried to remember. Didn't know if all eleven were possible. But listened. That was what Cinder wanted. Someone to listen.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder folded the report. Looking at the report there were tears. Not visible. Dark. But there was sound. Heard it. Pretended not to. That was the right thing.

speaker: narrator
text: Then sound. Outside. Toward the mine entrance. Footsteps. Multiple. MCC security. Not a regular check. Not supposed to come at this time. Something different.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder gripped the report. Back into the pocket. Touched the tools. That was a signal. Signal of preparation. Not preparing to fight. Something else. Preparing to flee. Or to protect.

speaker: narrator
text: Out of the abandoned mine. Cinder came out with the report. What she'd carried for three years. The names were there. Eleven. On Mars a person with a name remained there. Even without a record. Even when abandoned.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder touched the tool belt. Habit. Everything was there. Nothing missing. The eleven were gone. But the tools were there. The report was there. The memory was there.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC security came. Abandoned but there were guards. MCC guarded even abandoned mines. Things to erase there. No report. But it was in Cinder's memory. Memory had no security.

speaker: narrator
text: Back to base. Butcher was there. Before the fire. Cinder reported. Briefly. Butcher listened. No words. Looked down at the prosthetic. That was all.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun tilted toward Erebus. Martian sun. Small thing. Distant thing. Cinder checked the tool belt again. Habit. Everything was there. Nothing missing. The eleven were gone. But the tools were there. The report was there. The memory was there. Fire burned. Not warm. But burning.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC sealed the crater. Butcher watched. His hand went back in the coat pocket. Rested on the photo. Same as thirty years ago. The difference was that Cinder was beside him.

speaker: narrator
text: The outer edge of Kepler Crater. FSP was inside. The day Liang Wei declared. CV watched from outside. That was CV's position. Not inside. That had always been CV's position.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher came. That was rare. Butcher leaving the base. Left arm prosthetic. Old mining type. He had a coat. His hand was in the pocket. What was in that pocket was known. A photo. Thirty years old.

speaker: narrator
text: A sound came from inside the crater. Liang Wei's voice. The declaration. The voice of someone who had waited alone for thirty years. Butcher listened. The hand in the coat pocket didn't move. That was how Butcher paid attention. Didn't take out the photo. Listened.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC drones were in the sky above. One. Then two. Three. While the declaration proceeded inside the crater the drones multiplied. MCC was waiting. For when to intervene. Butcher looked at the sky. He took his hand from the coat pocket. Didn't take out the photo. Just the hand.

speaker: narrator
text: The CV scouting team had come here two days ago. From outer Hellas to Kepler. Red plains. Central Mars. Monotonous terrain. But monotonous terrain was easy to hide in. Twelve came. Without sound.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher walked first. The scouting team followed. The plains were wide. Wind blew low. Dust flew at ankle height. Kepler Crater was on the horizon. Still small. But Butcher's steps were fast. This person knew this direction.

speaker: narrator
text: They passed the exterior of Erebus Crater. CV territory boundary. From here it was neutral ground. Land nobody owned. That was the character of central Mars. Lands not yet worth owning. Until the Ancient Metal discovery.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher's health was deteriorating. Inside CV it was known. Lungs. Old mine dust. Different from Martian dust. Earth mine dust. Things from thirty years ago remained inside the body. Doing their work slowly.

speaker: narrator
text: They arrived at Kepler. The sun was tilting. Crater edge. Dust lay low. Couldn't see inside. Only sound. People gathered. Many people. More than expected.

speaker: narrator
text: People were at the crater edge. Miners. Tool belts. Helmets. Nameless people. Those who lived nameless on Mars had gathered. Come to hear Liang Wei's declaration. They were silent. Waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder was watching people. Judging. This person tested. Always. By situation. By people's reactions. Right now these people were being tested. By coming and waiting they were already saying something.

speaker: narrator
text: Then it was heard. Liang Wei's voice. From inside the crater. Without amplification. Bare voice. But it was heard. The shape of the crater held sound. Everyone heard it.

speaker: narrator
text: Silence. Then sound. The sound of miners. Not applause. Not words. The sound of helmets being struck. Mine signal. Agreement. That was their way. Learned in the noise of machines.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher listened. For a long time. The hand in the coat pocket moved. Touching the photo. Didn't take it out. Just touched. There had been a declaration thirty years ago. Back then it was different. No miners. No witnesses.

speaker: narrator
text: An MCC drone descended. One of them. From observation altitude to approach altitude. That was a signal. MCC was going to intervene. The miners saw it. The drone. The sound diminished. The helmet-striking stopped. But nobody moved.

speaker: narrator
text: It was also possible to sell to MCC. This information. Liang Wei's location. The content of the data. CV was neutral. Still. That could have a price. Cinder seemed to know that thought. She touched her tools. Checking.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher looked. At the miners. Those who had struck their helmets. Nameless people. Different from the people in the thirty-year-old photo. Different but the same. Things at the same place for the same reason. He took out the photo. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a decision. Cinder reacted. She moved her tools. Butcher looked at the photo. For a long time. Then put it back in the pocket. Putting it back was different from taking it out. Thirty years ago there had been no reason to take it out. Today there was.

speaker: narrator
text: The battle ended. The drones retreated. Or were gone. That was today's outcome. The miners were still there. Nameless people. Standing holding helmets. Facing Kepler Crater.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher took out the photo. Again. Second time. Twice in thirty years. Today. Looked at the miners. Looked at the photo. Looked at the miners again. The people in the photo and the people outside. Different. But the same.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun had completely tilted. Kepler was red. People began to scatter. Miners. Each in their own direction. Didn't stay long. Came. Watched. Left. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder looked at Kepler. The crater. Deep and dark. Ancient Metal inside. Extraterrestrial origin. Belonging to Mars. That was now declared. A declaration couldn't be undone. Whatever MCC might do.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher heard it. Cinder's words. No reaction. That was the reaction. This person did nothing when he agreed. Doing nothing was agreement. An old way. Learned in the mines.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC was still far. The drones had retreated. But hadn't disappeared. They would come tomorrow. More of them. That was known. But today CV was at the edge of Kepler. The Sandstone Promise had been here.

speaker: narrator
text: Kepler turned red. Butcher took his hand from the coat pocket. Not the photo. Just the hand. Cinder watched that hand. The hand that didn't meet the prosthetic. The right hand. The people in the thirty-year-old photo would still be there. Only in the photo. But today they were also here at the edge of Kepler. Because of the declaration.  Cinder saw FSP differently for the first time. That was what happened today. That was what the Sandstone Promise had done.

speaker: narrator
text: The room was quiet. Cinder's tool sounds were heard. From somewhere. Somewhere in the base. That was proof the base was alive. Butcher looked at the photo. With his right hand.
