The thirty-year-old thing. Names were there. Photos with names didn't disappear easily. He knew that. Had known since he was seventeen.

speaker: narrator
text: The battle ended. Couldn't get the records. Butcher sat in the chair. Mining chair. Old thing. He was holding the photo. Not flipped. The names were on the side you couldn't see. But they were there. Not gone. Memory was still there.

speaker: narrator
text: The deepest part of the Erebus base. Called the throne hall. Butcher liked that name. There was no throne. There was one chair. An old one. A mining chair. Taken from an MCC mine. Thirty years ago. That was the throne.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher was sitting there. Holding the photo. First time seeing it. Outside the pocket. Black and white. Old. Thirty years. There were people. Several. Miners. One of them looked like Butcher. Young. Seemed about seventeen.

speaker: narrator
text: The left arm. Prosthetic. Old mining type. Made by himself when MCC refused injury compensation. At seventeen. Thirty years since then. The same hand that made the prosthetic was now holding the photo. The right hand. Not trembling. No one had ever seen this man's hand tremble.

speaker: narrator
text: Flashback. The tunnel. Thirty years ago. Dark. Two hundred meters underground on Mars. Ore dust. Narrow passage. Several people working. Sounds were heard. Metal sounds. Ground sounds. That was the sound of a living tunnel. Miners knew that sound.

speaker: narrator
text: Third day of the strike. MCC cut the water. Reduced oxygen rations. The miners held. Seventeen-year-old Butcher held. There were names. Each person's name. Written in chalk on the tunnel wall. Recording who had been there.

speaker: narrator
text: Flashback. The morning after the accident. Tunnel entrance. MCC managers were there. Documents. Death processing. Quick paperwork. Official stamp. A manager showed the stamp to the seventeen-year-old. You're alive so sign here, he said. The seventeen-year-old didn't sign.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder was behind. Tool belt. No sounds. When this person didn't touch her tools. When there was no tool sound. She was waiting for something. In this room two people were waiting. For an answer.

speaker: narrator
text: Two people. Two identical stories. Different times. Different tunnels. Same company. Same method. Thirty years between them. But the stories were the same. That was something about Mars. There were things that repeated.

speaker: narrator
text: Erebus crater. Night. The base lights reflected off the crater walls. Down there was Mars. MCC's Mars. FSP's Mars. And the Mars of names. The third was widest. Not on any map. But widest.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder touched her tools. Sound came. Small. But heard. In this room even small sounds were heard. The room was built that way. A room Butcher had built. A room with a mining chair. A room where every sound was heard.

speaker: narrator
text: A question. The first question. The first reason. Remembering it. That was the test. Butcher's test. Memory. Remembering names. Remembering the first reason. Those were the same thing.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher flipped the photo. Names were there. Small writing. Many names. Thirty years old. Between the names there were gaps. Still space to write. Whether that was intentional was unknown. But there were gaps.

speaker: narrator
text: That was it. CV's way. Bringing a name. Remembering. Rewriting lost things. On Mars memory was power. As long as there were people who remembered names didn't disappear.

speaker: narrator
text: A name. That was the question. The first reason. Remembering. On Mars names disappeared easily. MCC deleted and they were gone. Gone from the records. Disappearing from memory was slower. As long as there were people who remembered.

speaker: narrator
text: The crater was quiet. Erebus. A volcano. A long-dead volcano. But inside was a base. Fires burned. People were there. A dead volcano holding living things. That may be why Butcher chose this place.

speaker: narrator
text: A mission. A mission to protect names. MCC archives. Zone 12 records. Cinder knew the route. She had worked there before. That memory remained. Memory became the path. That was also memory's way.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher put the photo in his pocket. Slowly. With the right hand. Not the prosthetic. That was unusual. This person always picked up the photo with the prosthetic. Today was different. The reason was unknown. But it was different.

speaker: narrator
text: This was the test. Butcher's thirty years were here. The names were on the back of the photo. Cinder was listening. The air in this room was old. The smell of a mining chair. The smell of earth. Old things. They were all here with this question.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder picked up her tools. That was the signal to move. When this person picked up tools work began. Thirty years ago this person wasn't here. But tonight she was. That was the difference. Tonight was not alone.

speaker: narrator
text: Night deepened. Erebus base. Fires burned. Barrel fires. Butcher sat by the fire. The photo was in his pocket. Not taken out. Cinder touched her tools without sound. That was how this base existed tonight. Fire. People. Tools. Things that were enough.

speaker: narrator
text: CV split in two. Crow's side. Reza's side. Cinder was neither. Only tool sounds were heard. From somewhere. Butcher looked down at the prosthetic. There had been no division thirty years ago. Because no one survived.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher collapsed. In the base. Alone. Cinder found him. The prosthetic had fallen off. That was something never seen before. Butcher without the prosthetic. Worn since he was seventeen. It had fallen away.

speaker: narrator
text: Medical came. Lung problem. Mars lung problems. Ore dust. Thirty years. What began in the mines appeared thirty years later. Butcher had been outside the mines for thirty years. But the lungs remembered.

speaker: narrator
text: Six months. That word spread through the base. Talk circulated in CV. Butcher's health. Who was next. CV had no official succession. No contracts. Only the code. The fifth code was made by each person. So each was different.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder reached for her tools. Stopped. Didn't touch them. That was strange. This person reaching for tools and stopping. When there was work she always touched them. There was work now. But she didn't touch them. The meaning was hard to know.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher's room. Throne hall. Mining chair. He came in. He walked as if he had never collapsed. He walked as if he had not heard the word six months. But slow. Slower than before. That was the only difference.

speaker: narrator
text: The room went quiet. Crow stepped back. Cinder didn't touch her tools. Butcher sat in the mining chair. Slowly. That was the first slow thing shown today. People pretended not to notice. Something had appeared in this room that shouldn't be seen.

speaker: narrator
text: Sounds from outside the crater. Vehicles. CV people gathered. Crow's people and Reza's people stood apart. There was an invisible line. Nobody had crossed it yet. But the line was there.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza. Reza Karimi. CV western sector commander. Ten years in CV. Same age as Crow. Raised in the same canyon. But a different person. Crow was tactics. Reza was territory. Taking the western passage of Erebus. That was Reza.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder picked up her tools. This time she didn't stop. She picked them up. That was a decision. In her way. Picking up tools. Not words but action. If CV survived it would be because of tool sounds.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza's people were in the western passage. Armed. Crow's people held the east in standoff. There was a line. No shots yet. But the line was narrowing. Three hours, Crow had said. But in reality it wasn't three hours. Less.

speaker: narrator
text: In Butcher's name. The weight of that name was known. Thirty years. A man who remembered names. A man who became a name. Going out in Butcher's name. That was the heaviest thing in this base right now.

speaker: narrator
text: Western passage entrance. Reza was there. Alone. For negotiations coming out alone was the rule. CV's rule. Reza knew the rule. That was someone ten years in CV. Knowing the rules and breaking them was different from knowing them and keeping them.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher heard. The report was delivered. He took out the photo. For the first time. During negotiations. Taking out the photo during work was a first. He looked at the back. Looked at the names. Thirty-year-old ones. Newly added ones. Zone 12. They were there.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza gave no answer. There was movement in the western passage. Crow's people tensed. Cinder was at the southern bypass. Alone. With her tools. Preparing the bypass. Silently. Only tool sounds.

speaker: narrator
text: Factions were forming. Crow's side. Reza's side. Cinder was neither. She picked up her tools. That was Cinder's answer. Being neither was the hardest thing. On Mars neutrality meant making two enemies.

speaker: narrator
text: Sound from outside the crater. MCC vehicles. External intelligence. MCC was approaching the outskirts of the CV base. MCC had sensed the faction conflict. Waited. Now moving. Internal fighting had called an external threat.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher stood. From the mining chair. Slowly. Like someone who had heard the words six months. But he stood. That was this man. He had stood like that for thirty years. That was the reason for being here.

speaker: narrator
text: Reza moved. To the west. That was the answer. No words. But he moved. Butcher's name still worked in this base. Six months remained. That was still enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Night. The plains were dark. Not darker than the canyon. Crow said it. The canyon was darker. Cinder touched her tools. Sound came. That was the music of this night. Butcher sat by the fire. Didn't take out the photo. Put his hand in the pocket. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: The gamble failed. CV scattered on the Argyre Plains. In the plains with nowhere to hide. But Butcher was still there. Coat. Pocket. Photo. As long as those were there CV could start again. As it had thirty years ago.

speaker: narrator
text: Argyre Plains. The largest basin on Mars. There CV gathered. Scattered things came together. Crow's group. Reza's group. Those with Cinder. And Butcher. They said six months but he was still there. On Mars six months was short but could be made long.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC and FSP went to the Olympus meeting. Two of three factions were at the table. A table without CV. CV was always outside the table. This time had to be different. Otherwise what was decided at the table came down to CV. That was what had happened thirty years ago.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher was wearing the coat. Hand in the pocket. On the photo. That was what he did before battle. For thirty years. Touching the names. Without speaking. With the hand. That was this man's preparation.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow looked at the Argyre Plains. Wide. One of the widest places on Mars. For someone raised in canyons plains were different. Battle in open ground was different. Nowhere to hide. That was what CV was choosing today. Not hiding.

speaker: narrator
text: It was a succession conversation. In this room. In the room with the mining chair. First time for this. Thirty years without it once. Butcher had always seemed like he would be here. Until six months ago. Now it was different.

speaker: narrator
text: Crow said it. His own weakness. In this room. Before Butcher. Whether it was courage or strategy was unclear. But he said it. In this room lying was meaningless. It was Butcher's room. He knew everything.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder's fear. Forgetting the names. That was the most honest thing in this room. Butcher heard it. Hand on the photo. Inside the pocket. Touching it. The names. While listening.

speaker: narrator
text: Communication from MCC. Sudden. They were going to exploit CV's internal conflict. Olympus talks were ongoing. A table without CV. MCC was trying to build an agreement without CV. An agreement dividing CV territory. Including Erebus.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher took out the photo. Flipped it. Looked at the names. Thirty-year-old ones. Zone 12. The ones in between. He placed it on the table. First time. The photo on the table. Both hands on the table. The prosthetic and the right hand.

speaker: narrator
text: CV gathered. On the Argyre Plains. There had been a crisis of division. But after Butcher placed the photo on the table things changed. Crow and Reza looked in the same direction. First time. Because of the photo. Because of the names.

speaker: narrator
text: The succession decision. Butcher didn't delay. Today could be the last chance. Had to be decided before Olympus. Who leads CV. Who carries the names.

speaker: narrator
text: A question. The last test. The names were on the table. The photo. Cinder touched her tools. Crow looked out the window. The Argyre Plains were beyond the window. Wide. Nowhere to hide. This question was the same.

speaker: narrator
text: Communication from FSP. They confirmed there was no seat for CV at the Olympus talks. FSP would accept MCC's proposal, they said. Dividing CV territory. Including Erebus. No time. A decision was needed.

speaker: narrator
text: Communications relay. Southern foot of Olympus. Cinder knew it. She was an engineer. A person with tools. Someone who could block it. But that could be the start of war. War with MCC. CV was gambling.

speaker: narrator
text: CV was on the Argyre Plains. Wide. Nowhere to hide. In the widest place on Mars CV was making a decision. That was the meaning of this moment. Not hiding. Deciding in the open.

speaker: narrator
text: External threat arrived. MCC advance team. Northern Argyre Plains. They came. They knew about CV's gathering. Intelligence was leaking. From inside. Another sign of division. From somewhere in Reza's side.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder picked up her tools. Crow moved. Two people who were on the verge of splitting moved together. The names made that possible. The photo was on the table. Carried from Erebus to here. Taken from Butcher's pocket.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher looked at the plains. Wide. Wider than the canyon. Wider than Erebus. This man had lived thirty years in narrow places. Canyon. Tunnel. Erebus. For the first time he was in a wide place. Whether that was good or bad couldn't be read from his expression.

speaker: narrator
text: Descending from Olympus Cinder checked her tools one by one. A habit. All there. Nothing missing. Like the names of Zone 12 not missing. Memory lasted longer than tools. That was known. But it was good for tools to last long too.

speaker: narrator
text: No table. Three factions went their ways. Cinder descended. No tool sounds. The way down Olympus. The names were in memory. Even without a document. There was memory. That didn't disappear.

speaker: narrator
text: Names appeared on the table. Zone 12. Eleven people. For the first time these names were in a document. With the signatures of all three factions. Cinder touched her tools. Sound came. On Olympus. At the highest point in the solar system. Tool sounds. That was the signature of this agreement.

speaker: narrator
text: Olympus Mons. Cinder Grace had ascended. With her tool belt on. Nobody had likely ever climbed this mountain with a tool belt. But that was Cinder's way. Tools had to always be present. Even on Olympus. Something might need repairing. Or even if not they had to be there.

speaker: narrator
text: Olympus Mons. The highest mountain in the solar system. Summit pressure 0.07 percent of Earth's. Without a mask ten seconds. That made it a meeting place. A place no one could stay long. That was the fair condition. For everyone.

speaker: narrator
text: She had been MCC. Six years. Then CV. Three years. Between them was Zone 12. Eleven people. Names. Names not on MCC's table or FSP's table. She came to this mountain carrying those. With the tool belt.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss held her tea. Didn't drink it. Rev. Hale seemed to be preparing to pray. Looked like preparation. Cinder touched her tools. Three people. Three ways. Three Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: A chair had been empty. From the start. Chen had left it empty. That meant she knew. That CV would come. Or that someone would. Everything in this room was what Chen had prepared. Including the tea.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder took out the photo. Black and white. Thirty years old. Flipped it. Names were there. She placed the names on the table. Next to documents. Next to the draft agreement. Next to what MCC had prepared. Those things and the photo were on the same table.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen set down her tea. On the table. The undrunk thing. Rev. Hale said something. Names. Kim Yong-jin. Mariam. Zone 12. Eleven people. Cinder heard. Hearing the Zone 12 names from outside was the first time. How this person knew. Prayer sometimes called names.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen knew. Everything. MCC recorded. The records reached this room. That was Chen. All records went to her. Zone 12 too. She knew. And today she left this seat empty. For CV.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder touched her tools. Sound came. In this room. At the summit of Olympus. Tool sounds. Chen picked up her tea. Didn't drink it. Rev. Hale closed his eyes. Prayer. Or thought. Hard to distinguish.

speaker: narrator
text: Pilgrim Arms. Mars's independent mercenary organization. Belonged to no faction. But moved when someone hired them. Four were on Olympus. Since this morning. Chen knew. That meant MCC knew.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen had mentioned the MCC board interior possibility. In this room. She had spoken of the inside of her own organization. That was a dangerous statement. Or a calculated one. Whether Chen's statements had ever been uncalculated was unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder picked up her tools. At the summit of Olympus. At the highest point in the solar system. Moving with tools. That was this person. Always. For the names. For Zone 12. And for the people here today.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen unlocked the Zone 12 records. As of today. What that meant. Something she had held for twenty-two years. Something locked away for twenty-two years. Her parents were in there. Chen's. Miners who died at Zone 12. She opened it today. In this place. Before Cinder. She didn't say why. But she opened it.

speaker: narrator
text: Pilgrim Arms four moved. The eastern two were approaching along the base's outer wall. Cinder went out. With tools. The western two were blocked by Rev. Hale's security. Chen and player remained in the room.

speaker: narrator
text: The names were on the table. On the back of the photo. Black and white. Thirty years old. Zone 12. That was the reason for this meeting. Ahead of the draft agreement. Ahead of MCC documents. The names came first.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen was the target. Pilgrim Arms was after Chen. Who hired them was unknown. MCC board interior. Or elsewhere. Chen may have known. But she wasn't surprised. She held her tea. Didn't drink it.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder touched her tools. Sound came. In this room. At Olympus. An answer. Not in words but in sound. Tool sound. That was Cinder's way. That was the answer to this situation.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder went out. With tools. To cut east communications.

speaker: narrator
text: Only Chen and the player remained in the room.

speaker: narrator
text: Sound from outside. Footsteps.

speaker: narrator
text: Fast ones. Pilgrim Arms.

speaker: narrator
text: Tool sounds from outside.

speaker: narrator
text: On Olympus. At the highest point in the solar system.

speaker: narrator
text: Tool sounds.

speaker: narrator
text: Then fast sounds. Twice.

speaker: narrator
text: Then quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: People gathered in the room again.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale. Chen Weiss. Cinder Grace. The player.

speaker: narrator
text: The photo was on the table. The one with Zone 12 names.

speaker: narrator
text: The draft agreement paper was there.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder's tools were at the table's edge.

speaker: narrator
text: This table was the Olympus table.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder touched her tools.

speaker: narrator
text: Sound came. On Olympus.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale heard that sound.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen drank the tea. First time in this room.

speaker: narrator
text: That meant something.

speaker: narrator
text: The agreement was written.

speaker: narrator
text: Clauses from three factions were included.

speaker: narrator
text: Zone 12 names were included. For the first time. In an official document.

speaker: narrator
text: A Talon Group investigation clause was included.

speaker: narrator
text: There were four signature lines.

speaker: narrator
text: Three faction representatives. And one more.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder picked up the pen.

speaker: narrator
text: Not something from the tool belt. A pen.

speaker: narrator
text: She signed. As a Zone 12 survivor.

speaker: narrator
text: Tool sound came. As she put down the pen.

speaker: narrator
text: That was her way.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central. Largest settlement in the southern hemisphere. Population four thousand. Half were miners. The rest lived off those miners. There was law. MCC had made it. That was the law.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a rumor. Something south. It had a name. CV. Crimson Warlords. Everyone who mentioned it said something different. Some called them raiders. Some called them survivors. Some said nothing at all.

speaker: narrator
text: You had been in this bar for two days. You planned to stay until the money ran out. When the money was gone you'd think about what came next. That was how you had lived until now.

speaker: narrator
text: That stuck. Dead or staying. Maybe no difference. But if there was a difference — couldn't tell if staying was worse or better.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a man in the corner. Scars on his hands. Not a miner's hands. Different scars. His eyes met yours first. He didn't look away. That was strange. No one in this bar held your gaze.

speaker: narrator
text: The man said nothing more. Drank his drink. When the glass was empty he stood. Left without looking back. His steps were quiet. Not the walk of someone from this city.

speaker: narrator
text: Next morning. You were walking south. Didn't know why. Just walking as if there was a reason. The south of Mars was colder. The ground was redder. The air thinner.

speaker: narrator
text: No map. Only direction. South. Only rumor. Erebus. Only a name. Crater. That was all. That was how you got here.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central disappeared from view. Only plains remained. Vast. Empty of people. On Mars empty places were dangerous. No help. But nothing to harm you either. That was the difference between danger and freedom.

speaker: narrator
text: Three hours walking. Not hungry. Cold. Day on Mars was minus thirty degrees. Night approached minus one hundred. You knew that. Didn't stop.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun tilted. The Martian sunset was different. Blue. Earth sunsets were red. Martian sunsets were blue. Those who knew that said it felt strange the first time they saw it. Now it felt natural to you. Couldn't tell if you had changed or adapted to Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Sound from behind. Footsteps. More than one. Stopped. Didn't turn around. Nowhere to run. No reason to fight. Just waited. That was all there was to do in this situation.

speaker: narrator
text: Two of them. Armed. Faces covered. Only eyes visible. Those eyes studied you for a long time. Top to bottom. Bottom to top. Couldn't tell what they were looking for. Whether you were dangerous. Useful. Or should disappear.

speaker: narrator
text: The two looked at each other. Said nothing. But something was decided. You could see it. In faces where only eyes were visible. Eyes that spoke.

speaker: narrator
text: The blindfold went on. Light disappeared. Only sounds remained. Wind. Footsteps. The two and your own. No way to tell direction. No way to know where. But you walked. That was what could be done now.

speaker: narrator
text: Didn't know how long. Felt the terrain change through the feet. From flat to slope. Downward. A sense of deepening. Descending into a crater. You could tell.

speaker: narrator
text: The air changed. Colder. But no wind. Inside the crater. Walls blocked the wind. Sound changed. Echo. Deep place. Firelight felt through the blindfold.

speaker: narrator
text: Stopped. Footsteps stopped. Blindfold removed. Eyes took time to adjust. Firelight. A large fire. Burning at the crater floor. People. Many of them. All watching.

speaker: narrator
text: No one spoke. That was strange. A place where someone arriving brought no words. But not dangerous. Not yet. You could tell.

speaker: narrator
text: A man sat before the fire. Large and heavy. A prosthetic. Left arm. Old mining-grade. He lifted his eyes from the fire. Looked at you. For a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: That was all. No welcome. No warning. The fire just burned. People went about their work. You stood before the fire. Not warm. Fire burning but not warm. Minus one hundred degrees.

speaker: narrator
text: This was CV. Fire was here. Burning. But not warm. That was this place. Didn't take long to understand. Already knew it. Maybe that was why you'd come this far.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher Vasquez looked back at the fire. The conversation was over. Or it had never begun. Someone else appeared. A woman. Tool belt on her arm. Sharp eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace turned away. Touched her tools. The ones on the belt. A habit. You stayed before the fire. It burned. Not warm. But burning.

speaker: narrator
text: Looked around. People. Each with their own wounds. People whose names you didn't know. But people in the same place. People around a fire. Around a fire that wasn't warm.

speaker: narrator
text: Night was coming. The sky above the crater darkened. Stars came out. Martian stars. Same stars as seen from Earth but different stars. Stars seen from here. That made them different.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone handed over a blanket. No words. Didn't know their name. Just handed it over. You took it. That was the first exchange here. Something done without words. That was CV.

speaker: narrator
text: Fire burned. Not warm. But a fire that had not gone out in thirty years. You were here. The first night. Couldn't tell if this was a choice or a discovery. Maybe this was a place where those two things were the same.

speaker: narrator
text: The tea had gone cold. Mikhail looked at the two cups. One was empty. The other was untouched. The person hadn't drunk it. Had held it and set it down.  Mikhail didn't find this strange. People who came to Mars came in their own ways. What mattered was that the cup had been accepted. With both hands.  And forty-nine were outside. That mattered too.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Basin. FSP headquarters. Morning. Mikhail Anders didn't look at the window. He knew Mars was on the other side. Knowing was enough. He boiled water for tea. Two cups. Two cups if a guest came and two cups if he was alone. It had been that way for thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: The water boiled. He waited. No hurry. This wasn't only true of tea. It had been true when he was a miner too. His right leg ached. It always did when he sat. The mine accident. The leg remembered it. He could forget other things. The leg didn't.

speaker: narrator
text: He poured the tea. With both hands. His right hand cradled his left. It was a thirty-year habit. He couldn't remember which miner had taught him. But he remembered the two hands. The cups filled. Both cups filled.

speaker: narrator
text: The door opened. Cold air came in. A person came in behind it. Carrying a small bag. Rough hands. Miner's hands, but not a miner. This was the one Amara had recommended. Why this person had come to Mars wasn't asked. What mattered was being here now.

speaker: narrator
text: The person took the tea. Held the cup in both hands. Didn't drink. Just held it. Mikhail saw this. Said nothing. There were people who took tea and didn't drink it. That was their way. That too was a way.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail said. Amara contacted me yesterday. Fifty-five miners north of Hellas. There was an accident. MCC sealed the site. Nobody knows if the miners are inside or out.  Get inside. Confirm survivors. That's all.

speaker: narrator
text: The person still hadn't drunk the tea. Still holding the cup. Mikhail looked at it for a moment. The tea was cooling. Tea always cooled fast. On Mars everything cooled fast. Warmth was something to protect.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena had a tattoo on her left arm. Names. Family names. Mikhail saw those names every time. He always had the same thought when he did. How many of them were still alive. He had never said the thought aloud.

speaker: narrator
text: A map was spread. Northern Hellas. Mine sector. MCC perimeter marked. Three entry routes. Two of them guarded. The third was clear. There would be a reason for it being clear.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail pointed at the map. With both hands. The right supporting the left. The same way as when pouring tea. A person whose way of handling important things was the same. Whether a map or tea.

speaker: narrator
text: Preparations were made inside the FSP base. Equipment. Communicator. Medical kit. Lena checked them. Quickly. That was her way. Fast but missing nothing. That was the way of surviving long.

speaker: narrator
text: Amara was still for a moment. No words. Then she nodded. That was her way. A political person accepted a valid counter. If there was a better way they took it. That was politics.

speaker: narrator
text: Heading north. Martian surface. Red. Wind. Sand flew low. Ahead the MCC perimeter was visible. Signs. Warning lights. One drone in the sky. Quiet. Quiet was the more frightening thing.

speaker: narrator
text: The guards watched. Two came forward. MCC standard security suits. Helmets. Communicators. They didn't speak. They stood. That was speech. Don't come here. Or say where you're from.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena stepped forward. The fast person. The arm tattoo was visible. The names swayed. That was all. That might be enough.

speaker: narrator
text: There was exchange with MCC guards. Words and wordlessness. Together that was negotiation. On Mars negotiation was like that. More than words the posture. More than posture the eyes. More than eyes the next action.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the mine. Dark. Only some lights alive. Tunnels. Narrow ones. From their end a sound came. Voices. Voices of living people.

speaker: narrator
text: Forty-nine were alive. Six injured. Two critically. Lena went in first. Looking for Park Sung-jin. Found. That name. The name on the arm. That living name.

speaker: narrator
text: Miners came out. One by one. They received light. The morning light of Mars. It touched them. Someone shielding their eyes. Someone just standing. One person knelt. Touched the ground. The Martian earth. The red thing.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena was with Park Sung-jin. No words. Two people. The name on the arm. The living name. That was here now.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC lifted the seal. There was a formal protest. That was for later. What mattered now was that forty-nine were outside. Tea was waiting. Mikhail's tea.

speaker: narrator
text: Gaia launched.

speaker: narrator
text: The first ship made on Mars. By Mars's own power.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu Adeyemi watched. With the letter in hand.

speaker: narrator
text: Mariam. The ship carried that name.

speaker: narrator
text: On the way back to the Hellas mining village Mikhail spoke.

speaker: narrator
text: 'The names are recorded. What comes next Yuna decides.'

speaker: narrator
text: Yuna held the cup with both hands.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail made tea. Two cups. Poured with both hands. Lena came in. She drank hers. This time the other person drank too. One miner was dead. That didn't change. But the tea was warm.  There was evidence. Three refusals. That didn't change either. There were two kinds of things that didn't change. Death and records. Both were here today.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena Torres was a fast person. Fast walk, fast talk, fast judgment. A tattoo on her left arm. Names. Family names. Wrist to shoulder. When she moved fast those names moved with her.

speaker: narrator
text: When those names had come to be wasn't known. They must have come one by one. A name being added wasn't someone being born. It was someone disappearing. That was why they became tattoos. Engraving lost things on the body.

speaker: narrator
text: A miner had died. Mine 7 on the outer Hellas belt. Tunnel collapse. MCC territory. MCC sealed the accident. No notice to the family. No notice was the notice. On Mars that kind of notice came often.

speaker: narrator
text: The name was Park Sung-jin. Thirty-four. Two daughters. From Hellas mining village. Three years on the rotation at Mine 7. Three days ago the body was found. MCC didn't extract it. Said accident investigation in progress. Three days had passed.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena's left arm was visible. The tattoo. The names. How many of those names had come this way was not something to ask. She hadn't said. Fast people often had things they didn't say.

speaker: narrator
text: The family was there. Outside the perimeter. A woman with two children. The older child held the younger one's hand. The woman stood. Did nothing. Only waited. On Mars waiting was work.

speaker: narrator
text: There was an MCC perimeter line. Signs. Two guards. Inside the tunnel was a body. The family waited. Sand rode the wind. Mars was not kind to those who waited.

speaker: narrator
text: One of the guards moved. Walked toward the family. Said something. The woman didn't respond. The guard returned. The small child cried. The older one comforted. A seven-year-old comforting a four-year-old.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena's arm was visible. Her fist was clenched. The tattoo names bunched together. That was how Lena held back anger. Clenching a fist. Clenching names inside it. The names holding her.

speaker: narrator
text: Action was taken. MCC responded. Whether it was negotiation or confrontation or documentation. Something moved. On Mars what moved was what was alive.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC didn't issue a formal apology. No compensation. No accident report came out. That was for later. For now the family had taken the body. That was today's thing.

speaker: narrator
text: Two children went. The woman went. Didn't look back. The mine was there. Mine 7. MCC perimeter still there. Signs. Guards. Drone. And inside there was nothing. Now.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail made tea. The right hand supported the left. The same way. Always the same way. Even after hearing accident news. Even after hearing news of death. That way didn't change. Having something that didn't change was important.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena came. Looked at her arm. The names. Didn't write a new name. Not yet. That was for later. For now she was holding it. That too was a way.

speaker: narrator
text: Night. FSP base. A few lights. People. People who knew today's news. But they didn't speak. Not speaking was respect. On Mars silence was sometimes like that.

speaker: narrator
text: There was evidence. Site documentation. Some MCC supervisor communication records. Support repair requests had been made three times. Three times refused. Because of cost. That was in the record.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena looked at her arm. In the dark. The tattoo was visible. The names. One by one. Under some names there was a date. The day they disappeared. The day of disappearing was engraved.

speaker: narrator
text: The next day Mine 7 was seen again. Perimeter. Signs. Guards. But different. One of the MCC guards watched. Eyes met. That person looked away first. That was saying something.

speaker: narrator
text: Mine 7 was there. Nothing inside. Still a sign saying investigation in progress. When that would come down wasn't known. But there was a record. Three refusals. That wouldn't come down.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn broke. Mikhail made new tea. Several cups. The right supported the left. Yuna received tea. With both hands. That was learned. Learned tonight. Learned in this village. The tea was warm.  Sixty stayed. The cemetery stayed. The names stayed. The temporary village on Mars. Twenty years old. Surviving one more day.

speaker: narrator
text: The village emptied. The fire went out. The cemetery remained. The names remained. What MCC would do with a cemetery that had names was unknown. It was not a thing to want to know.

speaker: narrator
text: A village. Outside the MCC mine. Not an official settlement. A temporary residential zone. On Mars temporary meant lasting. A twenty-year temporary village. People were born there and worked there. Some died there.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC issued an order. Zone evacuation. Two weeks. No reason given. Orders without reason were the most frightening thing on Mars. If there was a reason there was room to argue. Without a reason there was nowhere to argue.

speaker: narrator
text: The village had a cemetery. Miners' graves. Names were there. Some written in chalk. Some engraved on metal plates. Old. New. Mixed. What to do with that cemetery was also not in the order.

speaker: narrator
text: Yuna Kim. Born on Mars. Raised in this village. Her father was in the cemetery. That name was there. On a metal plate. An old one. But polished like new.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a fire. Outside fire was dangerous on Mars. But these people had one. They must have for twenty years. Mikhail made tea. The right hand supported the left. It was the same here. Lena held her left arm in the firelight. The tattoo was visible. The names swayed.

speaker: narrator
text: The fire burned. Mikhail's tea cooled. He drank it. Holding the cup with both hands. This man had been a miner. Before he made FSP. First generation on Mars. That was in those two hands. The hands of this village's people were the same. Same dust. Same calluses.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a neighboring village. Hellas outer Zone C. Twenty people lived there. Also MCC territory. Also had an evacuation order. If the two villages combined that was fifty. Ten short for the residency clause. There was another place. Farther away.

speaker: narrator
text: Yuna looked toward the cemetery. In the dark. Metal plates glinted in the firelight. Names. Those seemed to be listening to this discussion now. Protecting where names were and protecting people who had names. Whether those were the same thing or different.

speaker: narrator
text: The fire burned. The village was quiet. People were gathered. Each with their own thoughts. The weight of staying. The weight of leaving. On Mars when choosing between two things both were heavy. Sometimes there was no good choice.

speaker: narrator
text: There was an MCC order. Two weeks. No reason. It was over this village. Over the names. Over the children. Over the fire. There was a way to make it void. Sixty people. Residency rights. But that might not be a resolution.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a decision. It became movement. People moved. On Mars people moving meant something was decided. Without a decision there was no movement. With a decision movement was fast.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC came. Of course. When there was movement MCC came. Guards. Drones. Official documents. That was MCC's way. Coming officially. That was the most frightening thing.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC counted. Actually. One by one. That was how the bureaucratic thing worked. Count. Record. Count again. Yuna waited. Didn't move. Sixty people didn't move.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn broke. Light came to the village. Sixty people. Children came out. Those children ran through the village. Adults watched. Some smiled. Some just watched. Both were right.

speaker: narrator
text: Light reached the cemetery. Names received the light. Metal plates. Chalk names. Old. New. Mixed. The light touched them evenly. That was what Martian morning light was like. It didn't distinguish.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena stood before the cemetery. Looked at her left arm. The names on the arm. Whether any of them were among those here couldn't be known. Mars was wide. Names were scattered. But what was engraved was engraved.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC documents were still being processed. That would take a long time. MCC documents always took a long time. That too was a method. Pressuring with time. But right now there were sixty people. As long as sixty were here the documents had to wait.

speaker: narrator
text: Yuna bowed toward the cemetery. That was all. No words. That was her way. There was quiet courage. Courage that didn't speak loudly. That was how she had led sixty people.

speaker: narrator
text: Alone at the junction. The sun tilted. The sand turned red. Footprints scattered in three directions. There had been a meeting on Mars. There had been a promise. That promise would change the future of Mars. Or it would be erased by wind like the sand of Sandstone. Which it would be was not yet known.  But the Zone 12 name was on two arms. One as a tattoo. One as memory. That the wind couldn't erase.

speaker: narrator
text: No promise. Only footprints remained at the junction. Each in their own direction. Which direction Cinder went was not seen. Sandstone remained as it was. A place with a name for a reason. Sand and stone. Good for promises. Good for keeping them too. But not today.

speaker: narrator
text: Sandstone Junction. Central Mars. Not in any faction's territory. Which was why all three factions passed through it. The sand was red. Old footprints on the sand. All came from different directions. All left in different directions.

speaker: narrator
text: Sandstone. Sand and stone. The name had a reason. Here the road split in three. Hellas. Erebus. Olympus. Three directions. Somewhere between them MCC existed. Not visible but present.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace had arrived first. CV. Tool belt. Oil on her hands. This was someone who worked everywhere. Even when there was no work she looked like she was working. That was her way.

speaker: narrator
text: The tool belt told you. Worn things. Much used. Not used carelessly. Used precisely. Tools spoke of who used them. This person was a repairer. Not a destroyer. Those two were different.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder ran her hand over the tool belt. Unconscious. This was her check. Whether everything was there. Nothing missing. She was a person who confirmed what was present. Not a person who searched for what was lost.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder looked at Lena's arm. Looked for a long time. Didn't touch her tools. That was this person's attention. When she didn't touch her tools she was thinking something. Perhaps she was reading the names.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder's eyes stopped at a certain name. Recognizing. What that was couldn't be known. But there was a stopping. Names did that. A known name stopped the eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena looked down at her arm. That name. Zone 12. A name two people knew. One had engraved it on their arm. One had been there three years ago. That was at Sandstone now.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena listened. It was a moment when a fast person became slow. A promise. Zone 12 name. Tool belt. Those things were at this junction. Sandstone. A place with a name for a reason.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC wasn't visible. But that didn't mean absent. A drone was probably somewhere. Observing. MCC was always observing. That made this promise more important. Promises made before those who watched had different weight.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun tilted. The sand of Sandstone turned redder. Three directions. Hellas. Erebus. Olympus. Between them two people stood. FSP. CV. And one name. Zone 12.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a decision. Cinder heard. There was a reaction. She touched her tools. Or she didn't. What came next differed by that. At Sandstone decisions were like that. Small things made large things.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder said nothing. She took something from the tool belt. A small metal pin. She pushed it into the ground. Into the sand. What it was couldn't be known. No explanation. She just did it. This was Cinder's way. Testing with something other than words.

speaker: narrator
text: The MCC drone moved away. It had seen. It had recorded. That was MCC's way. Seeing. Recording. Then deciding. What it was deciding now couldn't be known.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena looked at her arm. Zone 12 name. Cinder had known that name. She had been there. That was what had happened here today. Together with a promise. Or without one.

speaker: narrator
text: That was the test. Not planting the pin. Leaving Sandstone as belonging to neither side. That was the first condition for this promise to be possible. Cinder didn't say it in words. She did it with action. The action of not planting the pin.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder turned her back. Looked in one direction. Toward Erebus. Something was there. Or wasn't. Unknowable. But Cinder looked that way. For a long time. That was the second test. Showing her back.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder turned around again. She took something from the tool belt. A small knife. Flat. For mining. She drew it across her left palm. Slowly. Without sound. Blood came.

speaker: narrator
text: The knife came across. From Cinder's hand. To this side. Lena looked. Cinder's bleeding hand. It was waiting. A hand bleeding alone. Waiting for an answer.

speaker: narrator
text: Blood mixed. Or didn't. That was today's business at Sandstone. There was a handshake. Or there wasn't. But that two people had stood at this junction didn't change. The arm with the Zone 12 name. The tool belt with the mine knife.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder wrapped her hand. With cloth. Taken from the tool belt. Something she had prepared. This person had come knowing this. The bleeding. The wrapping. Things prepared. That was this person's way. Planning and acting.

speaker: narrator
text: Dust rose from the Erebus direction. Not wind. Movement. CV people were there. Things that had been waiting. Waiting for Cinder's signal. Not coming this way now. Waiting. That was what Cinder had done. Came alone but not alone.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder looked at her wrapped hand. The cloth. Something she had prepared. This person had come today knowing this would happen. That the promise would be this way. Or not this way. Prepared for both. That was CV's way.

speaker: narrator
text: The Sandstone Promise was before Kepler. There was an order. First the promise. Then Kepler. That was Cinder's plan. This person planned and acted. Not just acted. That was the difference from Butcher.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder looked toward Erebus. She signaled. With her hand. The CV people that way moved. Moving away. That was it for today. Business at the junction had ended. Or begun.

speaker: narrator
text: Kepler Crater turned red. The Martian sun tilted. Liang Wei looked once more. At the crater. At what she had seen for thirty years. At what she had seen today for the first time with others. There were moments when what was alone became shared. That was a declaration. On Mars that was what a declaration was.  Ancient Metal was there. Extraterrestrial origin. Thirty years of data. One name. Kepler Commons. That existed now.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC sealed the crater. Liang Wei was gone. Where she went was unknown. The thirty years of data was gone too. Kepler Crater was still there. Deep. Dark. It had a name now. A name given by others.

speaker: narrator
text: Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. Where Liang Wei had surveyed alone for thirty years. Nobody had supported her. Not MCC. Not FSP. She came alone. Stayed alone for thirty years. She was the oldest thing in this crater.

speaker: narrator
text: Liang Wei Jin. Geologist. First generation Mars settler. Seventies. People in their seventies on Mars were rare. Most had left. To Earth. Or farther. Liang Wei had stayed. Because of Kepler.

speaker: narrator
text: Ancient Metal. The extraterrestrial origin hypothesis. MCC knew. MCC intended to monopolize it. Before that Liang Wei had contacted FSP. She didn't explain why. But the reason was visible. Someone who had been alone for thirty years wanted to share something. Especially something important.

speaker: narrator
text: The crater floor. Light came in. Morning light. The angle was special. Only at this time did the angle become this. Liang Wei knew. Thirty years had made it known. The light touched something. Something like metal. But not metal.

speaker: narrator
text: Words were spoken. What had not been said for thirty years was said now. The air changed. The air inside the crater. Thin. Cold. But those words were there. Harder than metal.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena's left arm was visible. Tattoo. Names. Whether any of those names were connected to this crater was unknown. But the way Lena listened to this declaration was different. It was a moment when a fast person became slow.

speaker: narrator
text: An MCC drone was visible above the crater. One. For observation. MCC was always observing. That was MCC's way on this planet. Sometimes it couldn't be seen. But that didn't mean it wasn't there.

speaker: narrator
text: The drone became two. Then three. Observation intensified. That meant MCC had learned something. Liang Wei's declaration had already reached MCC. Or the drones had been listening here.

speaker: narrator
text: The miners' assembly began. Liang Wei led it. At the crater floor. Nearly a hundred people circled. FSP miners. Hellas village people. Nameless people. People who had waited a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: People began to move. Data sticks. Copying. Hand to hand. That was how it spread. Not digitally. Person handing to person. The oldest way on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: One drone lowered. From observation altitude to approach altitude. That was different. Observation had distance. Approach had no distance. There was a difference.

speaker: narrator
text: Then a person came. From the crater entrance side. Not alone. Three of them. Their suits were different. MCC suits. They tried to enter into the crowd.

speaker: narrator
text: The miners moved. Without words. With their bodies. They stood before the MCC representatives. Blocking. No violence. Just standing. A hundred standing before three. The MCC representatives stopped.

speaker: narrator
text: The word seed was said. Something not yet existing. But spoken. On Mars things that didn't exist were of two kinds. Things not yet existing. And things that would never exist. What Liang Wei spoke today was on the not-yet side.

speaker: narrator
text: There was action. The drone responded. MCC responded. That was all. The rest time would decide. Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. Ancient Metal. Thirty years of data. One declaration. Those were colliding here now.

speaker: narrator
text: People came to the outside of the crater. People who had heard. Hellas miners. People from neighboring villages. They looked at Kepler. The crater. Three kilometers deep. Where Ancient Metal was. They said nothing. But they were there.

speaker: narrator
text: From the edge of Kepler Crater CV was watching. That was known. If there was the Sandstone Promise this moment was its test. CV was there. At the crater edge. Hadn't come inside. But was there.

speaker: narrator
text: The data spread. Hand to hand. Out of the crater. To the Hellas villages. The sticks moved. MCC blocked communications. But couldn't stop people walking. On Mars people walking couldn't be stopped.

speaker: narrator
text: Seventies. First generation on Mars. Thirty years. Alone. That was the reason for no fear. Being alone for thirty years changes fear. Doesn't eliminate it. Changes it. The object changes.

speaker: narrator
text: CV was at the edge. Cinder was there. Hadn't come inside. That was also the limit of the Sandstone Promise. The promise existed. But it wasn't coming all the way inside. Guarding from the edge. That too was guarding.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail heard the report. Made tea. The right hand supported the left. He drank it. There was an MCC person inside FSP. That might not be a new fact. On Mars no organization had no moles. Knowing it and not knowing it were different. Knowing meant you could choose.  The tea was warm. That was what could be confirmed tonight. The tea being warm. Beyond that was tomorrow.

speaker: narrator
text: Guards in the passage. Kenji was gone. Data was gone. MCC had already known. Moles were on both sides. It was always that way.

speaker: narrator
text: There was an underground passage. Below MCC headquarters. Built when it was constructed sixty years ago. MCC built it but MCC didn't know all of it. No one knew everything about a large building. That was the nature of large buildings.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central. MCC Hellas Basin headquarters. A large building. Glass and metal. Shining even in the Martian dust. That was intentional. Shining things looked strong. Looking strong mattered to MCC.

speaker: narrator
text: Kenji Nakamura. Grade 3 MCC technical engineer. Five years in the same position. Five years without promotion. On Mars five years without promotion meant one of two things. Incompetence. Or doing something else. Kenji was not incompetent.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a passage entrance. Behind the building. Waste disposal zone. A place nobody came. Even more so at night. That was why it was the meeting place. A place where nobody came. A place to exist as if not existing.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas labor district. Different at night. In the day people were there. At night fewer. But not completely empty. Night shift workers. Cleaners. People who worked in the Martian night were there. Always were.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena heard it. The fast person stopped. That was rare. When Lena stopped something heavy was there. The names in the tattoo on her left arm. One of them might have died because of the FSP mole. That was not yet knowable.

speaker: narrator
text: Kenji Nakamura. Thirty-five. Father had been a worker at Hellas Mine 8. After retirement there was no pension. MCC regulations had changed. He had worked thirty years before the change. After the change the pension was gone. That was why Kenji was here.

speaker: narrator
text: Kenji handed over a package. Small. A data stick. Liang Wei's backup. And other things. MCC internal communications. Five years' worth. That was in the hand. Small. But heavy.

speaker: narrator
text: Dangerous information. In two directions. First, this could make FSP stronger. Second, this could create suspicion inside FSP. The same information went two ways. That was the nature of intelligence.

speaker: narrator
text: A sound from the end of the passage. Not footsteps. The ventilation fan. Sixty years old. But mixed with it was another sound. Small. But MCC buildings carried sound well. Stairs. Passages too.

speaker: narrator
text: The data stick was in hand. Kenji was there. Lena was there. Sound from the end of the passage. Three minutes. That was the time for choices to become choices.

speaker: narrator
text: Action within three minutes. That was choice on Mars. Choices made with time and choices made without. Both were choices. But different ones.

speaker: narrator
text: The data was there. Or wasn't. Kenji was there. Or wasn't. One of two outcomes. But in both of them the FSP mole problem remained. That had nothing to do with data. It had been said. Already.

speaker: narrator
text: There was an MCC person inside FSP. Someone senior. Communication patterns. In five years of data. That was what was now known. Two things were unknown. Who. And how long.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena looked at her arm. The names. One of them might have died because of the FSP mole. Park Sung-jin. Mine 7. Three repair refusals. Whether that was coincidence. Or not. Couldn't yet be known.

speaker: narrator
text: There was suspicion. That was worse to have inside than outside. Suspicion inside FSP. Suspecting each other. That was what MCC wanted. That was known. But even knowing, suspicion arose.

speaker: narrator
text: An assembly member. That narrowed it. But there were five assembly members. Five candidates. One of them. Unknowable. Patterns couldn't identify a person. They only pointed a direction.

speaker: narrator
text: Need to go to Mikhail. Need to report. The FSP mole. Communication patterns. The assembly. That was what was now known. Mikhail would react. Quietly. That was this person's way.

speaker: narrator
text: The assembly ended. Mikhail remained alone. He stood before the window. The mines were visible. The people working in those mines. Their names had made this organization. Names outlasted organizations. He knew that. That was why he had made the windows.  A dust storm was coming. But the windows were there. They would be there even when the dust came.

speaker: narrator
text: The assembly reached no conclusion. Five people. Five directions. On Mars too many directions meant going nowhere. Mikhail stood. His leg was troubled. But he stood. That was this man's way.

speaker: narrator
text: The FSP Assembly Hall. Different from the MCC boardroom. Not sealed. There were windows. The outside was visible. The mines were visible. That was intentional. FSP tried not to forget the outside. That was what the windows were.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail had made the windows. When the hall was built twenty-eight years ago. There had been opposition at first. Security concerns. But Mikhail had insisted. He said the reason was simple. We must not forget the outside. That was all. So there were windows.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail was there. His right leg was troubled. That was old. Mine accident. The leg remembered it. Today it looked worse. He was sitting. When Mikhail sat in the assembly it was a bad day.

speaker: narrator
text: Five people. Amara Okafor. Yuna Kim. Pak Seung-ho. Dr. Renata Vieira. Thomas Alder. Five sat before the table. Through the window the mines were visible. All five had connections to those mines. That was FSP.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail listened. He wasn't holding tea. Today there was no tea. That was different. There weren't many days this man was without tea. His hands were on the table. Both hands. Still. When both hands were still this man was deciding something.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena looked at Yuna. The names on the arm were visible. Yuna's father's name was there too. Hellas mining village cemetery. Metal plate. Old thing. That was in this room now. A room with names.

speaker: narrator
text: Thomas Alder. There was what Kenji had said. The FSP mole. Communication patterns. Before and after assembly meetings. The pattern pointed to an assembly member. Alder was an assembly member. Three years. From MCC. That was in this room now.

speaker: narrator
text: Three more candidates. Pak Seung-ho was a pragmatist. Dr. Renata Vieira was a medical specialist. Thomas Alder had come from MCC. That was controversial. Could an MCC person become FSP chair. That was another item on today's assembly.

speaker: narrator
text: The difference between Mikhail and Amara. Mikhail doubted. Amara saw possibility. That was the difference between twenty-eight years and eleven years. Those who had seen longer doubted more. Whether that was good or bad was unknowable.

speaker: narrator
text: An environmental alarm sounded. Assembly hall system. Dust storm warning for outer Hellas region. Scale 4. Large by Martian standards. Through the window the horizon was changing. The red was getting redder.

speaker: narrator
text: Two things at once. The chair election. Environmental crisis. Two things coming at once on Mars was normal. But these two coming the same day might not be coincidence. If MCC had known.

speaker: narrator
text: The FSP mole. What Kenji had said. Someone senior. Communication patterns. That was in this room now. One of the five candidates might be it. Or one of the representatives. Or someone around Mikhail. Unknowable.

speaker: narrator
text: Dust began hitting the windows. Scale 4 storm. The lights in the assembly hall flickered. Switching to emergency power. But the windows were there. They were there even as the dust hit.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a vote. Representatives stood. Called names. On Mars decisions were made with names. Not machines but voices. That was FSP's way. Beings with names deciding with names.

speaker: narrator
text: The dust storm hit the windows. The lights flickered. But the voices were there. Those calling names. They didn't stop. On Mars voices didn't stop. Even when the dust came.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail knew. That was this person's thing. Knowing everything while not speaking. Making tea and waiting. The way of twenty-eight years.

speaker: narrator
text: The dust storm warning continued. But the assembly ended. FSP's decision had been made. Whether it was good or bad time would tell. For now there was a decision. That was what mattered.

speaker: narrator
text: Contact went to the mining villages. Evacuation preparation. Dust storm readiness. That was what FSP did. Even after the assembly ended the work continued. On Mars work always continued.

speaker: narrator
text: Thomas Alder. From MCC. Became an FSP representative. That was possible. On Mars many things changed. People too. Affiliations too. But some things didn't change. Things of the past. Things the body remembered.

speaker: narrator
text: The assembly hall was quiet. Dust hit the windows. The storm was coming. Mikhail stood before the window. The mines were visible. Visible even through the dust. That was why the windows had been made.

speaker: narrator
text: That was Mikhail's way. Even with suspicion, he waited for evidence. That's how it had been for twenty-eight years. That was what had brought FSP to now. Being right over being fast.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn. Light came to the shipyard. Light touched the side of Gaia. Meaning Earth. The name Hagar gave. A name given by the last generation to remember Earth.  Olu's letter was inside Gaia. Or wasn't. That depended on today's outcome. But the letter had been written. On paper. By hand. In the rarest way on Mars.  Mariam was there. In the letter. In the ship. As a name.

speaker: narrator
text: The shipyard passed to MCC. Gaia was there. It would become MCC's. Where Olu's letter was could not be known. Hagar said nothing. When a quiet person said nothing it was quieter still.

speaker: narrator
text: New Athens Shipyard. Southern hemisphere of Mars. A place of strong winds. Ships were built where the wind was strong. On Mars ships were spacecraft. Things that went to space. Mars people building spacecraft was rare. Most rode company vessels. This place was different.

speaker: narrator
text: Hagar Volkov. Chief engineer of the shipyard. First generation on Mars. The last generation to remember Earth. A large and quiet person. Hands faster than words. Scars on the hands. Old ones. Old scars on Mars each had their own story.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the shipyard was a ship. Gaia. Not large. Not a warship. Closer to a freighter. But something was different. Even without seeing the blueprints it was knowable. This ship was for going far. Outside Mars. Beyond Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Hagar raised his hand. Toward the ship. The scarred hand. That was the hand that had built that ship. First generation. Seventeen years on Mars. People who remembered Earth while building Mars. This ship was the result of those seventeen years.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu Adeyemi was there. Forties. Ship designer. Writing in a corner. By hand. On paper. Writing by hand on paper on Mars was rare. Digital was easier. But this person was writing by hand. That had a reason.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu and Mariam. Two people who designed Gaia. One year. That had been their wedding fund. Hagar said later. They had built Gaia with the money they had saved to get married. Whether everyone knew that wasn't certain. Olu and Mariam had known.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu was writing the letter. To Mariam. A letter that couldn't be sent. But he was writing. His hand moved over the paper. It didn't stop. He was someone without stopping. That was the person who had built this ship.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC escort vessels were near the shipyard. Two of them. Maintaining a legal distance. But there was something visible at legal distance. MCC always pressured through legal means. That was the most frightening kind of pressure.

speaker: narrator
text: Gaia's completion rate was 87%. Hagar said. Two more weeks were needed. MCC would wait two weeks. Or wouldn't. That was what was unknowable now.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena went inside the shipyard. The fast person got faster. Checking something. The ship. Connections. Systems. That was Lena's way. Seeing fast. Deciding fast.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu was writing the letter. In the corner. By hand. On paper. MCC escorts were there. Two ships. Thirty-six minutes. That was in this shipyard now. The letter. The ship. Time. They were together.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu folded the letter. Stood. Looked at Hagar. Those eyes said. Ready. Olu was a ship designer. Not a fighter. But this ship was his. Mariam's too. That had made him stand.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu's letter was folded. In his pocket. Written with the places Gaia would go. Written with the things Mariam had wanted to see. That was together with Gaia. The letter was with the ship. That was everything in this shipyard today.

speaker: narrator
text: Thirty-six minutes began. The shipyard moved. Hagar's hands. Scarred hands. They directed. People followed. The shipyard moved as if already rehearsed. These people had been waiting for this. For a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena worked on the cooling circuits. Fast hands. Things learned in the mines. The systems were different but the principles were the same. Pressure. Flow. Temperature. Those were the same. Things learned on Mars could be used anywhere on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Olu unfolded the blueprints. He knew Gaia's weak points. He was the designer. He went to guard the weak points. The letter was in his pocket. That was everything for this person today.

speaker: narrator
text: Gaia was there. 87%. Or more. Or complete. Depending. But Gaia was there. Built with Olu and Mariam's wedding fund. It was there regardless of which way.

speaker: narrator
text: Mariam had been gone for six months. Mining accident. That marriage could happen twice. But there was no marriage. The spacecraft was complete. That was there now. Gaia. Meaning Earth. The name Hagar gave.

speaker: narrator
text: The letter was inside Gaia. Beside the navigation computer. Written with the places Gaia would go. The things Mariam had wanted to see. Outside Mars. Far places. Things without names. The letter would go there. Together with Gaia.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn. Light came to the shipyard. Light touched the side of Gaia. Meaning Earth. The name Hagar gave. A name given by the last generation to remember Earth. On Mars those who remembered Earth were diminishing. But the name remained. Names outlived those who remembered.

speaker: narrator
text: What the first generation remembered the second didn't. That was generation. The Earth that Hagar remembered. Yuna and Lena didn't remember it. But Gaia was there. The name was there. Memory remained as a name.

speaker: narrator
text: Descending from Olympus Rev. Hale called the names.

speaker: narrator
text: Alone. Inside the mask.

speaker: narrator
text: Kim Yong-jin. Mariam Adeyemi. The three of Sector 7.

speaker: narrator
text: The names below. The names not yet written.

speaker: narrator
text: The Martian sky was red. It always was.

speaker: narrator
text: But descending while calling names the red sky looked different.

speaker: narrator
text: That was the effect of prayer.

speaker: narrator
text: The agreement collapsed.

speaker: narrator
text: After the assassination attempt distrust remained.

speaker: narrator
text: Three factions looked at each other. With suspicion.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale descended.

speaker: narrator
text: Praying. As when he had climbed.

speaker: narrator
text: The names still unrecorded. But the prayer continued.

speaker: narrator
text: If prayer stopped that would be the real end.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Elias Hale prayed while ascending.

speaker: narrator
text: Prayer was not words. It was breath.

speaker: narrator
text: The breath of climbing Olympus. Inside the mask.

speaker: narrator
text: Each breath a prayer. Prayer on Mars was like that.

speaker: narrator
text: The act of breathing itself had to be a choice.

speaker: narrator
text: Olympus. The tallest mountain in the solar system.

speaker: narrator
text: West of the Martian equator. 21 kilometers high. Three times Everest.

speaker: narrator
text: The summit sat above most of the Martian atmosphere. Almost.

speaker: narrator
text: It had taken three days to reach here.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC escort. FSP delegation. CV envoy.

speaker: narrator
text: Three factions walked the same road for the first time.

speaker: narrator
text: The summit station was small. One dome. Three rooms.

speaker: narrator
text: It had been a science outpost ten years ago. Now nobody lived there.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone had brought a table and chairs.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail had come up himself to set it up, they said. That sounded right.

speaker: narrator
text: On the table was one sheet of paper and one pen.

speaker: narrator
text: Whether for signing or for notes. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale knew why he was here.

speaker: narrator
text: Not a negotiator. A minister.

speaker: narrator
text: His congregation was miners. He held service at the tunnel entrance.

speaker: narrator
text: When they died he called their names.

speaker: narrator
text: Not many could conduct a funeral on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: So he had come. That was all.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena was beside him. The player was there. Amara was there.

speaker: narrator
text: FSP delegation. Five people.

speaker: narrator
text: There were others too. Bodyguards. Aides.

speaker: narrator
text: Fifteen people inside the station.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale looked at them one by one.

speaker: narrator
text: He wanted to know their names. That was his habit.

speaker: narrator
text: The room went quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss looked at Rev. Hale.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace placed her hand on the tool belt. Didn't grip it. Just placed it.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena uncrossed her arms.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale took out paper. Folded.

speaker: narrator
text: Old paper. Folded many times. Worn with handling.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss set down her tea. First time.

speaker: narrator
text: She hadn't drunk it. But she had set it down.

speaker: narrator
text: That meant something.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace spoke.

speaker: narrator
text: A sound from outside.

speaker: narrator
text: Not wind. The summit of Olympus had no wind. Too thin an atmosphere.

speaker: narrator
text: Footsteps.

speaker: narrator
text: One bodyguard ran in.

speaker: narrator
text: The room froze.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss and Cinder Grace looked at each other.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena looked at the player.

speaker: narrator
text: Amara moved to stand by the door.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale folded the paper. Quietly.

speaker: narrator
text: There were moments that required prayer. This was one.

speaker: narrator
text: Pilgrim Arms had a target.

speaker: narrator
text: Not just one.

speaker: narrator
text: Five people in the summit station. The key figures of the summit.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale. Chen Weiss. Cinder Grace. Lena. The player.

speaker: narrator
text: Three guards to protect them. Four assassins.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone could be sacrificed. That was the calculation.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside the station. The rocky terrain of Olympus summit.

speaker: narrator
text: Almost no air. Thirty seconds without a mask.

speaker: narrator
text: Four Pilgrim Arms assassins came from the west.

speaker: narrator
text: Their equipment was perfect. Trained for low-gravity combat.

speaker: narrator
text: But Amara and the player had ascended Olympus first.

speaker: narrator
text: They knew the terrain.

speaker: narrator
text: The battle at Olympus summit had no sound.

speaker: narrator
text: The atmosphere too thin to carry gunshots.

speaker: narrator
text: A silent battle. It looked like shadows moving.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the station Rev. Hale watched it through the window.

speaker: narrator
text: He prayed. Without names. There were assassins whose names he didn't know.

speaker: narrator
text: They too were someone's names.

speaker: narrator
text: Sound from outside the window.

speaker: narrator
text: Not the silent battle. The sound of something breaking.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale looked through the window.

speaker: narrator
text: Amara was down.

speaker: narrator
text: Getting up. Not injured.

speaker: narrator
text: Two assassins were down. Not getting up.

speaker: narrator
text: The battle ended.

speaker: narrator
text: Three of four assassins subdued. One escaped.

speaker: narrator
text: The player and Cinder Grace returned to the station.

speaker: narrator
text: Amara had a wound on her left arm. Not deep.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena saw it and said nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: That was Lena's way. Silence when she saw a wound.

speaker: narrator
text: Five people sat at the table again.

speaker: narrator
text: They had just been fighting assassins.

speaker: narrator
text: But at the table they were negotiators.

speaker: narrator
text: The Martian way. Continue as long as you're alive.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale unfolded the paper again.

speaker: narrator
text: There were names.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale was not a negotiator.

speaker: narrator
text: But he knew how people opened their hearts.

speaker: narrator
text: At funerals. At deathbeds. When children were born.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a common thread. Names.

speaker: narrator
text: When you called someone's name people changed.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss had a name. Cinder Grace too. That was where to start.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace looked at Rev. Hale.

speaker: narrator
text: For a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: Then she lowered her hand from the tool belt.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale saw that.

speaker: narrator
text: A small thing. But small things made tables.

speaker: narrator
text: Negotiations proceeded. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
text: Three factions looked in the same direction.

speaker: narrator
text: Not completely. But it was a first.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale looked at the paper on the table.

speaker: narrator
text: A pen was beside it.

speaker: narrator
text: Names could be written.

speaker: narrator
text: The door opened.

speaker: narrator
text: One subdued Pilgrim Arms assassin was dragged in.

speaker: narrator
text: Amara was holding the arm. With her injured arm.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale stood.

speaker: narrator
text: He walked first toward the assassin.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace watched that.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss watched that.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena watched that.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale wrote Ramos on the paper.

speaker: narrator
text: An assassin's name and negotiators' names on the same paper.

speaker: narrator
text: A first on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Talon Group. A name emerged.

speaker: narrator
text: Where there was a name there was existence.

speaker: narrator
text: What existed could be held accountable.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale wrote that name too.

speaker: narrator
text: Names accumulated on the paper.

speaker: narrator
text: The dead. The living. Those who had no names. Those now speaking their names.

speaker: narrator
text: The agreement took shape.

speaker: narrator
text: Each of the three factions didn't get everything they wanted.

speaker: narrator
text: But together they made one thing they all wanted.

speaker: narrator
text: A first in Mars history.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale looked at the window. The sky above Olympus summit.

speaker: narrator
text: Red. As always.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail contacted them. By radio.

speaker: narrator
text: He was below the station. Thirty kilometers.

speaker: narrator
text: He would be drinking tea.

speaker: narrator
text: Two cups. Right hand supporting the left.

speaker: narrator
text: But there was still something unfinished.

speaker: narrator
text: One escaped assassin.

speaker: narrator
text: Talon Group.

text: And an internal traitor.

speaker: narrator
