text: Three lines. As Rev. Hale had wanted.

speaker: narrator
text: First: Every Mars worker is recorded by name.

speaker: narrator
text: Second: Labor accidents are made public.

speaker: narrator
text: Third: Names cannot be erased.

speaker: narrator
text: Signed by Chen Weiss. Cinder Grace. Lena. The player. Rev. Hale.

speaker: narrator
text: And Ramos. The assassin's signature was there too.

speaker: narrator
text: That was Rev. Hale's insistence.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale prayed.

speaker: narrator
text: He didn't remove the mask.

speaker: narrator
text: He prayed inside the mask. With breath.

speaker: narrator
text: Kim Yong-jin. Mariam Adeyemi. The three of Sector 7.

speaker: narrator
text: The twenty of Zone C. The forty-two of Hellas. The nameless ones of Zone 12.

speaker: narrator
text: Now they would be recorded.

speaker: narrator
text: 2087. Year 17 of Mars settlement. New Athens — free settlement in Hellas Basin. Population 4,200. A town built by hand, not by a corporation.

speaker: narrator
text: Nine months from Earth departure. Three days after Mars atmospheric entry. From above Hellas Basin the surface was visible for the first time. Red. Redder than expected. Not like the photos.

speaker: narrator
text: You had just arrived. One sheet of paper with a green FSP stamp. That was all that proved you belonged here.

speaker: narrator
text: People were at the landing pad. Most were miners. Rough hands. Eyes were different. Eyes not seen on Earth. The eyes of someone who had endured a long time. But there was light. Light not yet extinguished.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas labor district. Too narrow to call a village. Too human-smelling to call a base. Made by the first Mars generation. Added to by the next. And the one after. Seventeen years of layers.

speaker: narrator
text: Names were on the walls. Written in chalk. Miners' names. Dates. Some were old. Some were new. Chalk was weak. But they were there.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena Torres. A tattoo on the left arm. Names. Wrist to shoulder. What it was wasn't yet known. But that it was important was known. People engrave important things on their bodies.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a corridor. Narrow. Leading inward. Lena walked ahead. A fast person. Fast walk, fast talk, fast judgment. Many such people in this village. On Mars being slow was expensive.

speaker: narrator
text: A room. Small. One window. Through the window Mars was visible. Red plains. Beyond that something was there. A mine. Lights still on. Night shift.

speaker: narrator
text: The sound of tea being made. From inside the room. And there was that person. Someone standing with their back turned. Shoulders not wide. Not tall. But that back was the largest thing in the room.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail Anders. The man who made FSP. Twenty-eight years ago. A man who had been a miner. That was in both hands. The right hand cradled the left. The way he poured tea. That was this man's way.

speaker: narrator
text: Tea was poured. Two cups. One came forward. With both hands. It was received. Still hot. Hot things on Mars didn't last. It was right to receive. To receive now.

speaker: narrator
text: Lena picked up her cup. One hand. Drank quickly. That was her way. Mikhail held his cup with both hands. Looked at it long. That was his way. Two ways in the same room.

speaker: narrator
text: The village was walked. Night. The Martian night. Many stars. Because the atmosphere was thin. Clearer than Earth. Below that the village. Lights. Coming from windows. People were living.

speaker: narrator
text: A sound. A child's voice. Laughter. A child laughing on Mars. That was strangely surprising. Mars had become a place where children grew up. Seventeen years had made it so.

speaker: narrator
text: The names on the wall were looked at again. Chalk. Dates. Some names had a star mark beside them. What that was wasn't known. Whether they were names of the dead. Of those who had left. Or something else.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine was visible. Lights still on. Night shift. On Mars mines didn't stop. People took turns inside them. That was why this village existed.

speaker: narrator
text: Yuna Kim. Twenty-one years old. Born on Mars. Mars 1.5 generation. What the first generation made and the next received. Children who had grown up. The newest and oldest things in this village.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn came. The Martian dawn. The sun rose slowly. Slower than Earth. The sky mixed red and yellow. First time seeing it. But not strange. There were moments when unfamiliar things felt natural. This was one.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail was outside at dawn. Alone. Holding tea. With both hands. Seen through a window. He was looking toward the mines. No words. That was this man's dawn.

speaker: narrator
text: Learned later. Mikhail's right leg. Mining accident. Old thing. It hurt more when the weather was bad. Bad weather days on Mars were many. But it was never seen mentioned. Nor stopping the tea making.

speaker: narrator
text: The village woke. People came out. Each had work. Those going to the mines. Those bringing out children. Those making food. Those repairing things. Everyone had rough hands. Everyone moved with familiarity.

speaker: narrator
text: Amara Okafor came. The person who had been unreachable. The reason for coming to Mars, half of it. She was waiting. Standing as if she had been waiting a long time and it was nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: Amara Okafor. FSP representative. From southern Hellas. A political person. But also an idealist. Both in one person. Whether that was possible on Mars wasn't known. Here it would be learned.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine was visible. The dawn shift started. People went inside. Someone waving. Someone nodding. Someone not looking back. Each their own way. The way of going inside.

speaker: narrator
text: Mikhail drank tea. Holding the cup with both hands. Looking at the mine. Finished it. Set the cup down. With the right hand. Looked at it a moment. The empty cup. Then began preparing the next cup.

speaker: narrator
text: The tea was warm. For the first time. This village felt like it could be home. If home is possible on this planet.  The mine had lights. Names were on the wall. Children were laughing. Mikhail was pouring tea with both hands.  That was FSP.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars. Red. Always red. Not the observer's first sight. But the first time. Feet touching ground. The surface of Mars. Pressure mask. Oxygen. Numbers. The observer didn't look at numbers. Looked at other things.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central. There were people. People going in. People coming out. People standing. People moving. The observer stopped. Only the observer had stopped. That was this person's nature. Stopping.

speaker: narrator
text: The MCC building was there. Different from before. The observer had seen photos. Before arriving on Mars. Photos and now were different. Whether the building had grown taller or shorter was unknown. But it was different. The people were different. The faces of the people were different.

speaker: narrator
text: The faces were tired. Or vigilant. Or both. Tiredness and vigilance made the same expression. Eyes narrowed. Mouths closed. Shoulders lowered. That was the expression of Mars people. Or the expression of Mars people in this time.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone looked at the observer. While passing. These people didn't stop. Stopping on Mars was a luxury. That gaze said the observer had stopped. A stranger. Someone who didn't know Mars. The observer saw that gaze. That too was a record.

speaker: narrator
text: Next to the MCC building was another building. An old one. Older than the MCC building. In front of it people stood in a line. Waiting for something. Rations or permits or news. The observer looked at that line. It was a long line.

speaker: narrator
text: In the line there was a child. Next to an adult. There were children on Mars. That was a first sight. Not in the photos. The child looked at the Martian soil. The adult looked forward. The child and adult saw the same thing differently. That too was Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: On the outer wall of Hellas Central there was something. Not clearly visible. The observer moved closer. A handprint. Old. Red soil embedded. Someone had leaned on this wall. The reason was unknown. But a hand had been there. The size of the hand. It was a small hand.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood next to the handprint. Raised their own hand. Didn't match. Someone else's. Long ago this hand had been on this wall. Where that person was now was unknown. Only the wall remained. Only the handprint remained.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine exterior was visible. From Hellas Central. Far away. There were smokestacks. No smoke. Smokestacks without smoke were different. Different from operating ones. Something had changed. Or was changing. The observer looked in that direction.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine exterior. Equipment. Things not in use. Things parked. They received the dust. Martian dust. Red. The equipment didn't rust. No air. But dust accumulated. If not used dust accumulated. That was the time of this equipment.

speaker: narrator
text: There were miners. At the mine entrance. Miners not going inside. Sitting. Standing. Some were talking. Some were not talking. Their eyes faced the entrance. But they didn't enter. There was some reason.

speaker: narrator
text: Two miners spoke in low voices. The observer heard. Not all of it. Fragments. Accident. Compensation. Numbers. A name. A name was audible. The observer didn't know it. But it was a name. On Mars there were many names. Some remembered. Some forgotten.

speaker: narrator
text: Next to the mine entrance there was a board. A notice of some kind. The observer read it. MCC logo. Date. Numbers. Legal terms. Below that someone had written by hand. A pen. In small writing. The observer bent down. The writing looked like it might be erased. But it was still there.

speaker: narrator
text: The writing was names. Three. Four. Five. Whether that was all was unknown. The space below the notice was small. The names were beneath MCC legal terms. The legal terms were large. The names were small. But the names were there. That they existed was what mattered.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood. The miners were still in front of the entrance. Not going in. The observer could have asked the reason. But didn't ask. Asking was intervention. Intervention was not the observer's work. That was this person's way.

speaker: narrator
text: A mining village. Empty. Not entirely. But many houses were empty. Doors were open. Doors with nothing inside. The observer walked. Walked through alleys. Footsteps sounded. No other footsteps. There was no way to know that this village had once been full of people. But it could be known. The way of being empty was different.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside a house there were objects. Some houses. Things left behind by those who left. A cup. A shoe. A photograph. There was a photograph. The observer didn't go inside. Only looked from the doorway. What that photograph showed couldn't be known. But it had been someone's.

speaker: narrator
text: In the center of the village was an open space. Something like a gathering place. There was a table. A broken one. Chairs too. In one corner there were traces of a fire. Ash. Recent and old mixed. People had come here recently too. To an empty village. To burn fires.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer crouched in front of that ash. Didn't touch it with fingers. Only looked. The ash was gray. Gray ash on red Martian soil. The colors were different. That fire had been there the color said. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: At the end of the village there were traces of an explosion. An old one. The wall was charred black. The observer walked in that direction. Where the explosion had come from. Whether from inside or outside. Unknown. But it was there. There were traces. Things not yet cleaned up.

speaker: narrator
text: On the charred wall there were handprints. Multiple handprints. Those of people who had escaped. They had leaned on the wall to get out. Those handprints all faced the same direction. The exit direction. All had tried to get out alive. Whether they got out alive was unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a person cleaning. One person. An old person. Looked at the observer. Didn't speak. The observer didn't speak either. The old person swept ash with a broom. Old ash. How long they had been sweeping was unknown. How long they would sweep was also unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: The outskirts of Zone 4. A closed zone. There was a sign. MCC logo. No entry. The observer stopped. Looked at the sign. Behind the sign there was something. Building rubble. Or what had been a building. The entire zone was blocked.

speaker: narrator
text: Next to the sign there was a small stone marker. Not erected by MCC. Erected by someone. Names were carved in the stone. The observer approached. Tried to read the names. Couldn't read them. The writing had been erased. Whether deliberately erased. Or erased by time. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: The names on the marker couldn't be read. But the marker was there. Someone had erected it. There was someone who wanted to remember names. There was also someone who wanted to erase names. The marker was between them. Between memory and oblivion. The marker was winning. For now.

speaker: narrator
text: Next to the marker there were flowers. No flowers on Mars. They had been brought. Someone had brought them from Earth. Or grown them on Mars. They were dried. Dead. But they had been brought. For these names. For names that couldn't be read.

speaker: narrator
text: The trace of an explosion was visible in the distance. An old one. Thirty years at least or more. Explosion traces on Mars didn't disappear. No air. No rain. Traces remained as they were. On Earth traces were erased after thirty years. Not on Mars. On Mars traces lasted long.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer looked in that direction. Looked for a long time. Even someone who didn't know what had been there could know that something had been there. That was the nature of Mars traces. They didn't disappear. So Mars was a place with many memories. A place with memories even when no one remembered.

speaker: narrator
text: Night. The labor district. There were lights. Windows. Small lights. People were there. Inside the windows. The observer watched from outside. People inside windows. The observer outside windows. One pane of glass was the difference. But the glass was there.

speaker: narrator
text: In one window there were shadows. Two people. They were talking. No sound was audible. Only shadows were visible. The shadows moved. One person raised a hand. Lowered it. The other watched. That was conversation. The content was unknown. Only that conversation existed was known.

speaker: narrator
text: In the alley a person sat alone. Leaning against a wall. Knees raised. Doing nothing. The observer passed by. That person looked up. Looked down. The observer passed. It was brief. But those eyes were there. The eyes were seen. What the eyes were saying was unknown. But the eyes were saying something.

speaker: narrator
text: In the center of the labor district there was a bulletin board. Flyers were posted. MCC notices. On top of them other things. Handwritten things. Small things. The observer read. Jobs. Missing persons. Names. Meetings. They were mixed. Each person's need was posted there.

speaker: narrator
text: One missing person flyer. There was a photo. A person. A name. A date. Contact information. The observer looked at it. Didn't know where this person was. No way to know. But someone was looking for this person. Someone was searching. That existed.

speaker: narrator
text: From high up in Hellas Central. The observer had ascended. Below was visible. All of it. MCC building. Mining village. Labor district. Mine. Zone 4. They were all in the same place. On the same red surface. Different things on the same surface.

speaker: narrator
text: Other routes were here. As traces. In one route MCC had won. In one route FSP had won. In one route CV had won. But here was different. Here nothing had won. Everything remained. As traces.

speaker: narrator
text: First night on Mars. The observer stood in front of the outer wall of Hellas Central. Where the handprint had been. A small handprint. A marker with unreadable names. An old person cleaning. A missing person flyer. All of those were in one day. The first day. That was Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer watched. That was why this person had come here. Watching. There were things seen on the first day. A handprint. Names. Ash. Explosion traces. Gazes. Those were traces. Traces of other routes. Traces of where this Mars had come from. The observer had to see more. Mars was there. That was everything.

speaker: narrator
text: The northern Hellas. The wilderness. Where few people were. The observer walked. The surface was uneven. The surface of Mars was always uneven. But this area was different. People had dug. Machines had dug. Those traces were on the surface.

speaker: narrator
text: A mining village. There was chalk. On the wall. Names. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. The observer looked. Who wrote them. Why they wrote. When they wrote. Those things were on the wall. Written by people who knew chalk was weak. So they wrote more.

speaker: narrator
text: Below the name Kim Yong-jin there was a date. An old date. Below that other names. Dates. Some names had no date. Whether there had been no time to write dates. Or dates hadn't mattered. There were ones with only names. Only names were enough.

speaker: narrator
text: The names were different sizes. Large names. Small names. Names written by trembling hands. Names written quickly. The names each spoke of their circumstances. Those with space wrote large. Those without time wrote small. Those who were afraid wrote with trembling hands. All of those were on the same wall.

speaker: narrator
text: Near the bottom of the wall there was one name. Low down. It looked like a child had written it. Or like it had been written while sitting. The name couldn't be read. The handwriting was rough. But it was known to be a name. It had tried to say it had been here. The name said that.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer read the names. Couldn't read all of them. Some had been erased. Erased by time. Or someone had erased them. Or part of the wall had broken. But there were names that could be read. The observer read those. Without sound. Not with the mouth. Only with eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: Sandstone Junction. Where three directions split. There was much sand. Martian sand was red. This sand was also red. But there were footprints here. Many. In many directions. Many people had passed through this junction.

speaker: narrator
text: The footprints were each different. Different sizes. Different depths. Footprints of heavy people. Footprints of fast people. Footprints of those who had run. Footprints of those who had walked. Those were in the sand. Sand was erasable. But they were still there.

speaker: narrator
text: In each of the three directions there were traces of flags. Marks of flags planted and pulled. Small holes. The MCC direction. The FSP direction. The CV direction. Three flags had been here. Not now. They had been planted and pulled. The order was unknown. But it was known all three had been here.

speaker: narrator
text: Three holes. The same size. The same depth. The same diameter flag poles. Three factions had used the same flag poles. Or had the same size will. The observer looked at the holes. The holes were empty. Empty holes said more than full ones.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood in the center of the junction. Three directions were visible. In the MCC direction there was dust. In the FSP direction there were footprints. In the CV direction there was nothing. Three directions each had different things. The observer watched from the middle. The middle was the place that saw the most.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine shaft entrance. The observer entered. Light decreased. Gloves. Hard hat. Equipment. These should have been there. The observer didn't have them. But entered. Observation could be done without equipment. Or the observer believed so.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the shaft there were tools. Abandoned things. A drill. Surveying equipment. Metal containers. Those leaned against the shaft walls or lay on the floor. Things used and discarded. Or things left behind. There was a difference. Discarded meant value was gone and left behind meant intending to return.

speaker: narrator
text: On one container a name was carved. An owner. The observer read it. An unknown name. But a name was there. This container had been this person's. The person whose whereabouts were now unknown. Only the container was here. The container stood in for that person.

speaker: narrator
text: On the shaft walls there were scratch marks. Traces of searching for ore. But there were other things too. Stars. Dates. Simple drawings. Someone had waited here. While waiting for ore. While waiting in the shaft. Drew something. Those were on the walls.

speaker: narrator
text: Among the drawings there was a person. A stick figure. A simple one. Next to it was a smaller stick figure. Two people. An adult and a child. In a Martian mine shaft there was a drawing of an adult and a child. What the person who drew it had been thinking was unknown. But they had drawn it. There.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC archive sublevel. The observer entered. Entered without permission. That was not the observer's way. But entered. There were cases where watching crossed a boundary without intervention. This was the first time the observer had crossed a boundary.

speaker: narrator
text: There were documents. Old ones. Early Mars. When MCC was founded. The observer didn't look at them. Didn't want to know their content. But there was something else. Fast footprints. Recent. Two people. One of them had black hands. Ore dust. A miner's footprints in the archive.

speaker: narrator
text: A drawer was open. Empty. Something had been there and was gone. Someone had taken it. Inside the drawer there was dust. A rectangular mark without dust. Where a chip had been. How long it had been there was unknown but a chip had been there. Not now.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer looked at the empty drawer. For a long time. Didn't know where the chip had gone. Didn't know who had taken it. There were miners' footprints. Two people. The chip was gone. Whether those were connected was unknown. The observer didn't connect them. Looked at traces. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC Sector 12 ruins. This too was closed. For a different reason. Not an explosion. It had become unused. MCC had decided not to use it. Deciding not to use something and something being abandoned were different. But the result was the same. No one was there.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the building there was equipment. Equipment with MCC logos. Things not properly cleaned out. Things that could be used. But they were here. Usable equipment was here unused. What that said was unknown. Budget. Plans. People. One of those or all of them.

speaker: narrator
text: In one room there was a photo. Posted on the wall. Not posted by MCC. Posted by someone later. In the photo there were people. A group photo. People wearing helmets. Miners. Or engineers. The observer looked. Didn't know who they were. The photo was here.

speaker: narrator
text: Below the photo there was a note. A small one. The observer read it. A date. Names. And a short sentence. Zone 12. We were here. That was everything the note said. It was trying to say that they had been here. Nothing more or less.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside Erebus crater. The observer had come. Come from far away. Coming here was not easy. But came. Because it was known there were traces here. Erebus had traces. Old ones.

speaker: narrator
text: Ash from barrel fires. Old. New. Thirty years' worth were mixed. People had lived in this base. They burned fires. After fires went out ash remained. Ash was a trace too. Trace that fire had been there.

speaker: narrator
text: The ashes were layered. Old ones below. New on top. That was time. The layers of ash spoke of time. Someone had burned fires here for a long time. Whether the same person or different people was unknown. The reason for burning fires was also unknown. There was fire. For a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside Erebus base. A small base. Not an MCC base. Something someone had built. Built by one person. The observer looked. There were characteristics of a base built by one person. Only necessities. Nothing unnecessary. Built by someone who knew what was necessary.

speaker: narrator
text: On the table there was a photo. One. Old. Multiple people. Miners. That photo was on the table. No dust on it. Someone looked at it often. Or it had been wiped recently. The photo had been here a long time. The person who was here with the photo had looked at it for a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: Kepler Crater. Footprints. Equipment marks. Analysis tools. Thirty years of traces were here. Liang Wei. The person who came alone. Who was alone for thirty years. Those traces were layered. Thirty-year layers.

speaker: narrator
text: There was one set of footprints. One person's footprints. For thirty years walked in many directions. All those footprints were in this crater. Came alone. Walked alone. Analyzed alone. Those showed as footprints. That it had been alone the footprints said.

speaker: narrator
text: In the center of the crater there was a collection point. There were markings. Numbers. Dates. Layered. The observer looked. Dates spanning thirty years. The same person every year. Every month. Some things every day. Had recorded. Recorded for thirty years to find out what this was. Whether it had been figured out yet was unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood at the edge of the crater. The sun was setting. Evening at Kepler Crater. Red sky. Redder crater. Thirty years of traces caught the evening light. Traces were more visible. Or looked more beautiful. The observer didn't record beauty. Only recorded traces.

speaker: narrator
text: There was an abandoned object. At the edge of the crater. An old cup. Without an MCC logo. A personal item. Must have been some miner's. Or an engineer's. The cup was there. No one had taken it. Its owner was not here. Only the cup was here.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stopped in front of the cup. Didn't pick it up. Only see traces. That was the observer's way. If an object is picked up that object moves. The trace changes. The observer must not change traces. So didn't pick it up. Looked. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: But while looking at the cup, thoughts arose. Who owned this cup. How this cup had come here. Why there was a cup at Kepler Crater. There were questions. The observer didn't ask questions. But there were questions. That was the first thing the observer had admitted. That there were questions.

speaker: narrator
text: Came back to Zone 4. The closed place. The marker. The marker with unreadable names. The observer looked again. Nothing had changed. The names were still unreadable. There were flowers. Dead flowers. But there was something different from before. There was a new flower. Someone had come. Had brought a new flower.

speaker: narrator
text: There were traces. Names. Footprints. A cup. Photos. Ash. A marker. A new flower. These were the history of Mars. History not in official records. History that existed only as traces. The observer watched them. Didn't pick up objects. Didn't connect. Watched. That was enough. For now.

speaker: narrator
text: The foothills of Olympus Mons. The observer had come. After the Three Flags conference. How long after was unknown. That didn't matter. What mattered was that a conference had been. And that the observer was now at that place.

speaker: narrator
text: Olympus was vast. The largest thing on Mars. The largest volcano in the solar system. The observer looked up. The summit wasn't visible. There were clouds. Or there was distance. Below on the foothills were traces of the conference site.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a conference site. Traces of temporary structures. Where pillars had been. Where tents had been. Marks on the ground of things placed. Marks of people who had stood. It could be known that three groups had come. Each group had come from different directions. Footprints said that.

speaker: narrator
text: Where flags had been. Three. Holes. The same kind of holes as seen at Sandstone. But larger. Larger flags had been here. More significant. Three holes formed a triangle. The center of the triangle was empty.

speaker: narrator
text: The center of the triangle. The observer stood there. Three holes were around. MCC. FSP. CV. Three directions. The observer was in the middle. The fourth position. The place without a flag. But someone could stand there. The observer was standing there now. Without any flag.

speaker: narrator
text: There was something there. The observer looked down at their feet. It was blood-colored. A bloodstain. Old. The red surface of Mars hid blood. But the color was different. A little darker. There was blood. Someone had died here.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer crouched. Looked at the bloodstain. Not a small amount. May not have been instant death. Or it may have been. The amount didn't tell. What could be known was that someone had bled here. At the conference site. At the center of the triangle.

speaker: narrator
text: There were other things around. Glass fragments. Metal fragments. Things that had broken. The conference had not been peaceful. Or something had happened after the conference ended. Three factions had left this place. Before that something had occurred.

speaker: narrator
text: The footprints had changed. Before and after the conference were different. The incoming footprints had come slowly. The outgoing footprints were fast. Some were disordered. Had run or fought. Directions were different. Not all had gone the same way. They had scattered.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stepped back from the conference site. To see the whole. Wider. At the edge of the conference site there was something. Small. The observer approached. It was a fragment of a flag. A piece of colored cloth. Which of the three factions it belonged to couldn't be determined. The piece was too small.

speaker: narrator
text: Next to the piece there was another piece. A different color. Another piece. Another color. Three pieces. Flag pieces of the three factions. Those were in the same place. Torn. There had been anger. Or an accident. Or intent. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: But there was a fourth piece. The observer found it. A little away from where the three were. A different color. Not the color of the three factions. What color exactly wasn't clear. Old. Hit by Martian dust. But it was different. A fourth color.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer looked at the fourth piece. Didn't pick it up. Looked. Who had brought this. Someone who was not among the three factions had come here. There had been a person who brought a fourth flag. Or someone who had tried to bring one. That person had bled at the center of the triangle. Or not. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood. Looked up at Olympus. The summit was still not visible. This mountain had watched the conference. Below it. The mountain was old. Older than Mars. Geologically. There had been a conference. There had been blood. There had been a fourth piece. The mountain had seen them. Didn't speak.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun was setting. Evening at the foothills of Olympus. Shadows grew long. The shadow of the conference site also grew long. Bloodstain. Flag marks. The fourth piece. The shadows of those grew long. As the sun set the shadows of traces grew long. That was Mars evening.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer sat. Sat for a long time. Looked at the conference site. Three holes. Bloodstain at the center. Scattered footprints. Torn flag pieces. The fourth piece. What these were saying couldn't be known. Yet. But these things existed. That was known.

speaker: narrator
text: In the evening light the conference site looked different. Different from daytime. Shadows made the traces clearer. Or made them more ambiguous. The same thing looked different depending on the light. The observer knew that. Traces were different depending on when they were seen. That was the nature of traces.

speaker: narrator
text: There were things the observer knew about the conference. Three factions had come. Had tried to reach agreement. Whether agreement was reached or not. Unknown. But traces said something had happened after the agreement. The bloodstain said that. Agreement was not peace. On Mars agreement was never peace.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer walked again. Walked around the conference site. Slowly. Drawing a large circle. To see if things further away were visible. Whether there were traces away from the conference site. The observer searched. There were.

speaker: narrator
text: Ten meters away were lone footprints. Unlike the three groups' footprints they had come alone. Had a size. Adult. Neither fast nor slow. Whether the person of these footprints had joined the conference was unknown. The footprints headed toward the conference site. But whether they had arrived was unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: The footprints stopped. In the middle. On the way to the conference site. Where they stopped there were knee marks. Had fallen. Or had sat. And then went in a different direction. The footprints changed. Became heavier. Were dragged. Had been injured. Or tired. Or decided not to arrive.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer tried to follow those footprints. Stopped. Not the observer's way. Seeing traces. Following traces. Those two were different. Following would lead to finding the end. Finding the end would lead to intervention. The observer didn't intervene. That was this person's condition.

speaker: narrator
text: But the observer thought about whether the person of those footprints was the one who had brought the fourth flag. Tried not to think. But thought came. This person had come with the fourth flag. Stopped in the middle. Went another direction. Couldn't take the fourth flag. That piece remained here.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer came back to the center of the triangle. Bloodstain. The fourth piece. Whether two things were the same person's or different people's was unknown. Couldn't be known. To know would require following. Following was not the observer's way. So it was unknown. That was the price of the observer's way.

speaker: narrator
text: Why had a fourth flag been needed. The observer thought. There were three flags. Mars could be divided with those. Three factions could divide Mars. But someone had tried to bring a fourth. Something other than the three factions. What was it.

speaker: narrator
text: The answer was unknown. That was the observer's way. Not knowing the answer. Seeing traces. Waiting until traces give an answer. Or seeing traces even without an answer. That was what the observer could do. That was all that could be done.

speaker: narrator
text: Night passed. The observer had spent the night here. Near the conference site. That was a first. Spending the night near traces. Wanted to see if traces looked different at night. They did. At night traces were quiet. In the day traces talked a lot. At night traces only existed.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn light came. Dawn at the foothills of Olympus. Red light came first. Then other lights came. The conference site became visible again. In the dawn light. Looked different. Different from evening and from day. The same traces were different three times. That was the nature of traces.

speaker: narrator
text: In the dawn light the fourth piece looked different. The color looked different. The color that couldn't be determined yesterday. The dawn light told it. It was white. It had been a white flag. The fourth flag was white. What a white flag meant was unknown. But it was white.

speaker: narrator
text: A white flag. Surrender? Peace? Something else? The observer didn't know. White things were rare on Mars. No snow. No flowers. White things were brought. Someone had brought a white flag here. To know what that said more needed to be seen.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood. Prepared to leave the conference site. Looked one last time. Three holes. Bloodstain at center. White flag piece. Footprints. Those were here. Would be here even after the observer left. On Mars traces lasted long. No rain. Wind was weak.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer saw one more thing last. Next to the three holes there was a small stone. A stone without a mark. Whether natural or placed by someone was unknown. But it was inside the triangle of three holes. Near the center. What this was. Who had placed it. Unknown. That was everything.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stayed looking at the stone for a long time. The stone seemed to be saying something. But the words couldn't be heard. The stone didn't speak. Traces had things they said. Traces had things they didn't say. This stone was one of the things that didn't speak. But it was there.

speaker: narrator
text: Eventually the observer picked up the stone. The first time. The first time a trace had been picked up. That went against the observer's way. But picked it up. Under the stone there was something. A small thing. A metal piece. A name was carved in it. Read it. It was a name. A name the observer didn't know. But a name was there.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer placed the metal piece back under the stone. Covered it with the stone as before. Returned the trace to its original state. But the name was known. That was what had changed. The observer knew a name. What that name meant was unknown. But a name was there. That name was here.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer began descending the foothills of Olympus. Slowly. Looking back. The conference site grew distant. Traces became smaller. But didn't disappear. On Mars traces didn't disappear. Grew distant. Became smaller. But were there.

speaker: narrator
text: Descending the observer thought. The person who brought the fourth flag. A white flag. A metal piece with a name carved. A bloodstain. Whether these were connected. Whether from the same person. Or different things. Unknown. But there were thoughts. For the first time the observer had thoughts. Thoughts about connection.

speaker: narrator
text: That was dangerous. The observer knew. When beginning to connect, intervention would follow. With intervention, not an observer. But there were thoughts. Couldn't stop them. Olympus watched the observer from behind. The mountain watched. Had watched the conference. Had watched the bloodstain. Had watched the white flag. And watched the observer thinking.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stopped. Tried to stop thinking. Couldn't. When traces were seen they became a story. When they became a story they became thoughts. When they became thoughts they became connections. That was the danger of observation. For the first time the observer understood that danger. On Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Descended the foothills of Olympus. The conference site became invisible. But it was there. Three holes. A bloodstain. A white flag piece. Metal with a name. Had there been a fourth flag. The observer didn't know the answer. That was the observer's way. Not knowing the answer. But this time was different. Wanted to know the answer. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
text: Erebus Crater. The observer had come again. Not the first time. Different from the previous visit. This time there was a purpose. Coming with a purpose was not the observer's way. But came. There was a person at Erebus.

speaker: narrator
text: Watched from afar. There was a person. On the outer wall of Erebus Crater. Alone. Standing. Looking at the crater. The observer watched that person. That person didn't look at the observer. Only looked at the crater. It was Butcher.

speaker: narrator
text: Recognized Butcher. Prosthetic arm. Coat. Wide back. The age was visible in the back. Thirty years were in that back. The observer watched that back. Watched for a long time. Butcher didn't move. Looked at the crater. The observer also didn't move.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer moved closer. Without sound. That was not natural. Moving closer and moving without sound were different. Moving without sound was hiding. The observer hid. That was a first. Hiding one's own existence.

speaker: narrator
text: Twenty meters. Ten meters. Butcher still looked at the crater. Inside the crater. The site of an old mine. Where it had been thirty years ago. The observer also looked inside. Saw the same thing. Same thing as Butcher. But each saw something different.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the crater were mine traces. Old. More than thirty years. The entrance was sealed. MCC had sealed it. Sealed long ago as well. In front of the sealed entrance there was a sign. The observer read it. Danger. No entry. Date. Old date.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher tried to descend toward the sign. Stopped. Descended. Stopped again. Several times. There was something other than what that body wanted. Whether legs hurt. Or afraid. The observer didn't know. But Butcher tried to descend. Toward the sealed entrance.

speaker: narrator
text: Eventually Butcher descended. Slowly. Along the crater wall. Stood before the sealed entrance. Raised a hand. To the sealed wall. Touched it. With the hand that was not the prosthetic. It had been there. Beyond the sealed wall. Thirty years ago. It was still there now.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer watched. Didn't intervene. Butcher had to be alone. At that place. Had to do it alone. If it were known the observer was there it would change. So watched from afar. Was there but as if not. That was what the observer could do.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher murmured something. Inaudible. Only saw the lip movements. Whether a name. Or a sentence. Unknown. There were words. Those words came out in front of the sealed wall. After thirty years. After thirty years words came from this place. Where those words went was unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher stayed for a long time. The observer also stayed for a long time. Martian time passed. Martian time was different from Earth. A day was a little longer. That made Earth people age a little more on Mars. Butcher had lived thirty years on Mars. Thirty years was a little longer time than on Earth.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher lowered the hand. From the sealed wall. Turned around. Came up. Climbed out of the crater. The observer stepped back. To a place not visible. Butcher came up to the top. Looked far away. At Erebus Crater. Looked again. And walked away.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher left. The observer came out. Stood again at the crater edge. At the place Butcher had been. The observer looked at the same crater. Saw the same thing as Butcher. The sealed entrance. The old mine. The thirty-year-old thing. But it was different. The observer had no memory. Butcher did.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer descended into the crater. On the path Butcher had descended. The same path. Stood before the sealed entrance. Looked at the spot where Butcher's hand had touched. There was a handprint. In the dust. The mark of the hand that was not the prosthetic. It was there. That hand had been there. After thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood next to it. Next to the handprint. Raised their own hand. Next to Butcher's handprint. Didn't touch. Couldn't touch. The observer had no memory of this place. What was contained in that handprint couldn't be known. But the handprint was there. There.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Zone 4. The observer had come. Come from Erebus. Come after watching Butcher. Zone 4 abandoned mine. Similar here too. Sealed things. MCC signs. Old things. But here was different. Older than Erebus. Or there was more here.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside the abandoned mine there was rubble. Things that had been buildings. Things that had been buildings thirty years ago. There were walls. Partially. Walls without roofs. On the walls there were names. Not chalk. Old. Scratched. By fingernails. By something sharp.

speaker: narrator
text: There were many names. More than the chalk names. They were scratched. Deeply scratched. Forceful. Hands with fear scratched hard. Or desperation. Desperation to leave a name gave force to hands. That was visible in the names.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer read one name. Kim Yong-jin. Here. A name also in the chalk names. That name was scratched here. Thirty years old. Same name. Different tool. Same desperation. Kim Yong-jin had been here. Thirty years ago. And had left a name.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood for a long time before that name. Kim Yong-jin. Name seen in chalk. Name seen in scratches. Same name. Twice. Thirty years apart. That name had lived thirty years. Whether the person who wrote that name had lived thirty years was unknown. But the name had lived.

speaker: narrator
text: Entered the abandoned mine. The observer. Without permission. Second boundary crossing. The first was the archive. The second was here. Crossing boundaries was becoming easier. That was worrying. For the first time the observer had a worry. A worry about oneself.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the abandoned mine it was dark. There was light. The observer's light. Walls were visible. Ceiling was visible. Thirty-year-old things were visible. Supports. Cables. Equipment. They were old. Thirty years of neglect. But hadn't collapsed. The dryness of Mars had maintained things. No rot.

speaker: narrator
text: There were traces of the strike. Inside the shaft. Graffiti. Slogans. Thirty-year-old things. 'We are people'. 'This belongs to everyone'. 'Zone 4 will be remembered'. Those were on the walls. For thirty years. Because MCC hadn't come inside. Traces remained as they were.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer read those. One by one. Words from thirty years ago. Words written by striking people. They had had things they wanted. Things they feared. Things they claimed. Those were on the walls. For thirty years no one had read them. Now the observer read them.

speaker: narrator
text: Went deeper. The shaft narrowed. More old things. Older things. Things before the strike. Things from when miners worked. Mining tools. Surveying equipment. Those were things used and then stopped. Stopped suddenly.

speaker: narrator
text: Things that had stopped suddenly. Miners had been mining and stopped. There had been a strike. Or an order. Or something had been found. Something had been found. Mining tools had stopped at a specific point. That point was different. The wall was different. The color was different.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer approached that wall. The color was different. Not ore. The strata were different. A mineral. Not a common mineral. The observer couldn't tell. Not an expert. But it was different. That was what mattered. Something different was here. Deep in this shaft. Since thirty years ago.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer didn't know that it was Ancient Metal. Didn't know that name. But knew it was special. Miners had found this. Had struck. MCC had sealed it. Names had remained on walls. People had died. Everything had been because of this. Because of this different color.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood before it. For a long time. It glinted. A little. Receiving the observer's light. Not glinting but receiving light in a different way. Absorbed and released differently. That was different. There were minerals that handled light differently. This was one of those.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer raised a hand. Stopped just before touching. Touching would not be observation. Would be intervention. Lowered the hand. But watched for a long time. It was on Mars. Since thirty years ago. It was the beginning of everything. The strike. Death. Names. The sealing. Thirty years. It was here.

speaker: narrator
text: Came out of the abandoned mine. There was light. Martian light. Red. What was inside the shaft was in the eyes. In the observer's eyes. A mineral of different color. It remained in the eyes. For a long time. Even with eyes closed it was there. That was a first sight. Something containing thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer looked at the abandoned mine from outside. The sealed entrance. MCC signs. Rubble of the wall with names. A marker. A marker with unreadable names. These were together. In the same place. Traces of the event thirty years ago were in the same place. The observer stood in the middle of them.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer had seen what Butcher did at Erebus. Touching the sealed wall with a hand. Knew what that was. It was remembering what had been there. Only someone with memory could do it. The observer had no memory. So did it in a different way. Watched. That was the observer's way.

speaker: narrator
text: Leaving Zone 4 the observer looked one more time. At everything. Abandoned mine. Rubble. Signs. Marker. Flowers. Names. And the different colored mineral deep in the shaft. Those were one story. A thirty-year story. The observer knew that story. Not all of it. But knew it.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer thought. What Butcher had done at Erebus. Touching. The sealed wall. What had that been. The observer wanted to know. Could have asked Butcher. But didn't ask. That was this person's way. But wanted to know. That desire existed. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
text: It was dawn. Outside Zone 4. The observer had spent the night here. Near the abandoned mine. That was the second time. Spending a night near traces. The first was Olympus. The second was here. There was a pattern. The observer was getting closer to traces.

speaker: narrator
text: In the dawn light Zone 4 looked different. The ruins looked different. Night and day and dawn were all different. The same ruins. The observer had seen three times. The same thing differently. That had now become meaning. Not one ruin. Three ruins. Depending on time.

speaker: narrator
text: Butcher had been here thirty years ago. Or at Erebus. There was a strike. It ended. People died. Butcher survived alone. Thirty years passed. Butcher came back to Erebus. Touched the sealed wall. That was thirty years. The observer had seen that.

speaker: narrator
text: Whether the observer knew or didn't know. That was unclear. The thirty-year story. The observer was seeing that story. In pieces. In traces. Didn't know the whole. Couldn't know. But was watching. That was what the observer could do.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn grew brighter. The Zone 4 abandoned mine received light. The wall with names. The marker. The sealed entrance. Those had waited thirty years. The observer came. Watched. That was everything. For now. But it would not be everything. There was more. Had to see more. There were still things Mars had not said.

speaker: narrator
text: Was ascending. Olympus Mons. The highest place in the solar system. The observer was climbing. There was a reason. To see the whole. All of Mars. This would be the last thing the observer did. Ascending.

speaker: narrator
text: The ascent was long. The longest path on Mars. Olympus had a gentle slope. The highest in the solar system but with a gentle slope. That was Mars's paradox. The highest thing had the gentlest slope. It took a long time to ascend. The observer walked.

speaker: narrator
text: While ascending Mars looked different. Low and high were different. At low altitude individual things were seen. At high altitude the whole was visible. The reason the observer had wanted to ascend was there. Seeing the whole. Things not seen from low altitude.

speaker: narrator
text: While ascending dawn came. Dawn at Olympus. Light came from below. Light did not come from above. Came from below. That was the nature of high places. Light rising from below. The observer received that light. While ascending.

speaker: narrator
text: Below began to be visible. Mars. Red. The places the observer had come from were visible. Hellas Central. Mines. Zone 4. Erebus. Sandstone. Kepler. Those were below. The observer watched from above. For the first time. The whole.

speaker: narrator
text: The result of the MCC route was visible. Down there. There were cities. Large cities. Things MCC had built. But what the observer had seen was there. People in lines. Villages emptying. Dust-accumulated equipment outside mines. Even in the route where MCC won those things were there.

speaker: narrator
text: The result of the FSP route was visible. In another direction. There were villages. Small ones. Things FSP had built. But there too. Miners still worked. Still dangerous. Still names were written in chalk. Even in the route where FSP won those things were there.

speaker: narrator
text: The result of the CV route was visible. In yet another direction. There were bases. CV's bases. But there too. Things not yet resolved. The story from thirty years ago was still a story. Not ended. Even in the route where CV won.

speaker: narrator
text: Three routes. Three results. None of them a complete victory. The observer watched from above. Things not visible from below were visible from above. All three routes were similar. Different flags. Different names. But similar things remained. Names. Traces. Unresolved things.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars was there. Below the three routes. Mars was older than the three routes. Older than all factions. Older than all people. Mars was there. Under the blood-red sky. The three routes were on top of it. Mars had seen them. Didn't speak.

speaker: narrator
text: Reached near the summit. The observer. Could have gone higher. But stopped. What was visible from here was enough. The whole was visible. All of Mars. All three routes. Things beneath those. Names. Traces. People.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun was setting. Mars's sun. Different from Earth. Smaller. Looked colder. But it was the sun. The same sun. Earth and Mars received the same sun. From different distances. That was the same thing. Things that didn't know each other received the same thing.

speaker: narrator
text: A blood-red sky. The Martian sky. The observer had watched. Watched often. From when first arriving. But seeing it from here was different. The blood-red sky seen from the highest place. The sky was closer than seen from below. Or wider. Or both.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars was still there. Under the blood-red sky. The results of three routes were there. MCC. FSP. CV. None of them complete. But Mars was there. Still. Red. Always red. That hadn't changed. The color of Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer sat. Near the summit. Watched Mars. Watched for a long time. There were things seen from when first arriving. Handprints. Names. Ash. Footprints. A marker. A cup. Photos. Bloodstain. A white flag piece. A mineral. Butcher's hand. All of those were there. Below.

speaker: narrator
text: Were those connected. The observer thought. At first didn't connect. That was the observer's way. Only see traces. Don't connect. But now was different. Connections were visible. Lines were visible. Between traces. Those spoke of one story.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a story. Something that started thirty years ago. A mineral was discovered. People died. Names remained. Thirty years passed. Names were written again. People died again. Factions fought. A conference happened. There was blood. There was a white flag. That was the story. One story.

speaker: narrator
text: Had that story ended. Didn't know. Had seen three routes. In none of the three routes had it ended. That story. Continued in different ways. In the MCC route. In the FSP route. In the CV route. The story continued. Even if flags were different. The story was the same.

speaker: narrator
text: For the first time the observer was sad. No. Not sadness. Didn't know what it was. But there was something. While watching the things below. The things of three routes. Names. Traces. There was something. The observer didn't know the name. Of that sensation.

speaker: narrator
text: The Martian sun descended further. The sky grew redder. The blood color deepened. The observer watched. The sky. Mars. Below. Three routes. Names. Traces. Watched everything. That was why the observer had come. Watching. Watching was everything.

speaker: narrator
text: The sun set. Completely. Remembered the first night. The first night seen from Hellas Central. Lights. MCC. Labor district. Mine. Those lights were still there now. In three routes too. There were lights. That meant people were there.

speaker: narrator
text: There were people. On Mars. In all three routes. In the MCC route too. In the FSP route too. In the CV route too. People with names. People who left traces. People who burned fires. People who wrote in chalk. They were there. On Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer recorded. For the first time. Recording. On what the observer had. Not paper. An electronic device. The observer recorded for the first time. Names. Traces. Things seen. That was the first. The recording.

speaker: narrator
text: Kim Yong-jin. Wrote the name. Zone 12. Wrote. Sandstone Junction. Wrote. Erebus Crater. Wrote. Butcher's hand. White flag. Zone 4 mineral. Names. Traces. Wrote all of it. That was a record. The observer's record.

speaker: narrator
text: Thought about whether recording fit the observer's way. Did observation include recording. Unknown. But recorded. Didn't pick up traces. Didn't move traces. But recorded. Whether that was right or not. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Night passed. Near the summit. The observer had spent the night. The third time. First time was the Olympus foothills. Second was Zone 4. Third was near the summit. Spent night while ascending. That was a pattern. The higher, the more was visible.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn came. Dawn near the Olympus summit. Light came from below. Light rising from Mars. The observer received that light. There were recorded things. On the electronic device. Those existed as records. The observer's record. The fourth record.

speaker: narrator
text: In three routes there were official records. MCC records. FSP records. CV records. Those were official. The observer's record was not official. Unofficial. But it existed. There was a fourth record. Not the record of three factions. The record of names.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer looked at the record. Things written. Names. Places. Dates. Traces. Those were there. Didn't know what to do with that record. Who to give it to. Where to put it. Unknown. But it existed. The record.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars was below. The observer was above. That difference was there. Above and below. Height. But Mars was Mars. Seen from above or below. Red. Always red. That hadn't changed.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC won. In one route. But it was not a complete victory. Names remained. FSP won. In one route. But it was not a complete victory. Names remained. CV won. In one route. But it was not a complete victory. Names remained.

speaker: narrator
text: Names remained. That was common. In all three routes. Whoever won names remained. Kim Yong-jin. The Zone 12 people. Those who struck. The people from thirty years ago. Their names remained. On walls. In chalk. In scratches. As markers.

speaker: narrator
text: That was Mars. The observer understood. Not flags. Not factions. Names. What remained were names. On Mars. Names were Mars. Chalk names. Scratched names. Names on markers. Names were Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: A second sun was setting. The second sun seen near the summit. The observer watched. Mars was below. Red. The blood-red sky grew redder. Sky and Mars were the same color. That was Mars evening. An evening without boundaries. An evening where sky and ground were the same color.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer wrote the last thing in the record. Date. Location. Near the summit of Olympus Mons. And what was seen. All of Mars. Three routes. Names. Blood-red sky. That was the last record. The observer's last record. On Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Closed the record. The observer. It existed. The record. Names. Traces. Thirty years. Three routes. Those were in the record. Were inside the observer. Mars was inside the observer. For the first time. That was what had changed. Mars had entered inside the observer.

speaker: narrator
text: Would descend. The observer thought. If descending where would go. To Hellas Central. Or Zone 4. Or Erebus. Or would continue ascending Olympus. No answer. That was this person's condition. Having no direction. Being able to see everywhere. No place being a destination.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars was below. Under the blood-red sky. The results of three routes were there. None complete. There were names. There were traces. There were thirty years. Those were Mars. Not factions. Not flags. Names. Traces. Memories.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer stood. With the record. With names. With traces. Those were inside the observer. Mars was inside the observer. Where the observer would go with those. Unknown. But had them. That was a first. Having something.

speaker: narrator
text: Looked at Mars one last time. The observer. From near the Olympus summit. The whole. All of Mars. Under the blood-red sky. On top of three routes' traces. On top of names. On top of thirty years. Mars was there. Still. Red. Always red.

speaker: narrator
text: That was everything. The observer understood. Mars was everything. Names were everything. Traces were everything. Three routes were everything. Nothing was everything. Everything was everything. That was Mars. That was the last thing the observer had understood.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer did not descend.

speaker: narrator
text: What it meant that the observer did not descend. The observer didn't know. Didn't need to know. Mars was below. Names were below. The observer was above. That was enough. The observer had seen the names. The names hadn't waited for the observer. But were there. That was Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars was there. Under the blood-red sky. The observer was above. That was the last observation. Mars seen from above. Blood-red sky. Names. Traces. Three routes. Thirty years. Those were together. That was everything.

speaker: narrator
text: The observer did not descend. Mars was below. The blood-red sky was above. The observer was between them. Names were below. The record was inside the observer. That was enough. Mars was there. Had always been there. Before the observer came. After the observer left. Mars was there. Red. Always red. That was everything.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang stood at the window looking at the northern sky. The direction the storm was passing. What he was thinking was unknowable. On Mars nobody tried to know that. Everyone was busy with their own thoughts.  It was the first day.

speaker: narrator
text: The briefing room light flickered. Li Fang cleared the map. The convoy marker disappeared. When missions ended markers disappeared. New markers would appear. On Mars markers always appeared.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central. MCC headquarters. The building was enormous. Nothing on Mars was this large. It had been built sixty years ago. It had kept growing since. It never stopped.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC. Mars Colonial Corporation. No company was as honest as its name. It was unashamed of calling Mars a colony. It knew that shame didn't make money.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a line at the checkpoint. Miners. Technicians. Mercenaries. They were given numbers. When a number was called they entered. If not called they waited. Not many people on Mars didn't have to wait in line.

speaker: narrator
text: The checkpoint officer took the ID card. Scanned it. Returned it. That was all. No eye contact. They looked at the card before the person. That was how Mars worked. Cards came before people.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC main lobby. Thirty meters high. Martian stone floor. At the center of the lobby was a map of Mars. A map that updated in real time. Where what was being mined. Where oxygen was being produced. Where MCC facilities were. All visible. There was a will to show it.

speaker: narrator
text: Employees passed by. Everyone was busy. No one looked unbusy. Whether they were pretending or genuinely busy was impossible to tell. In MCC that distinction didn't matter.

speaker: narrator
text: Gate 3. Briefing room. One fluorescent light flickered. A map on the table. Nobody by the map. A moment later someone came in.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang. Director of Operations for the Hellas region. Age was unclear. A face of someone who had worked on Mars a long time. Mars didn't age people, it hardened them. Li Fang was hardened.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang didn't pull out a chair. Didn't say to sit. He stood looking at the map. The table was wide. The map covered the table. Northern Hellas.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang stood before the map. Northern Hellas sector. Oxygen refinery markers. Seven bases. Numbers written. What the numbers meant couldn't be asked. It wasn't yet the time to ask.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang pointed to a spot on the map. Northern transport corridor. A convoy was passing through there. Already departed, it meant. Not yet arrived. Something could be done in between.

speaker: narrator
text: The fluorescent light flickered again. It hadn't been repaired. No one cared about the flickering fluorescent light in MCC headquarters' briefing room. Other things were more important.

speaker: narrator
text: 850 kilotons. Recover it and MCC acquires the refineries. Fail and it vanishes in the storm. Li Fang looked at you. The briefing room light flickered again.

speaker: narrator
text: A last look at the map. Northern transport corridor. Convoy position. Predicted storm path. Six hours. Calculated distance and time. The calculation might be right or wrong. On Mars calculations were often wrong.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside headquarters. Two vehicles. Three team members waiting. All expressionless. Hard to find someone with an expression on Mars. Expressions were a luxury.

speaker: narrator
text: The northern sky was different. Not red. Dark. The direction the storm was coming from. Whether six hours was accurate was uncertain. Martian storms sometimes came before the predicted time.

speaker: narrator
text: Northern Hellas transport corridor. Unpaved road. The vehicle ran. Dust rose. The dust wasn't a good color. Martian dust was always like that. Not good.

speaker: narrator
text: The radio crackled. One team member adjusted the channel. Noise remained after adjustment. Radio on Mars always had noise. You had to listen through the noise.

speaker: narrator
text: Two hours passed. Midway along the transport corridor. Traces of the convoy. Tire tracks. Oil marks. Recent ones. Ahead.

speaker: narrator
text: The northern sky got darker. The storm was accelerating. Faster than predicted. On Mars some things were faster than predicted. The storm was one of them.

speaker: narrator
text: The convoy was visible. Tank trucks. Thirty-six tanks. Moving slowly. Heavy. 850 kilotons was heavy. Guard vehicles on both sides.

speaker: narrator
text: Helion guards spotted the MCC vehicles. They accelerated. Just as Li Fang said. They would block. Blocking was their job. Being blocked wasn't allowed. Six hours had become four hours. The storm was coming fast.

speaker: narrator
text: The lights of Hellas Central came on. It was night. The Martian night was long. Inside the building MCC kept running. It never stopped. You were inside it now.

speaker: narrator
text: The storm passed in the north. Hellas Central windows shook. Briefly. The building shook but didn't fall. A sixty-year-old building. It had weathered storms for sixty years. It would weather tomorrow's too.

speaker: narrator
text: The outer Hellas.

speaker: narrator
text: A relay station. Closed. The name had been deleted from the records.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC had a long memory. But it also deleted well.

speaker: narrator
text: The old miner's words came back. Someone to put it in the record, he had said.

speaker: narrator
text: One more name that didn't make it into the record.

speaker: narrator
text: But there was chalk. The alley children would write it.

speaker: narrator
text: [ Ending: Casualty — One the System Doesn't Remember ]

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn broke on Olympus.

speaker: narrator
text: The highest point in the solar system. Where light came first on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: No MCC. No FSP. No CV.

speaker: narrator
text: For the first time there were no three flags.

speaker: narrator
text: But Mars was there. People were there.

speaker: narrator
text: People working in mines. Children. Chalk names.

speaker: narrator
text: Those remained. Things that outlasted flags.

speaker: narrator
text: Outlasting a cup of tea. Outlasting twenty-five degrees. Those things were Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: [ Ending: Crown — One Who Transcends All Three Factions ]

speaker: narrator
text: The largest building on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Built sixty years ago. Kept growing since. Now it was yours.

speaker: narrator
text: Not only that. The mines of Mars. The refineries. Oxygen supply network. Water distribution system.

speaker: narrator
text: All yours. There was an empire. On Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside the window Hellas was visible. Small. From an empire everything was small.

speaker: narrator
text: But in C-7 block there was chalk. Small things continued.

speaker: narrator
text: [ Ending: Empire — One Who Controls Mars as One ]

speaker: narrator
text: The 25-Degree Lounge.

speaker: narrator
text: You sat. Held the tea. Didn't drink it.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside the window was Hellas. The city MCC built. Now the city you would inherit.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen turned her back. Didn't leave. Just looked out the window.

speaker: narrator
text: Two people looking at the window. Twenty-five degrees. Tea didn't cool.

speaker: narrator
text: Things to be remembered didn't cool.

speaker: narrator
text: [ Ending: Heir — One Who Would Change MCC ]

speaker: narrator
text: It wasn't over. Things rarely ended on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Starting again was Mars's way. Miners descended into tunnels every morning. That was Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: A decision was made. Chen heard it. Lifang heard it at the door.

speaker: narrator
text: The 25-Degree Lounge was quiet. Tea didn't cool.

speaker: narrator
text: But outside Hellas there was movement. Osei hadn't resigned. Instead Pilgrim Arms came again.

speaker: narrator
text: There were lights in Hellas Central. Below was block C-7.

speaker: narrator
text: Chalk names. Kim Yong-jin. The names below. The eleven from Zone 12.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine elevator was still descending. Still ascending. Mars didn't stop.

speaker: narrator
text: Three days had passed since Olympus.

speaker: narrator
text: The lights of MCC headquarters were on. It was night. The Martian night was long.

speaker: narrator
text: The 25-Degree Lounge was lit too. Chen Weiss was there.

speaker: narrator
text: The Zone 12 records had been released. All three factions received them.

speaker: narrator
text: The MCC board reacted. Seventy-two hours. Within seventy-two hours they demanded an explanation from Chen Weiss.

speaker: narrator
text: And from you too.

speaker: narrator
text: Lifang was waiting in the corridor.

speaker: narrator
text: Twelve years. From the first time, he had been in the corridor. A person more often outside the door than inside.

speaker: narrator
text: Osei. Marchetti. Ryu. Those three names had been heard before. In the board chamber. During the Kepler presentation. During the C-7 block interrogation.

speaker: narrator
text: All of that connected. To ten in the morning.

speaker: narrator
text: The first time she saw the records. Those words came slowly.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen saw the Zone 12 records in her second year. Internal MCC audit. But the records were locked. For twenty-two years.

text: Hellas was visible. In the window the entire city.
