speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss drank her tea. Drank the second cup too.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone who hadn't drunk for twenty-two years drank today. After passing through the board. After presenting evidence. After speaking of thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: The tea didn't cool. Twenty-five degrees. That hadn't changed.

speaker: narrator
text: It was night. The mine didn't stop. The mine ran at night too. Shift system. Miners shifted. The mine didn't shift. The machines didn't shift. Some things didn't stop.  The report was uploaded to the server. It became something that couldn't be undone.

speaker: narrator
text: The sector was still unsafe. The miners had to go back in. They had no other choice. The old man looked at the radio. Said nothing. That too was how Mars spoke.

speaker: narrator
text: The old miner went back. His back still small. But slightly different from before. Exactly what was different was unclear. Just a little different. On Mars some things changed just a little.

speaker: narrator
text: The next mission was an audit. Li Fang pushed a file across. A thick file. No need to ask what was inside. Mine audit report. All MCC mines on Mars were audited quarterly. It was a formality.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang stood up. He took the file back. Left one sheet. Audit checklist. Thirty-seven items. Safety equipment status. Support conditions. Ventilation system. Emergency exit locations. Accident records. Item thirty-seven was last. Accident records.

speaker: narrator
text: Northern Hellas transport corridor. Three hours to the mine facility. Wilderness outside the window. Nothing. The northern Hellas had nothing. That was why they mined there. In a place with nothing, there was something.

speaker: narrator
text: Occasional structures in the wilderness. Exhaust pipes. Old signal towers. Power line supports. All MCC's. There was nothing that wasn't MCC's. In the northern hemisphere of Mars. Nobody asked about ownership. Those who had asked were gone.

speaker: narrator
text: Mine entrance. Iron gate. A guard. The guard checked the ID. MCC audit team, it was said. The guard relayed something on the radio. A short wait. The gate opened.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine facility manager came out. Quick steps. A prepared expression. He knew the audit team was coming. Knowing means preparing. Preparing means hiding. That was the premise of an audit.

speaker: narrator
text: Sector 7. An asterisk was made on the checklist. The manager saw it. His expression didn't change. A prepared person. A prepared expression was the most frightening expression.

speaker: narrator
text: Started with Sector A. Checklist. Safety equipment status. Present. Ventilation system. Operating. Emergency exits. Marked. Everything satisfactory. Prepared things.

speaker: narrator
text: The mine elevator descended two kilometers below the surface. As it went down the temperature rose. The surface was below zero but underground was different. Miners knew this difference. Whether knowing it was a good thing was unclear.

speaker: narrator
text: Sector B. Sector C. Sector D. Check. Check. Check. The manager walked ahead. Gave explanations. Stated numbers. Production output. Efficiency. Shift system. The numbers were good. Numbers were always good.

speaker: narrator
text: Miners were working. Some had no safety equipment. No masks. Hands black with ore dust. How much they'd inhaled wasn't visible. Not visible didn't mean not there.

speaker: narrator
text: Written on the checklist. Multiple workers not wearing safety equipment. The manager saw it. His expression didn't change. He said it. Only today. Usually everyone wears them. A few forgot during today's inspection. A plausible explanation.

speaker: narrator
text: Sector E. Passed. Sector F. Passed. Sector 7. The manager stopped. He said next. Said to go to Sector 8. Said again that Sector 7 was under work and couldn't be entered. The asterisk on the checklist was looked at again.

speaker: narrator
text: Went to Sector 7. The manager followed. He couldn't stop you. Stopping would be more suspicious. Sector 7 entrance. Yellow tape. A sign saying under work. No sound. Under work should have sound.

speaker: narrator
text: Sector 7. Where a support had collapsed. The support had been repaired. But the date of collapse wasn't in the records. No record meant no accident. That was MCC's record-keeping.

speaker: narrator
text: New supports and old supports were mixed. Where the new support had been installed there was evidence. Fresh cement. Around it older cement. The cement colors were different. Different dates.

speaker: narrator
text: Marks on the ground. Scrape marks. Marks from something heavy being dragged. The marks of a stretcher. There was one reason a stretcher would be dragged in a Martian mine.

speaker: narrator
text: The old miner turned away. His back was small. It was the look of someone who had worked there a long time. The clipboard person wrote something. You didn't look at what they wrote.

speaker: narrator
text: The manager came close. His expression still unchanged. He said the old man had always had complaints. Maintaining accurate records was MCC policy. If there had been an accident it would have been recorded. His words sounded right and not right at the same time.

speaker: narrator
text: The radio was turned on. Li Fang was contacted. The situation in Sector 7 was relayed. Stretcher marks. Fresh cement. The old man's testimony. Li Fang was silent for a moment. There was a length to the silence. Short silence and long silence were different.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang cut the radio. The radio went quiet. The mine wasn't quiet. Machine sounds. Distant work sounds. Among those sounds the old man was working. Couldn't be seen. His sound couldn't be heard. But he was there.

speaker: narrator
text: The checklist was in hand. Thirty-seven items. Thirty-six checked. Last item. Accident records. Not checked. There was nothing to check. Or there was too much to check.

speaker: narrator
text: The elevator ascended. Surface light returned. Blood-red. The mine stayed below. The miners stayed below. The old man stayed below. The report was in hand. The hands didn't tremble.

speaker: narrator
text: Twenty-five degrees. It was a temperature. But it was not only that. On Mars maintaining warmth was power. Chen Weiss knew this. She held the tea. Didn't drink it. Tea that wouldn't cool. But that tea was made from miners' allowances. She knew that too. She maintained twenty-five degrees to not forget. That was this room's real name.

speaker: narrator
text: You returned. The data was incomplete. Chen would already know. She always did. She would be holding her tea. Not drinking. Tea didn't cool at twenty-five degrees. She could wait. That too was a form of power.

speaker: narrator
text: A summons arrived. Sender: Chen Weiss. Content: 10 AM. 25-Degree Lounge. Brief. In MCC brief summons meant one of two things. Unimportant or very important. This was the second.

speaker: narrator
text: On Mars maintaining twenty-five degrees cost money. A great deal. Chen Weiss's office was always twenty-five degrees. That was the room's name. The 25-Degree Lounge. There was a reason it had a name.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC executive floor. Sixth floor. There was an elevator. But the elevator required a separate key. The 6th floor button was locked. Stairs existed. The stairs also needed a code. The code changed. Weekly. That was why the sixth floor was the sixth floor.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss was holding a cup of tea. The cup was full. But she wasn't drinking it. This was her way. In the twenty-five degree room the tea wouldn't cool. It could stay like that forever.

speaker: narrator
text: Her parents had been miners. Born on Mars. Second generation. They worked the mines and they died in them. Chen didn't talk about it often. But whenever she held the tea it was there somewhere.

speaker: narrator
text: The window was full-wall. All of Hellas Central visible. A panorama. The city's layers visible. Upper. Middle. Lower. More dust the lower you went. From the window everything was small. The layer where her parents had been was smallest.

speaker: narrator
text: Tea came. The cup was taken. Chen looked at her own cup. Didn't drink. Just held it. In the twenty-five degree air the tea wouldn't cool. That was this room's power.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen looked toward the window. Briefly. Came back. Held the tea. Didn't drink. This repeated. There were things that repeated in this room. Those things made this room what it was.

speaker: narrator
text: She looked at the window. The panoramic window. All of Hellas. The mine district was visible. Small. She held her tea. Didn't drink. Even while telling that story. That said more. More than words.

speaker: narrator
text: The tea didn't cool. Twenty-five degree air. Chen held the tea. Didn't drink. The conversation continued. But not drinking the tea said more. In this room what was not done was heavier than what was done.

speaker: narrator
text: Later. When that word was said in this room it had different weight. A later that was certain. Not many people in MCC had a certain later. Chen Weiss was one. That was another name for this room. A place where later was certain.

speaker: narrator
text: Your thoughts. That was strange. In MCC people rarely asked for your thoughts. It was an organization that wanted your reports. Reports were facts. Facts could be managed. Thoughts were different. Chen Weiss wanting thoughts had a reason.

speaker: narrator
text: Tea was in the hand. Warm. Twenty-five degrees. Miners paid for that warmth. Chen kept this room at twenty-five to not forget. That was understood. But whether fully understood was uncertain. On Mars nothing was fully understood.

speaker: narrator
text: Quiet. Beyond the panoramic window was Hellas. The city MCC built. From this room everything was small. That was intentional. Distinguishing what should look small from what should not. That was what twenty-two years had taught.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen looked at the window. Long. Held the tea. Didn't drink. Hellas was in that window. Small. But from this room it was known that wasn't everything. What looked small wasn't actually small. That was what Mars taught.

speaker: narrator
text: Contract. Everything on Mars was contract. Oxygen was contract. Water was contract. Mines were contract. But when people died within contracts the cause section was blank. That blank was in the contract. Filling that blank. That was what Chen said without saying.

speaker: narrator
text: Held the tea. Drank. Warm. Chen held her cup. Didn't drink. Two cups. One emptying. One staying full. That difference was this room's real name.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss was holding the tea. Still not drinking it. Through the window Hellas Central was visible. The city MCC built. From this room everything looked small. She had intended that.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen reacted. Subtly. Lowered the cup slightly. Just slightly. The hand of someone who had held a cup for twenty-two years lowering it. That was the largest movement in this room.

speaker: narrator
text: Before leaving looked at the window. All of Hellas visible. Upper. Middle. Lower. Dust. Mine. Block C-7. Where chalk names were. From this room not visible. Too small. But they were there. Always there.

speaker: narrator
text: Walked toward the door. Chen was looking at the window. Holding her tea. Not drinking. From behind her shoulders were visible. 22 years of MCC. Miner parents. Twelve and alone. Those things were in those shoulders. Invisible but there. Things on Mars were like that.

speaker: narrator
text: Kepler Crater was still there. Deep and dark. A basin within a basin. Now it was known what was inside. Dark silver. Thirty years of waiting. Blue sunset. Those things were there. Whose it was had not yet been decided.

speaker: narrator
text: The site was lost. FSP got there first. Or CV. Either way the sample was gone. Liang Wei said nothing. That was heavier. The silence of someone who had waited thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. A basin within a basin. Where MCC and FSP disputed mineral rights. Whether there were minerals or not nobody knew exactly. That was also why they disputed it.

speaker: narrator
text: 400 kilometers east of Hellas Central. Six hours by transport vehicle. No road. Martian surface. Red bedrock. Dust. Occasionally wind struck the window. Low sound. Martian wind always made low sounds. Different from Earth wind. Earth wind was higher.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn. The Martian dawn was different from Earth. The sky was red. Still red at dawn. Redder when the sun rose. Not going from dark to light. Going from red to redder. The first dawn at Kepler.

speaker: narrator
text: Liang Wei was a geologist. An outsider. Neither MCC nor FSP. But she knew Kepler better than anyone. She had surveyed it for thirty years. Thirty years of data was in her head.

speaker: narrator
text: Her research base was at the crater's edge. Small. Two containers. Solar panels. External antenna. Only what was necessary. The space of someone who had researched here alone for thirty years. Unnecessary things disappeared after thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: Liang Wei was talking to an MCC person. Knowing that. Someone who had researched alone for thirty years speaking to someone for the first time. That was felt. Careful. But she didn't stop. Thirty years of waiting kept her from stopping.

speaker: narrator
text: Descended into the crater. Lifang came along. Lifang was silent descending. Inside the crater was quiet. Quieter than the Martian surface. Wind circled above. Didn't come down into the crater. Deep places were quiet. The quietest things on Mars were in the deepest places.

speaker: narrator
text: One kilometer. Two kilometers. Three kilometers. Descended. The place where the geology team had stopped was visible. A marker. A warning marker. Ground instability. MCC standard marking. Below it no marker. Below it you could keep descending. There was a reason to.

speaker: narrator
text: Liang Wei went first. Below the warning marker. She didn't hesitate. Someone who had spent thirty years in this crater. This warning marker wasn't a warning to her. It was a guide. Indicating to go further down.

speaker: narrator
text: Looked at the stratum. What Liang Wei said was visible. Dark silver. Different from Martian minerals. Mars was red and ochre. This was different. Reached to touch it. Liang Wei stopped the hand.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a mineral sample. The color was different. Not like ordinary Martian minerals. Analysis was needed to know what it was. Report to MCC before analysis and it would become MCC's. That was what the contract said.

speaker: narrator
text: Liang Wei was looking at the sample. She had waited thirty years for this. What was in that face was hard to read. But her hands trembled. Slightly. The hands of someone who had waited thirty years.

speaker: narrator
text: Lifang was beside. Said nothing. That was Lifang's way. A person who said only what was necessary. But his silence now was different. A silence waiting for something. A silence waiting for a decision.

speaker: narrator
text: Above the crater the Martian sky was visible. Red. The sun tilted. The dark silver sample was in the hand. Small. But heavy. The weight of thirty years. The weight of the MCC contract too. Two weights in the same hand.

speaker: narrator
text: Sunset. Edge of Kepler crater. The sun was going below the horizon. Martian sunsets were different from Earth. They turned blue. The red sky turned blue at dusk. That moment was brief. But it was there. The first time seeing it at Kepler.

speaker: narrator
text: In the blue sunset was Kepler Crater. A basin 3 kilometers deep. Dark silver inside. Thirty years of research. MCC contract. Academic rejection. All of that was in this sunset. In the blue light. Light only visible on this planet.

speaker: narrator
text: Night came. Kepler's night. No wind below in the crater. Wind above on the rim. Inside the crater and outside were different. Standing on this boundary. Inside and outside. Before decision and after decision. On that boundary.

speaker: narrator
text: Next day's dawn. Second dawn at Kepler. Red again. From red to redder. The sample was in a pocket. Had been there all night. Decision not yet made. But dawn came. Time for decision came.

speaker: narrator
text: A decision was made. Whatever that decision — Kepler Crater was unchanged. Three kilometers deep. Basin within basin. Dark silver inside. The decision didn't change that. But it changed what came after.

speaker: narrator
text: A dust storm. Came suddenly. Martian dust storms came suddenly. Visibility decreased. 50 meters. 20 meters. 10 meters. FSP vehicle signal was approaching. In the dust. Not visible but there. Things on Mars were like that.

speaker: narrator
text: Li Fang was waiting for the report. That was his way. What to tell him had already been decided. What remained undecided was what not to say. The difference between the two was large. On Mars it always was. Chalk names were on the alley wall. Wind blew. They didn't erase.

speaker: narrator
text: No chip. No miner. MCC security filled the stairs. Sublevel 4. A place where footsteps carried well. The deaths since 2009 remained underground.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside. Martian air came through the mask. The miner walked a different direction. His name wasn't asked. That was right. Names weren't protection. The chip was there. Small. The history of Mars was in the hand. The history that officially didn't exist.

speaker: narrator
text: Returned from Kepler. Hellas Central. Same city. But looked different. Seen through eyes that had been to Kepler it was different. Three kilometers down. Dark silver. Blue sunset. Those were in memory. Hellas was unchanged. But different.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC's archive was on the fourth sublevel. No elevator. Stairs. MCC favored spaces without elevators. Stairs made people slow. Slow people had time to think. People who thought became afraid. Afraid people kept quiet. That was the purpose of stairs.

speaker: narrator
text: A message arrived. No sender. The content was short. Sublevel 4. Three in the afternoon. Alone. Bring only what you remember. That was all the message said. The message was deleted. But the memory wasn't deleted. Memory couldn't be deleted.

speaker: narrator
text: Descended the stairs. Sublevel 4. 16 flights. The lighting grew darker with each level. Level 1. Level 2. Level 3. Level 4. Lowest. Darkest. That too was intentional. In MCC nothing was unintentional.

speaker: narrator
text: He was there. Forties. Hands black. Ore dust. The kind that wouldn't wash out. Hollow around the eyes. Not the face of someone who hadn't slept. The face of someone who had never known sleep.

speaker: narrator
text: He was standing. Didn't sit. Nothing to sit on in sublevel 4. Archive shelves. Documents packed tight. 30 years. 40 years. 50 years of documents. MCC's memory was here. The irony was this. In this room of memory was where the most things absent from memory were.

speaker: narrator
text: The chip lay in the palm. Small. A fingertip's length. Seventeen cases. The deaths of Mars since 2009 were inside it. He was trembling. The hand that held out the chip. But the eyes didn't tremble. The eyes of someone who had decided long ago. Those were the heaviest kind of eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: Personal negligence. That phrase was in the sublevel 4 air. How many such phrases were in the archive shelves. Phrases that filled cause sections. But not the real cause. MCC's memory was filled with such phrases.

speaker: narrator
text: Those words were heavy. You're the only one. In MCC. To take the chip holding 17 deaths. That was true. Here in sublevel 4. In this thick archive. That was true.

speaker: narrator
text: The record remains. That phrase had strange resonance in this place. MCC archive. Place of records. But these records were not real records. Falsified records. Deaths without cause. A real record was being passed here in this sublevel. Among the falsified ones.

speaker: narrator
text: A sound came from the stairs above. Footsteps. MCC's building carried sound well. The stairs especially. Two people. Descending slowly. People who descended slowly were not in a hurry. People not in a hurry were more dangerous.

speaker: narrator
text: He turned. Went to the shelves. Pulled out documents. As if nothing had happened. A person who had waited thirty years became in two minutes someone for whom nothing happened. That was how you lived on Mars. The ability to become nobody in an instant.

speaker: narrator
text: The chip was in the hand. Into the pocket. Footsteps grew closer. Two people. Slow footsteps. On the third sublevel stairs. Now the fourth. Would be visible soon. Had to explain what was being done here in sublevel 4.

speaker: narrator
text: The decision was made. The next moved with that decision. Two people appeared from the stairs. MCC internal audit armbands. They came down. Slow. Not in a hurry. Knew that was more dangerous.

speaker: narrator
text: The auditors looked. As if there was nothing. But they looked. On Mars auditors' eyes always looked. They recorded what was visible. They also recorded what was not visible. That was auditing. Recording absences more than presences.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside. Hellas Central exterior. Night. The chip was in the pocket. Small. But heavy. Seventeen people. Since 2009. Names. Dates. Repair requests. Approval denials. All of that inside this small thing.

speaker: narrator
text: The Hellas labor district was visible. Night. There were lights. Windows. Windows with people. Where miners lived. Where the seventeen had lived. Where their families still lived. The chip was in the pocket.

speaker: narrator
text: A name appeared in an old MCC document. Cinder Grace. Former MCC mechanical engineer. Contract terminated three years ago. Reason: conduct violation. Current affiliation: unknown. There was a photo. The kind of person whose eyes you'd still remember. People on Mars with eyes like that had gone somewhere else.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace. Conduct violation. What that was wasn't in the documents. In MCC documents there were things without reasons. Those things held the most stories. The absence of a reason was the reason. Many things on Mars were like that.

speaker: narrator
text: Lifang's words. Whether that was a warning or permission was unclear. That was how Lifang's words were on Mars. Both or neither. Had to decide on that boundary. The chip was still in the pocket.

speaker: narrator
text: In the labor district alley children were playing. Night. Wearing masks. Martian children. Chalk names on the wall. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. People who died in mines. Written by the children.

speaker: narrator
text: The chip was in the pocket. Seventeen names inside. The wall names were there too. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. The names in the chip connected to the names on the wall. The same kind of names. Names not in records. But names written in chalk.

speaker: narrator
text: The chalk names of block C-7 would not be erased by the morning wind. Chalk was weak. But no matter how strong the Martian wind, it could not erase names that had already been remembered. Kim Yong-jin. The names below. The names below that, not yet written.

speaker: narrator
text: No server. FSP was first. The children watched from the alley. They knew which side had lost. Children on Mars learned such things quickly.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss read the report. Holding her tea. Not drinking it. Outside the window was the Hellas labor district. A sector MCC built. A sector of people who lived for MCC. The window was thick. No sound came through. That was intentional.

speaker: narrator
text: Information had leaked. MCC knew it. They knew where it came from. And who helped. MCC had a long memory. On Mars there was only one organization with a long memory. That was MCC's real power.

speaker: narrator
text: Vendetta. On Mars that word took a different shape. Not violence. MCC didn't use violence. Violence left traces. Instead they suspended permits. Cancelled contracts. Adjusted oxygen allocations. That was cleaner than violence. And more complete.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. Even giving this order. Orders on Mars came like this. In a quiet voice. Holding tea. Without directly threatening. But every word contained a threat. Chen Weiss's way.

speaker: narrator
text: Understood. But understanding didn't justify everything. Understanding and agreement were different. On Mars that difference was large. But an order was an order. Refuse an order and there was a next. The next was also MCC's way.

speaker: narrator
text: Block C-7. Night. The Martian night was long. People were in the alleys. Children. Miners' children. Wearing masks. Children wearing masks in alleys. That was what children on Mars were.

speaker: narrator
text: Names were written on the wall. Chalk. Kim Yong-jin. More names below. Several. Not the names of people who died in FSP labor districts. The names of people who died in MCC mines. Written by the alley children.

speaker: narrator
text: The children looked. There was a stranger. No MCC armband. But they knew. Martian children learned that quickly. Who was MCC. By gait. By gaze. By how they looked at the alley.

speaker: narrator
text: The block C-7 server room was there. First sublevel. MCC built this block. MCC knew the structure of every block. Where servers were. Where emergency exits were. Where people gathered. MCC always knew.

speaker: narrator
text: FSP contact network. Miners' contacts. A network for sharing safety information. Mine accident information. Danger zone information. Those were in this server. That was what MCC wanted. Without it FSP couldn't reach the miners.

speaker: narrator
text: A name appeared in an old MCC document. Cinder Grace. Former MCC mechanical engineer. Contract terminated three years ago. Reason: conduct violation. Current affiliation: unknown. There was a photo. The kind of person whose eyes you'd still remember. People on Mars with eyes like that had gone somewhere else.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace. The name was remembered. Seen in documents five sections back. Conduct violation. No reason. In MCC documents termination without reason. What that meant was now known. Had leaked safety reports. To FSP. Three years ago.

speaker: narrator
text: Lifang said no more. That was enough. Cinder Grace was someone who had learned MCC's way. And someone who had told the outside. MCC didn't tolerate that. Vendetta came. Contract terminated. Deleted from records. On Mars deletion meant non-existence.

speaker: narrator
text: Children were watching from the alley. Looking toward the server room direction. Children understood faster than adults. What was happening. Martian children grew up that way. As children who quickly understood what was happening.

speaker: narrator
text: In front of the server room. Miner database. FSP contact network. What MCC wanted. But in this database were names. Miners' names. Their families' names. Contact information. What that would become in MCC hands was known. It would become a negotiating card.

speaker: narrator
text: Lifang gave the decision to you. That was strange. Lifang was someone who followed orders. But now he didn't give an order. He gave a decision. That difference was large in this alley. Children were watching. Chalk names were there. Server room was there. One minute left.

speaker: narrator
text: Decision made. The FSP team arrived. Into the alley. Children moved to both sides. The children knew situations like this. Knew when to get out of the way. They were Martian children. Fast learners.

speaker: narrator
text: The FSP team stopped. Assessed the situation. They also had to decide. In this alley there were two decisions. MCC's. FSP's. Children were against the wall. Beside the chalk names. That was this scene.

speaker: narrator
text: On the way back. Chalk names. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. Written by the alley children. Where the children went was unknown. Home probably. The homes where miners' children lived. Homes MCC built.

speaker: narrator
text: One miner survived. Because of Cinder Grace. That was the conduct violation. MCC's logic. That logic came from the same organization as the person holding tea in the 25-Degree Lounge. Mars was like that. Different logics within the same organization. People lived between them.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside Erebus Crater. Information arrived. Cinder Grace's trace was here. CV territory. A place MCC didn't reach. Or chose not to reach. CV was a different kind of danger. MCC threatened with contracts. CV threatened differently.

speaker: narrator
text: Erebus. There was a reason for that name. In Greek myth Erebus was the darkness of the underworld. On Mars names were mostly from Earth. Names brought from Earth. But Martian landscapes fit those names. Erebus Crater. Crater of darkness.

speaker: narrator
text: Lifang stopped. Would wait here. That was Lifang's final line on Mars. A place with no MCC order. He was someone who stopped there. That was his way. The way of someone who had lived like that for a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen left the chamber. Still holding her tea. But the cup was empty. One person saw it. In twenty-two years nobody had seen Chen Weiss's cup empty. First sightings were rare on Mars. But they happened.

speaker: narrator
text: The board deferred the decision. That was a rejection. Board deferrals were always rejections. The tea had cooled. They said tea never cooled in this room. That was one more thing that wasn't true.

speaker: narrator
text: The board chamber was completely sealed. No outside air entered. Its own oxygen circulation system. In all of MCC headquarters only the board chamber had its own air. The directors understood what it meant to have your own air on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: A summons arrived. Brief. Board chamber. 9 AM. There was a sender. MCC Board Secretariat. What the summons meant was still unknown. But it was to be accepted. Nobody in MCC refused a call from the Board Secretariat.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss was waiting in the corridor. Holding her tea. Not drinking it. She had arrived first. That was a message. This person always arrived first. That was how she existed in this organization.

speaker: narrator
text: Seven directors. The table was circular. No head seat. But everyone knew where Chen Weiss sat. That was another form of head seat. The form power takes without marking itself.

speaker: narrator
text: Stopped briefly at the entrance. Voices from inside the door. Low. Indistinct. Seven directors. The most important people on Mars. Their decisions set oxygen prices. Set water prices. Set miners' contract conditions. One door away.

speaker: narrator
text: You entered. The directors looked. Chen didn't stand. She held her tea. Didn't drink it. That was the introduction. That was enough. In the MCC boardroom Chen's silence was a statement.

speaker: narrator
text: The directors listened. No expressions. That was the board's way. Trying to read expressions was pointless. There was nothing to read. When directors showed something it was because a decision had already been made. What was shown in this room was result. Not process.

speaker: narrator
text: The board knew. It said so. And still wanted to hear it from you. That was this room's test. How you say what is already known. Or don't say it. Or say it differently. Three things were different.

speaker: narrator
text: Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. Dark silver mineral. Extraterrestrial origin possibility. This was being said in this room. Before the directors. Seven of them. No expressions. But listening. The air in this room was its own. Different from outside.

speaker: narrator
text: The third option. What wasn't said clearly. In MCC that was deletion. Research terminated. Researcher terminated. On Mars deletion took various forms. Contract terminated. Records deleted. Permits revoked. The result was the same. They ceased to exist.

speaker: narrator
text: Directors waited. Circular table. Seven expressionless people. Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. In this room Chen always held her tea. For twenty-two years. No one had seen her drink it in this room. That was her ritual in this room. Hold the tea. Don't drink. Wait.

speaker: narrator
text: The board knew everything. Block C-7. Server. Decision. They knew and were asking. They wanted to hear it from you. That was a test. The board's test. The oldest kind of test on Mars. Confirming what is already known.

speaker: narrator
text: Directors waited. Seven. Circular table. Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. The air in this room was its own. Sealed. Knew where words spoken in this room went. MCC's memory. Remembered forever. Never erased.

speaker: narrator
text: Already been handled. That phrase sounded soft in this room. Board words were soft. But their meaning was sharp. Already been handled. What that meant was something you didn't ask about. In this room. The things not asked made this room what it was.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside the window Hellas was visible. MCC's city. The mine district visible. Small. Block C-7 visible. Smaller. Chalk names not visible. Too small. But they were there. Not gone. What was decided in this room went down there. That was what this window said.

speaker: narrator
text: Directors waited. Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. Twenty-two years in this room. Never drinking it. Nobody knew the reason. For twenty-two years. But today she hadn't yet. Not yet.

speaker: narrator
text: The 25-Degree Lounge. Adjacent to the board chamber. Chen was here. Holding tea. Not drinking. This room too was the same temperature as the board chamber. Always twenty-five degrees. That was why the lounge was called 25-Degree. That was where Chen was.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen was asking the same question. The same as the board. But in a different way. The board asked through tests. Chen said it directly. What that difference meant was still unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Board approval. The weight of those words was known. When approval came from this room Mars changed. That change went down to the mine district. Down to block C-7. To where chalk names were. Board approval came from here but results were down there.

speaker: narrator
text: Dawn. Outside Hellas Zone 4. The dust storm had passed. Mars's dawn was different from Earth's. Redder. The sun smaller. In the direction Cinder Grace walked was that light. She was someone you felt you could understand where she'd come from. Where she was going was still unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace was gone. The miner was gone. MCC would find out. MCC always found out. The relay station remained closed. There was still nothing in the records.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Zone 4. Dawn. MCC operational area. Intelligence arrived. CV and FSP were operating a joint base. Outside Hellas Zone 4. They had occupied an old MCC facility. Unconfirmed intelligence. But the board requested confirmation.

speaker: narrator
text: The intelligence was brief. Outside Zone 4. Closed MCC relay station. Multiple CV operatives. And something being moved. What unknown. When today. MCC left many things unexplained. Missions from the board were always like that.

speaker: narrator
text: Zone 4 ruins. A place where there had been an accident thirty years ago. Same zone as Zone 12. Different tunnel. MCC closed it. Three years ago. No reason in the records. There were many things on this planet with no reason in the records.

speaker: narrator
text: Sector 12 ruins. Outer Hellas. There had been an accident here three years ago. The MCC report said equipment failure. But records differed on who wrote the report. Multiple versions existed. In MCC records. Which was the truth was still unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the relay station. Someone was there. Alone. A woman. Tools hung on her belt. Several. An engineer's tools. Oil on her hands. Working. But no weapon. On the outer plains people without weapons were rare.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder Grace. She hadn't said her name. But it was known. Those were the eyes from the file. Even in the photo it had seemed like eyes you'd remember. In person more so. This was someone who had been through something. It was in the eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: The report. Three deaths in Sector 7. Writing it had meaning here. Cinder knew it. A report from inside MCC. It saved the miner. Someone MCC had processed as dead. It was connected. The report and this person and this day.

speaker: narrator
text: Zone 12. Eleven people. Report. Revision request. Refusal. Tunnel collapse. That was Cinder Grace. Someone in MCC three years ago. Someone in CV now. Zone 12 was in between. That was why this person was here.

speaker: narrator
text: A dust storm came. Mars's dust storm. Visibility narrowed. Outside the relay station was invisible. Through the dust storm an MCC team was approaching. An MCC team that didn't know about this mission. Standard procedure. Neutralize on CV operative detection.

speaker: narrator
text: The miner was there. In the corner. Hidden. Old. Sixties. Oil on the hands. A miner. Listed as dead in the records. Three years ago. What Cinder had said. Someone processed as dead in MCC records. Alive. Here.

speaker: narrator
text: A Zone 12 witness. Hidden for three years. Listed as dead in MCC records. Alive. And records were needed. Of what was seen. Cinder was moving for that. With tools. An engineer from MCC. Now a CV person.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder wasn't trying to kill. That was the strange thing. When CV met MCC it was battle. Always. But this person was talking. Holding tools. Asking about reasons. What that meant. Still unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: The dust storm strengthened. MCC team sounds grew closer. At the relay station's outer wall. Minutes away. Had to decide. Cinder and the miner. The mission. MCC team. And reason. The difference between people with reasons and without.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder waited. Holding tools. The miner was in the corner. Dust storm sounds were heard. And MCC team sounds too. Two kinds of sound. Which was closer. That was what mattered most right now.

speaker: narrator
text: The board. Circular table. Seven people. Expressionless. They knew. But they wanted to hear it from you. That memory was different here. What this person saw. At Zone 12. If it was put on record. Even before the board things could change.

speaker: narrator
text: MCC team reached the outer wall. Through the dust storm. At the relay station door. Thirty seconds. That was the decision time. Mission. Or reason. Which carried more weight in this moment.

speaker: narrator
text: This was the moment. Cinder Grace. Zone 12. Eleven people. Old miner. Records. MCC team. Mission. All of it was in this room. With dust storm sounds. With tool sounds.

speaker: narrator
text: Descending from Olympus. All of Mars was visible. Red. Below was Hellas. MCC's city. Smaller still was block C-7. The chalk names. Coming down they would be large again. That was what this mountain taught. Small things became large again on the way down.

speaker: narrator
text: The meeting didn't end. A meeting that didn't end was a collapse. Three factions went their separate ways. Olympus remained. Mountains always remained. Even when people left. Even without agreement. Zone 12 names remained locked. But Cinder had picked up her tools. That was different.

speaker: narrator
text: The agreement was signed. Three factions. Three signatures. Chen's was last. Before taking the pen she set down her tea. She signed with both hands. The right supporting the left. That was not her way. But today it was. This signature was worth that.

speaker: narrator
text: Olympus Mons. The highest mountain in the solar system. Summit pressure was 0.07 percent of Earth's. Without a mask ten seconds. That was why this place was chosen for the meeting. No one could stay here long. That was the fair condition.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen Weiss arrived first. That was her way. The person who arrived first defined the space. She held her tea. Didn't drink it. Even on Olympus it was the same as the 25-Degree Lounge. That consistency was hers.

speaker: narrator
text: Three factions. Three flags. MCC. FSP. CV. Same planet. Different futures. One table. Three chairs. Fewer chairs than people was a problem anywhere in the world. On Mars more so.

speaker: narrator
text: Rev. Hale sat. Didn't pray. This was not the place for that. Cinder Grace stood. Tool belt unchanged. She had worn it climbing to this summit too. Watching the two of them Chen held her tea. Didn't drink it.

speaker: narrator
text: Not a negotiation. Intelligence gathering. Chen said that. In this room. To you. That was MCC's way. Everything was purpose. The tea too. This room too. The meeting too. All of it was for information.

speaker: narrator
text: Zone 12. Eleven people. Photo. Names. Chen had known. For twenty-two years. It came to this table. Cinder brought it. With the tool belt. To Olympus. That was why today was a different day.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen decided. At this table. To unlock the Zone 12 records. For the first time in twenty-two years. Cinder's photo made that decision. That was why today was special. Not information gathering. A decision.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen's story. In this room. Before Cinder and Rev. Hale. First time telling it. Twenty-two years without telling it. Today first. In this room. In a room without windows. That was why this meeting was different.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen said it. That her mother had called Butcher. Thirty years ago. This was the first time it was said in any room. Her mother died. Eight years later. At Zone 12. Twenty-two years inside MCC. And today. On Olympus. In a room without windows. That was what was said in this room.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen had been keeping CV alive. For twenty-two years. Inside MCC. The eight years before that were her mother. Butcher didn't know. Cinder didn't know. Now they knew. In this room. On Olympus. At the highest point on Mars. That was said for the first time today.

speaker: narrator
text: Pilgrim Arms. Hired from inside the board. To stop Chen. To stop the Zone 12 record unlock. To stop what had been held for twenty-two years inside MCC. That was what was happening on Olympus today.

speaker: narrator
text: A choice. Follow Chen's instructions. Or act independently. Follow the board's instructions. Or protect Chen. Those were different directions. On Olympus. At the highest point on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside Olympus. Pilgrim Arms four were moving. Two east. Two west. Along the base's outer wall. After Chen. To stop the Zone 12 record unlock. Hired by the board. Inside MCC.

speaker: narrator
text: Cinder went out. With tools. On Olympus. At the highest point in the solar system. Tool sounds. That was the answer to this situation. Cinder's way. Fixing with tools. That went from this room to the outside.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen held her tea. Didn't drink it. In this room. Twenty-two years without drinking. But today. A little. She drank. Zone 12 photo was on the table. What Cinder brought. It was in this room. That was why today was different.

speaker: narrator
text: Names appearing in official documents. That was what the board was trying to stop. What had been locked away for twenty-two years. That was trying to open in this room today. And Pilgrim Arms had come to stop it. On the board's order.

speaker: narrator
text: Chen picked up the pen. Before the agreement. The agreement with names. Zone 12. Needing the signatures of three factions. One of them. That was about to happen. Sounds from the west. Close.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars was waiting for you. What would you become on this planet. Chen Weiss would be reading the report. Holding her tea. Not drinking.

speaker: narrator
text: Time to Mars — 14 hours. Black space beyond the cargo ship window. You knew you wouldn't be coming back when this journey ended.

speaker: narrator
text: The ship was called Kariope. Full of cargo. Oxygen tanks. Food packs. Machine parts. And people. People loaded like cargo too. Not enough seats. Nobody complained. People who boarded this ship had already made their choice.

speaker: narrator
text: 2087. Mars population: 12 million. Three factions divided this planet. MCC — Mars Corporate Consortium. Those who hold the resources. FSP — Free Settlers' Pact. Those who worked the land. CV — Crimson Warlords. Those who live without law.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars was once a shared dream. Sixty years had passed. The shared dream divided into stakes. Stakes divided by negotiation. Negotiation ended with force. Now it was just like that. Like every place in the world eventually becomes.

speaker: narrator
text: You received a summons from MCC. The reason was simple — they needed someone like you. What kind of person that was — you'd find out when you arrived on Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Others were in the cargo bay. Miners. Tired faces. People too tired going to Mars. Or people going to Mars to become tired. Hard to tell the difference. On Mars it amounted to the same thing.

speaker: narrator
text: Lifang looked out the window after speaking. Space was there. He said nothing more. That was his way. A person who said only what was necessary. People who had lived long on Mars became that way. People who knew words used oxygen.

speaker: narrator
text: There was an observation deck. A small window. People stood there. Looking out. Nothing. Just space. Still they looked. People trying to see Mars. It wasn't visible yet. Still they looked. That was the shape of hope. Looking for something not yet visible.

speaker: narrator
text: Twelve hours passed. Sleep came. Before sleeping looked out the window. A red dot was there. At first it looked like a star. As it grew closer — it became a planet. Blood-red. Beautiful. Frightening.

speaker: narrator
text: Two hours to landing. Announcement came. Masks on. Seatbelts. Entering Martian atmosphere. The voice was calm. A daily announcement. That calm felt strange. Strange that atmospheric entry could be daily and calm.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars filled the window. Red. Different from photos seen on Earth. Photos were flat. In reality it had depth. It looked alive. Mars wasn't alive. But it looked that way. That was Mars's first lie.

speaker: narrator
text: The docking bay. People disembarked. Miners. Engineers. Bureaucrats. Everyone wore masks. Masked faces were unreadable. No expressions. The first face of Mars. A mask.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central. The largest city on Mars. Population 800,000. An atmospheric dome. Inside was like Earth. Similar pressure. Similar oxygen. But Mars outside the windows was different. Red dust. A place humans couldn't survive. The dome maintained that boundary.

speaker: narrator
text: The city was divided into layers. Upper floors MCC administration. Middle floors engineer residences. Lower floors labor district. On Mars hierarchy was vertical. More dust the lower you went. Quieter the higher you went. Every hierarchy eventually took the same shape.

speaker: narrator
text: A briefing room. Other new arrivals. Six of them. From different places. Different ships. But in the same room. People MCC had called. Different reasons each. Same destination. That was MCC's way.

speaker: narrator
text: The regulations were thick. 247 pages. Someone had underlined them. A previous person's copy. The lines were thick. Important sections. Procedure for oxygen shortage. Emergency medical report channels. Those were heavily underlined. You could guess what the previous person had been through.

speaker: narrator
text: The first day ended. A residential zone was assigned. Middle level. There was a window. Through it the outer Hellas was visible. Beyond the dome. Red dust moving. Wind. The Martian wind made no sound. The dome blocked it. Wind visible but inaudible. Most things on Mars were like that.

speaker: narrator
text: Night came. The Martian night was long. 37 minutes longer than Earth. A day was 24 hours 37 minutes. For the first few days those 37 minutes felt strange. Feeling that strange things were strange was the first stage of adapting to Mars. The next was those strange things becoming normal.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside the mine. A tunnel entrance. An elevator. Going down. 3 kilometers. Where miners went every day. Miners were coming up. A shift change. Faces caked in dust. Masks darker. They said nothing coming up. The silence of exhausted people.

speaker: narrator
text: One of the miners was young. About twenty. He lifted his mask. Just briefly. His face was visible. A tired face. Tiredness of that age. That age shouldn't be tired. But on Mars it didn't matter. The mine shaft was equal.

speaker: narrator
text: Day three. Lifang gave documents. The first assignment. Sector 7 safety audit. Standard procedure. Field inspection. Write a report. Two-day deadline. Simple. That was how it started.

speaker: narrator
text: Sector 7. A small mining outpost on the outer Hellas. Staff 30. Primary mineral iron ore. A report form existed. A checklist. Safety equipment. Emergency exits. Oxygen backup. Checked one by one.

speaker: narrator
text: There was a problem. Not on the checklist. The ventilation system was old. No parts. Signs of improvised repair. Multiple times. Below standard. But formally it had passed. The checklist was designed to allow that.

speaker: narrator
text: More was there. Accident records. Past two years. Three cases. The cause section was blank. All three. Only names. Death. Death. Death. Deaths without cause. That was possible on Mars. If you didn't write the cause there was no cause.

speaker: narrator
text: Told Lifang. The ventilation system. Accident records. Three deaths without cause. He listened. No expression. Still no expression after everything was said. The face of someone who had hidden expressions for a long time. That too was what Mars made.

speaker: narrator
text: Wrote the report. Wrote what was seen. Ventilation system. Aged parts. Improvised repairs. Blank cause of death. Three cases. The names. Wrote them. Didn't erase them. The first decision. The first decision on Mars. Mars would remember it.

speaker: narrator
text: Submitted. The report was submitted. Exactly as seen. Lifang took it. Read it. Slowly. When done he was still for a moment. That silence was long. But it didn't feel long. It was a silence worth waiting through.

speaker: narrator
text: Day four. Hellas Central was becoming familiar. Memorized routes. Memorized faces. Masks made faces hard to memorize. So people memorized other things. Gait. Voice. The way they moved. Knowing people on Mars was like that.

speaker: narrator
text: A red dot appeared beyond the window. At first it looked like a star. As it grew closer — it became a planet. Blood-red. Beautiful. Frightening. Now inside that planet. Seen from inside it was different. That was Mars's second face.

speaker: narrator
text: The Kariyope left six hours later. Berk checked the manifest. The last name to disembark was there. Berk didn't read that name. A name on Mars began here. Different from the Kariyope's manifest.  The soil of Mars was beneath the feet. The blood-red sky was above. Somewhere was walked toward.

speaker: narrator
text: The stars didn't move. In space stars were always where they were. Only the ship moved. Cargo freighter Kariyope. Eighty thousand tons of freight. Forty-seven passengers. Under Captain Berk, twenty-three years in service, following the course toward Mars. The stars didn't know that.

speaker: narrator
text: The Kariyope drifted three more days before reaching Mars orbit. Navigator Berk didn't call it drifting. But his not calling it drifting didn't make it otherwise. The engines were efficient. The course was accurate. Still the arrival was late.

speaker: narrator
text: Arrivals are always late. That was one thing Berk had learned in twenty-three years. There were other things too but he hadn't written them down. There were more unwritten things than written ones.

speaker: narrator
text: The Kariyope's cargo hold was always filled with things returning from Mars. Scrap metal. Processed ore. Empty oxygen tanks. The next voyage would fill it again with the same things. Mars received and sent back. It didn't send people back.

speaker: narrator
text: This voyage's manifest. Two thousand eight hundred forty-seven items. Berk read half of it. The other half was always the same. The last entry was forty-seven passengers. Writing non-items as items was a navigator's job.

speaker: narrator
text: The vending machine was at the end of the corridor. Three drinks. Brown liquid. Different brown liquid. Yellowish brown liquid. Berk always chose the first. Called coffee. It wasn't coffee. But when he drank it Berk could pause for a moment. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: The Kariyope was entering Mars orbit. Final deceleration. Thirty-nine hours of it. There was nothing to do. Nothing that could be done was more accurate. Berk took a cup from the vending machine. He drank it. He could drink it. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Twelve surveillance monitors. Berk could see all twelve at once. Old habit. Sector 1 sector 2 sector 3. The cargo hold. Engine room. Corridor. Dining cabin. Passenger cabin. Passenger cabin corner. Someone was there.

speaker: narrator
text: A small bag on the lap. A hand resting on top. The hand didn't move. Two days now. For two days Berk hadn't seen that hand move. Whether they were sleeping was unclear. The monitor resolution wasn't good.

speaker: narrator
text: Two days, Berk said to himself. No sleep. Standing at the vending machine. How far is Mars. Thirty-nine hours. That's survivable without sleep. Probably. He looked at the monitor again.

speaker: narrator
text: The name was on the manifest. Berk didn't look at it. People going to Mars often left their names behind. Sometimes they brought new ones. Either way it was the same to Berk.

speaker: narrator
text: One of the crew asked Berk. Is that person alright. Berk thought for a moment. Said yes. He didn't know precisely what alright meant but he said it anyway. People going to Mars were usually not alright. That's why they were going to Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: Dining cabin. Evening ration. Three of four rows full. Two mining families. Men who looked like engineers. A woman sitting alone. No expression. She ate. She didn't think about what the food tasted like. That too was a way of going to Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: A mining family's child dropped their tray. A sound. Everyone looked. The child didn't cry. The adult looked at the child. The child looked at the adult. No words. Mining children learned early. They learned before knowing what they were learning.

speaker: narrator
text: One person hadn't appeared at the dining cabin. A crewmember brought a ration tray. It wasn't accepted. The next day another tray. Also refused. On the third day no one brought one.

speaker: narrator
text: It was a seat without a window. The chosen seat. There was no desire to know Mars was out there. Not yet. When you get to Mars you'll see Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: The bag was heavy. It had always been heavy. Heavy since leaving Earth. Heavy even knowing what was inside. The weight wasn't about the contents.

speaker: narrator
text: There wasn't much in the bag. Even the owner didn't know everything that was in it. One old thing. What it was, there was no need to open the bag to know. The bag wasn't opened.

speaker: narrator
text: What would be on Mars. That question had ended long ago. There was no asking it now. On Mars there would be Mars. That was all. Whether that was enough could only be known by going there.

speaker: narrator
text: Whether there was somewhere to go or not, that was unknown too. There were people on Mars. That was known. Which direction to walk hadn't been decided. Decisions came after feet touched soil.

speaker: narrator
text: The Kariyope shuddered. Vibration from the deceleration. The cabin lights flickered. The hand still didn't move. Berk watched that hand for a long time. Then he looked away from the monitor and drank his coffee.

speaker: narrator
text: A small child from the mining family stirred awake. Slipped free from an adult's arm and wandered the cabin once. The adult didn't wake. The child returned. A hand in sleep closed around the child. The child slept again. The walls were thick. People were alone inside them.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone snored. Someone moaned. Someone whispered. Sleeping on a ship was different from sleeping on Earth. On the ship the ship kept moving. It didn't stop. That wasn't a bad thing. They were going to Mars. Whether going to Mars was a good thing was also unclear.

speaker: narrator
text: Berk went up to the observation deck. Four in the morning. No one on the deck. Stars through the glass. The stars didn't move. The ship was moving. Berk had felt this difference for twenty-three years. The difference was getting smaller.

speaker: narrator
text: The person was there too. Corner of the observation deck. The bag was on the floor. A hand rested on the strap. Not looking out the window. Eyes half-closed. It wasn't clear if they were sleeping. Berk didn't go in.

speaker: narrator
text: Berk went back to the corridor. One cup of brown liquid. He looked up at the ceiling. The ceiling was dark. Twenty-three years. Now Mars was twenty-two degrees off the right viewport. It was starting to look large.

speaker: narrator
text: An announcement. Six in the morning. Berk's voice. Approaching Mars. Beginning contact with Hellas control. Eighteen hours to arrival. Passengers please return to your seats and fasten your seatbelts.

speaker: narrator
text: People moved. Footsteps in the corridor. A child asked something. Is Mars visible. The adult answered. You'll see it soon. The child ran. Toward the window. The child's palms pressed against the glass.

speaker: narrator
text: No getting up from the seat. No going to the window. No desire to see Mars. Not yet. But knowing Mars was there. It was felt. The ship had changed. The sounds changed. The vibration changed. Mars was close.

speaker: narrator
text: Mars on the screen was a little larger. Blood-red. Like a sunset. But it wasn't a sunset. Mars was always like this. That was what Mars was. Someone said it was beautiful. There was no thought about beauty.

speaker: narrator
text: Berk exchanged communications with ground control. Kariyope. Hellas control. Requesting cargo clearance code. Hellas control responded. Code received. Protocol. Protocol that hadn't changed in twenty-three years.

speaker: narrator
text: Ten hours. Those words remained. Ten hours. Whether it was long or short was unclear. It had taken six months to come from Earth to Mars. And ten hours felt far.

speaker: narrator
text: The ship tilted. Entry angle adjustment. Where the Martian atmosphere began. Red light came through the windows. The Martian atmosphere wrapped around the ship. Deceleration. Heat. Sound. That was how Mars received the ship.

speaker: narrator
text: The vibration intensified. The child cried. The adult held them. The engineers looked at each other. They all had experience. Still the vibration was heavy. The Kariyope was always like this. Berk knew. On the deceleration this ship made noise.

speaker: narrator
text: A hand rested on the bag. The hand didn't move. The ship shuddered. The shuddering wasn't unfelt. It wasn't that it wasn't felt. It was felt but not reacted to. The arrival was coming soon.

speaker: narrator
text: A red horizon appeared. The Hellas Basin. The lowest point on Mars. The deepest basin. People lived there. The child's palms pressed to the window turned red. It was Mars's light.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central was visible below. Its size was hard to judge. It looked small. It grew larger as they got closer. Upon arrival it would be enormous. All buildings on Mars were like that. Small from outside, enormous inside. It should have been the other way around but wasn't.

speaker: narrator
text: Berk made an announcement. Prepare for landing. Seatbelts. All electronics off. Luggage under seats. Protocol. Twenty-three years of the same words. The voice hadn't changed. The content hadn't changed. Mars hadn't changed.

speaker: narrator
text: The landing runway was visible. Long concrete. Blood-red dust running across it. There was wind. Hellas always had wind. Small winds. Before a major storm the small winds always came first.

speaker: narrator
text: The Kariyope landed. Sand struck the windows. That was Mars's business. Impact. The ship stopped. The sound stopped. Quiet. The quiet of Mars. Different from the quiet of space. The quiet of Mars had something in it.

speaker: narrator
text: No one moved. Just a moment. The moment after landing. Everyone seemed to be confirming they were on Mars. When confirmed they would move. The child moved first. Children confirm quickly.

speaker: narrator
text: The airlock opened. Air came in. Recycled air. Purified Martian atmosphere. Low oxygen content. It would be dizzying at first. That too was protocol. Three days to adapt.

speaker: narrator
text: The mining family disembarked first. A child holding an adult's hand. The engineers came down. The woman alone. No expression. No expression for the entire voyage. No expression on Mars. Whether that was the right way was unknown.

speaker: narrator
text: Everyone disembarked. Last one remaining. The bag was lifted. Heavy. Walking down the aisle. Through the airlock. There were stairs. At the bottom of the stairs was Mars.

speaker: narrator
text: The soil of Mars was there beneath the first step. Under a blood-red sky. Hellas Central stood ahead. Enormous. Enormous even from outside. Inside it would be more enormous. Wind came. The bag was gripped tighter.

speaker: narrator
text: Berk was watching from the gangway above. Looking down at the people disembarking. Saw them all. He'd been seeing this for twenty-three years. The last person off stood with the bag and stopped. Looking at Hellas Central. Berk saw that too.

speaker: narrator
text: Where to go was unknown. There was no answer to that question. No answer was given. Berk was expected to ask again. He didn't. That was Berk's way. On Mars not answering was an answer.

speaker: narrator
text: Hellas Central. Standing before it. Inside the building something was running. Things that didn't stop. To the right was MCC. To the left was the labor district. Straight ahead the main hall. Behind was the Kariyope. The Kariyope would leave in six hours.

speaker: narrator
text: Six hours. A return was possible. Some people came to Mars and turned back. Berk knew about them. People like that existed. They too set foot on Mars. That was enough for them. Those for whom it wasn't enough stayed.

speaker: narrator
text: The bag wasn't set down. Setting it down made it a decision. Holding it still meant not yet. People walked past. Miners. Engineers. Everyone going somewhere. They all had somewhere to go.
